title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: I'm Marcus Ellingham (employee ID EMP-40821) and I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-MELLINGHAM) at the Frankfurt office while preparing for remote work. After approving the Okta MFA push notification on my phone, the VPN session authenticated briefly — I could see the 'Connected' status for about two seconds — and then disconnected almost immediately, preventing access to internal web applications including our Sales CRM portal. My machine IP was 10.47.83.112 at the time. Investigation focused on whether the drop occurred after MFA success and whether device certificate validation was failing during tunnel establishment.
root_cause: Device certificate on the endpoint had expired, causing the GlobalProtect TLS handshake to fail immediately after successful Okta MFA approval and forcing the VPN tunnel to disconnect.
resolution_steps: Confirmed Okta MFA was succeeding for mellingham and isolated the failure to post-authentication tunnel establishment in GlobalProtect on LAPTOP-MELLINGHAM rather than an MFA rejection; Okta logs showed clean approval at 09:01:23 UTC.

Renewed the expired device certificate (serial 4A:7C:91:EE, expired 2026-03-15) through the Device Certificate Service for the affected endpoint LAPTOP-MELLINGHAM, generating a new certificate valid until 2027-04-18. Performed by desktop support engineer Priya Dasgupta (pdasgupta).

Refreshed the GlobalProtect VPN profile on LAPTOP-MELLINGHAM for user mellingham and removed stale profile data from C:\ProgramData\Palo Alto Networks\GlobalProtect so the renewed certificate was presented during connection to the EMEA gateway.

Retested the VPN connection from LAPTOP-MELLINGHAM (IP 10.47.83.112) and verified the tunnel remained established without the previous TLS handshake failure; gateway session showed stable for over 10 minutes.

Confirmed internal applications including the Sales CRM portal and SharePoint were reachable over the VPN and advised Marcus Ellingham to reboot the device to fully apply the renewed certificate and profile state. Provided direct contact nwilliams@corplabs.com for any recurrence.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether the GlobalProtect prompt drops before or after you approve the Okta MFA request on your device LAPTOP-MELLINGHAM, and whether internal apps such as the Sales CRM portal are unreachable as soon as the VPN disconnects. Also, can you confirm you're connecting from your usual Frankfurt location? You can reach me at nwilliams@corplabs.com if the portal is inaccessible.

title: Unable to connect to Corporate Wi-Fi — EAP-TLS authentication failures
description: Multiple users in the New York office were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi (CorpWiFi) from managed laptops, but authentication failed or devices repeatedly disconnected after association. The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40291) from the Sales team, who noticed her laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG could not connect after returning from a meeting. Several endpoints displayed "EAP-TLS: certificate expired" during 802.1X login against RADIUS server 10.40.12.5. The issue started immediately after the scheduled certificate rotation maintenance window on 2026-05-04 and blocked normal corporate wireless access across affected SSIDs for the NY Office / Sales user group.
root_cause: The RADIUS/Wireless Controller server certificate used for 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication expired during the certificate rotation window, causing clients to reject the authentication server and fail wireless login.
resolution_steps: Validated that the active RADIUS/Wireless Controller certificate (CN=radius.corplabs.internal, serial 4A:7C:0E:91) presented during EAP-TLS authentication was expired as of 2026-05-04T23:59:59Z and confirmed it matched the controller (WLC-NY-01) and RADIUS (10.40.12.5) failure logs reviewed by Nathan Williams (nwilliams).

Renewed and reissued the wireless authentication certificate with the correct validity period (2026-05-05 through 2028-05-05) and full certificate chain from the internal CA, then deployed it to the RADIUS service on 10.40.12.5 and Wireless Controller WLC-NY-01.

Restarted the RADIUS and controller authentication services on 10.40.12.5 and WLC-NY-01 so the new certificate was actively presented during 802.1X handshakes. Service restart completed at 2026-05-05T02:15:00Z.

Verified successful EAP-TLS authentication in controller and RADIUS traces after deployment — confirmed affected clients including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG (mgonzalez) and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DP (dpham) could authenticate to CorpWiFi normally and received correct VLAN/NAC policy assignments.

Instructed users with cached trust or profile issues (including three legacy macOS 12 devices on the Sales floor) to forget and rejoin the SSID or re-enroll through MDM, and kept temporary NAC relaxation only for previously trusted legacy endpoints until re-enrollment was completed. Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez) and Derek Pham (dpham) confirmed connectivity restored. Follow-up email sent to nwilliams@corplabs.com to schedule a post-incident review.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether affected users (yourself, Derek Pham, and others on the Sales floor) all see the same "EAP-TLS: certificate expired" error on CorpWiFi, and whether the failures began right after the wireless certificate maintenance window on Sunday evening. Also, can you check if the issue reproduces on both your device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG and Derek's machine WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DP? You can reach me at nwilliams@corplabs.com or ext. 212-555-0147 if you need to call in.

title: Software Center install blocked by Endpoint Protection - ContosoApp
description: I was trying to install ContosoApp from Software Center on my Windows 10 21H2 managed device (hostname WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES), but the app was shown as blocked and returned an Endpoint Protection policy denial (Error 0x800704EC) instead of allowing installation. My username is mreeves (employee ID EMP-40821) and I'm based out of the Portland office. Software Center did not present a usable install option, and the blocked install prevented me from completing the requested software deployment for a project deadline this week. My device IP is 10.42.17.88.
root_cause: Defender Application Control policy was blocking the approved ContosoApp installer on the device, and stale Intune inventory delayed policy visibility and refresh in Software Center.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Endpoint Protection/Application Control block condition for the ContosoApp installer on WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES (user mreeves) and confirmed it was being denied by Defender Application Control policy with error 0x800704EC under the Portland device scope.

Updated the Defender Application Control allow policy for the applicable Portland device scope so the approved ContosoApp installer hash was permitted. Change approved and applied by endpoint security analyst Nadia Okonkwo.

Triggered an Intune device inventory refresh for WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES (IP 10.42.17.88) to update the device state and policy reporting, bringing the sync current from the previous stale date of 2026-03-06.
Forced a Software Center policy/application sync on WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES so the revised Defender Application Control allow policy and app targeting were reevaluated for user mreeves.

Retested the deployment from Software Center on WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES and verified that ContosoApp installed successfully without the Endpoint Protection block message. Confirmed with Marcus Reeves via email at mreeves@corplabs.com that the application is functioning as expected.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm what Software Center shows for ContosoApp on your device WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES and whether you receive any specific block or policy error (such as 0x800704EC) when you try to install it. Also, can you confirm you're logged in as mreeves@corplabs.com?

title: Disk encryption not enabled on corporate laptop
description: Corporate laptop LAP-1234 (hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MK) assigned to Marco Kessler (emp ID EMP-40821) was re-imaged last week at the Frankfurt office and re-enrolled through Company Portal, but BitLocker did not start afterward. Intune reports the device as noncompliant for disk encryption, manage-bde shows Protection Off, no BitLocker recovery key is escrowed in Intune, and TPM-related warnings are present in the local event logs. The device remains blocked from meeting corporate compliance requirements until encryption is enabled and the recovery key is successfully escrowed. Ticket raised by mkessler@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: TPM initialization warning in event log
Intune shows device noncompliant for encryption
root_cause: After the device was re-imaged and re-enrolled, the Intune disk encryption policy was not effectively applied to the device and BitLocker protection remained off; TPM initialization warnings were a contributing factor that required local protector initialization before encryption and recovery key escrow could proceed.
resolution_steps: Confirm the device LAPTOP-SALES-MK is in the correct Intune group (EMEA-Sales-Devices) and assign the active disk encryption policy 'EMEA-Encryption-Standard' to that group so the re-enrolled endpoint belonging to Marco Kessler (mkessler) receives BitLocker settings.

Force an Intune sync from LAPTOP-SALES-MK via Company Portal and verify the latest check-in completes without assignment errors for the encryption policy; confirmed sync succeeded at 2026-01-25 18:22 UTC.

Validate TPM readiness on the endpoint LAPTOP-SALES-MK using Get-Tpm and initialize a TPM-based BitLocker protector because local status showed Protection Off and TPM warnings were present; TPM ownership was taken successfully after clearing stale state.
Enable BitLocker on the system drive and confirm encryption starts successfully on C: after the protector is created; manage-bde -status confirmed Encryption In Progress on LAPTOP-SALES-MK.

Back up and rotate the BitLocker recovery key to Intune using BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector and verify the key becomes visible in escrow for LAPTOP-SALES-MK before closing the ticket; recovery key ID confirmed present in Intune Key Escrow blade.

Recheck Intune compliance status for LAPTOP-SALES-MK after policy application and key escrow to confirm the device is no longer marked noncompliant for encryption; compliance evaluation passed and Marco Kessler (EMP-40821) regained full access to corporate resources from the Frankfurt office.
agent_questions: Hi Marco — please confirm whether the laptop LAPTOP-SALES-MK was recently re-imaged or had its TPM cleared, and share the latest Intune sync time so we can determine whether the encryption policy was reapplied after enrollment. Also, can you verify the device is connecting from your usual network? We see client IP 10.47.83.112 in the last check-in record.

title: Laptop slow after login
description: Finance analyst Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40218) on a managed Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) reported that immediately after each login the device became very slow, applications such as Outlook and Office took a long time to open, and CPU stayed abnormally high. The user, based in the Philadelphia office, contacted the service desk at extension 215-555-0147 explaining that the recurring slowdown on the corporate laptop (IP 10.22.74.113) was preventing normal post-login work. The issue was traced to endpoint protection activity during startup.
root_cause: Microsoft Defender endpoint protection scan backlog after login, compounded by low available disk space below 10%, which caused sustained MsMpEng.exe CPU usage and delayed application launches.
resolution_steps: Cleared the queued Microsoft Defender scan backlog (approximately 200 pending items) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN for user rnguyen so pending post-login scan activity no longer saturated CPU.

Updated endpoint protection scan scheduling through Endpoint Management to run during off-peak hours (daily at 02:00) instead of user login periods, applied to the Philadelphia Finance device group including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN.

Removed temporary files (18 GB+ under C:\Users\rnguyen\AppData\Local\Temp), Windows Update cache, and stale Defender artifacts to raise free disk capacity from 9.2 GB to approximately 30 GB, well above the minimum healthy threshold.
Disabled unnecessary startup items (including redundant OneDrive sync triggers and legacy inventory agents) to reduce competing resource usage during user sign-in on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN.

Refreshed device policy via Endpoint Management so the updated scan schedule and startup configuration were applied to WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN; confirmed with Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen) that post-login CPU returned to normal levels within 60 seconds on next login.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm whether the slowdown happens right after every login on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and whether Task Manager shows a specific process using most of the CPU. Also, could you let us know roughly how long the high-CPU period lasts before the machine becomes usable? — Kevin Marsh, Desktop Support

title: Outlook mobile stopped syncing mail — shows 'Disconnected' and Inbox stale
description: I (Danielle Martin, EMP-40291) was trying to access current email from Outlook Mobile on my managed iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-DM) at the Austin office, but the app began showing a disconnected state this morning and the Inbox had not updated since the previous day. My Exchange Online mailbox (d.martin@corplabs.com) remained accessible via OWA, indicating the issue was isolated to the mobile sync path. The stale mobile mailbox prevented me from receiving new messages on the device during normal Sales work, impacting my ability to respond to client communications promptly.
root_cause: A stale Outlook Mobile/ActiveSync device partnership and mismatched local Outlook profile state on the user's iPhone prevented the Exchange Online mailbox from maintaining a healthy mobile sync session. A minor MDM compliance state issue also needed to be refreshed before sync fully recovered.
resolution_steps: Validated that Danielle Martin's Exchange Online mailbox (d.martin@corplabs.com) was reachable via OWA and that the issue was limited to Outlook Mobile sync on WORKSTATION-IPHONE-DM rather than a mailbox outage.
Removed the stale mobile device partnership for Danielle Martin's primary iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-DM) in Exchange Online admin to clear the broken sync relationship.
Had the user remove and re-add the Outlook Mobile account/profile (d.martin@corplabs.com) on the iPhone to rebuild the local mailbox cache and connection state.
Verified the device compliance state for WORKSTATION-IPHONE-DM in Intune and refreshed the minor compliance condition so the device could resume normal mailbox access under MDM policy.

Performed a manual sync after profile re-creation and confirmed the Inbox updated with current messages and the disconnected status cleared; notified Danielle Martin (EMP-40291) that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Danielle Martin, please confirm whether Outlook on your iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-DM) shows 'Disconnected' continuously and whether the Inbox has stopped updating since yesterday, while web mail at https://outlook.office365.com is still reachable for your account d.martin@corplabs.com.

title: BitLocker encryption not enabled and recovery key not escrowed on Intune-managed device
description: My Intune-managed Windows 10 device WORK-LAP-07 (assigned to user mgarcia, employee ID EMP-40291) showed BitLocker encryption as not enabled in Company Portal. No recovery key was visible in Intune for this device, and it became noncompliant for encryption after the most recent policy rollout on 2026-01-26. This blocked the device from meeting endpoint security compliance requirements for the Sales team at the Phoenix office and indicated the encryption configuration was not being applied correctly. I reached out to the service desk after noticing the noncompliance banner in Company Portal.
observed_errors: Recovery key not found in Intune
root_cause: The device did not have an effective assignment of the current BitLocker encryption policy because it was still associated with a stale/deprecated policy reference (Encryption policy v1.2). As a result, the active encryption configuration was not applied, recovery key escrow to Intune did not occur, and the device was marked noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the device's Intune encryption policy targeting for WORK-LAP-07 (user mgarcia, EMP-40291) and confirmed the current BitLocker profile (Encryption policy v2.0) was not effectively assigned to the Sales-Devices-West device group containing this endpoint.
Assigned the updated Encryption policy v2.0 to the correct device scope (Sales-Devices-West) to replace the stale v1.2 policy reference that was still mapped to WORK-LAP-07 in the Intune console.

Initiated a forced Intune MDM sync on WORK-LAP-07 (IP 10.42.17.88) from the Intune device actions blade so the corrected encryption configuration would be received immediately rather than waiting for the next scheduled 8-hour check-in cycle.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery protector on drive C: using `manage-bde -protectors -add C: -RecoveryPassword` and confirmed the new recovery key (ID prefix 7A3F2B) escrowed successfully into Intune under the device record for mgarcia.

Verified BitLocker protection was present and encryption of drive C: had started on WORK-LAP-07 via `manage-bde -status C:` (showing Conversion Status: Encryption in Progress, Protection Status: Protection On), then confirmed the encryption compliance issue was cleared in the Device Compliance Service and the device was progressing toward compliant status.

Flagged internal documentation for update so older references to Encryption policy v1.2 are removed to prevent repeat assignment gaps, and notified the endpoint security team lead (jthompson@corplabs.com) to audit other devices in the Sales-Devices-West group for similar stale policy mappings.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please provide the Intune device ID and last successful MDM sync time for WORK-LAP-07, and confirm whether BitLocker shows any protector locally via Control Panel > BitLocker Drive Encryption or by running `manage-bde -status C:` from an elevated prompt. Also, can you confirm the device IP address so we can cross-reference the MDM enrollment record? You can reach me at r.chen@corplabs.com if you need to share screenshots.

title: Outlook desktop and mobile failing to sync
description: I (Rachel Nguyen, Sales team) was trying to receive and view new email in Outlook desktop and Outlook mobile for my primary Exchange Online mailbox (rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com), but new messages stopped appearing starting this morning around 8:15 AM EST. Outlook desktop on my workstation WORKSTATION-RNGYN intermittently showed a Disconnected state and my iPhone (Outlook mobile) reported Last synced: never despite normal network connectivity on both Wi-Fi and cellular. This is preventing normal mailbox access from both desktop and mobile clients and I'm missing critical sales correspondence.
root_cause: A stale Outlook profile and corrupted local OST prevented stable desktop synchronization, while mailbox-level EWS throttling in Exchange Online slowed or blocked client re-sync attempts. Mobile background synchronization was also briefly impacted by device compliance state until the partnership was reset.
resolution_steps: Validated the mailbox sync issue by confirming Outlook desktop on WORKSTATION-RNGYN (user: rachel.nguyen, IP 10.22.47.88) showed intermittent Disconnected status and Exchange Online logs contained repeated EWS throttling activity (HTTP 429) for the affected mailbox rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com.

Rebuilt Rachel Nguyen's Outlook profile on WORKSTATION-RNGYN, removed the corrupted OST file from the local AppData path, and allowed Outlook to create a fresh OST to remove the stale local cache condition. Profile rebuild was performed by desktop support technician David Ortiz (dortiz).

Cleared the existing mobile device partnership for Rachel's iPhone in Exchange Online admin center, re-established the managed mobile mail connection via MDM, and forced an initial mailbox synchronization — confirmed by Marcus Webb (security team) that compliance state returned to compliant.

Applied a temporary mailbox throttling policy adjustment for rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com to allow the affected mailbox to complete client re-sync from both desktop and mobile, and monitored Exchange Online EWS behavior during the stabilization window.

Verified that new mail appeared normally on Outlook desktop (WORKSTATION-RNGYN) and Outlook mobile, confirmed stable mail flow and folder updates over a 2-hour observation period, and received confirmation from Rachel Nguyen (ext. 4127) that both clients were fully operational before closure.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether Outlook on your desktop (WORKSTATION-RNGYN) is currently showing Connected or Disconnected in the status bar, and whether Outlook mobile on your iPhone shows any sync timestamp or error message while on a stable network. Also, can you confirm your current IP address so we can rule out any network-level filtering? You can reach me at ext. 4127 or via Teams if the issue worsens.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: denied access to Finance shared drive (FIN_SHARE)
description: I'm Jennifer Smith (jsmith, EMP-40821) and I was trying to open the Finance shared drive (FIN_SHARE) from a mapped network drive (F:) on my Windows 10 workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JS after a recent AD group access change processed last Friday. The drive prompted for credentials and then returned Access Denied / Error 5, preventing access to the \\FS-EAST-02.corp.local\FIN_SHARE department folder and blocking normal Finance file work on the SMB file server. I'm based in the Philadelphia office and need this resolved to complete month-end reconciliation reports. My direct number is 215-443-8817 if you need to reach me.
observed_errors: FileServer log: DENY on SMB read
root_cause: The user's AD membership was updated, but access continued to fail because the workstation was still presenting stale mapped-drive or cached SMB credentials that did not reflect the new Finance share entitlement. AD group membership was correct, and the deny behavior was caused by credential/session mismatch rather than a missing share permission.
resolution_steps: Confirmed jsmith (Jennifer Smith, EMP-40821) was a member of the FINANCE_SHARE AD security group and that the group change (CR-20260302-114, processed by mrivera) had replicated successfully across all domain controllers including DC-EAST-03.corp.local.
Validated the Finance shared drive path (\\FS-EAST-02.corp.local\FIN_SHARE mapped as F:) being used on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JS and ruled out access through an outdated mapped path or stale shortcut.

Cleared cached Windows credentials from Credential Manager on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JS (stale entry for FS-EAST-02.corp.local dated 2026-02-18) and disconnected the existing mapped network drive session (net use F: /delete) for the Finance share.

Refreshed the user's Kerberos logon token (klist purge) and remapped FIN_SHARE (net use F: \\FS-EAST-02.corp.local\FIN_SHARE /user:CORP\jsmith) using the current corporate identity context with updated group membership.

Retested access to the Finance department folder (F:\Finance_Dept) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JS and confirmed the share opened without credential prompts or further DENY events. Notified Jennifer Smith at jsmith@corpfinance.com that access was restored.
agent_questions: Hi Jennifer — thanks for reporting this. Could you please confirm whether you are opening the current FIN_SHARE mapped drive (F: pointing to \\FS-EAST-02.corp.local\FIN_SHARE) or an older shortcut, and whether the credentials prompt appears before the Access Denied message? Also, can you verify you're logged in as CORP\jsmith on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JS and not using a secondary account? I can see your IP is currently 10.22.47.115 — just want to confirm that's the machine in question.

title: Account locked again after password reset
description: I reset their corporate password through the Password Reset Portal for user mgarcia (employee ID EMP-40821) and could successfully sign in from the desktop, but the account was locked again shortly afterward when using the company-issued mobile device (hostname IPHONE-MGARCIA-01). Failed sign-in attempts continued from the mobile platform at IP 10.42.17.88 against Active Directory and SSO-connected services, blocking normal mobile access after the password change. The user, Maria Garcia, is based in the Charlotte office and reported the issue via phone at 704-555-3192.

Failed authentication events logged for user from mobile device

Instructed the user to remove the corporate account from the mobile device (IPHONE-MGARCIA-01), clear saved credentials in mobile mail and collaboration apps, and re-add the account using the new password. Maria Garcia confirmed completion of these steps at 15:25 UTC.

Invalidated existing SSO sessions at https://sso.corplabs.com and revoked prior authentication tokens for mgarcia to stop stale sessions from retrying with old credentials across all SSO-connected services.

Confirmed successful sign-in from both WORKSTATION-MGARCIA and IPHONE-MGARCIA-01 after mobile reconfiguration and monitored for additional failed authentication attempts from IP 10.42.17.88 to verify lockouts had stopped. No further incidents observed through end of business day.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — desktop sign-in is working after the password reset, but lockout events are still occurring against your account mgarcia@corplabs.com. Please confirm whether your company mobile device (IPHONE-MGARCIA-01) is still configured with the old password in mail or collaboration apps such as Outlook and Teams. title: BitLocker encryption not enforced
description: I (Jane Martinez, emp ID EMP-40821) on Surface Laptop 4 device SL4-WS-0924 was trying to meet Windows disk encryption compliance, but the device showed BitLocker enabled locally while Microsoft Intune continued to report EncryptionNotEnabled and no recovery key was visible in Azure AD/Intune. A recent policy push and manual device sync had already been performed from IP 10.42.17.88, leaving the endpoint noncompliant and support unable to confirm recovery key escrow for jmartinez@corplabs.com. The device hostname is WORKSTATION-SL4-JM and the user is based out of the Portland office in the Sales group.
observed_errors: Recovery key not found in Device Compliance Service
Local event log: BitLocker reported as ENCRYPTION_COMPLETE
root_cause: BitLocker was started locally before management state fully reconciled, leaving TPM protector and recovery key escrow in an inconsistent state so Intune compliance continued to report encryption not enabled.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM readiness via tpm.msc on WORKSTATION-SL4-JM and re-initialized the BitLocker TPM protector on the endpoint using manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm so the OS drive had a valid protector bound to the device hardware for user jmartinez (EMP-40821).

Confirmed OS volume encryption status locally via manage-bde -status C: on WORKSTATION-SL4-JM and re-triggered BitLocker protection with manage-bde -on C: to ensure the managed encryption state was fully active rather than only locally reported, verifying the TPM protector was now listed.

Rotated and escrowed the current BitLocker recovery key to Azure AD/Intune using BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector for WORKSTATION-SL4-JM, then verified that a recovery key record was available to support under jmartinez@corplabs.com's device entry in the Intune portal.

Re-applied the assigned BitLocker and compliance policies in Intune for device SL4-WS-0924 (WORKSTATION-SL4-JM) and forced a device sync from the Intune portal so the endpoint could submit updated encryption and escrow state for jmartinez's account.

Monitored the device record for WORKSTATION-SL4-JM until Intune compliance reconciled with the local BitLocker state and the device no longer showed the EncryptionNotEnabled condition. Confirmed with Jane Martinez at the Portland office that the endpoint now reports compliant and the recovery key is visible in Azure AD. Ticket closed per Enterprise SLA.
agent_questions: Hi Jane, this is Kevin Osei from Desktop Support. Please confirm whether BitLocker shows the OS drive (C:) as fully encrypted locally on WORKSTATION-SL4-JM and whether the device has completed a recent Intune sync after the policy push. Also, can you verify you're logged in as jmartinez and that the TPM Management console (tpm.msc) shows the TPM as ready for use? We need to rule out a protector initialization gap before proceeding.

title: Laptop slow after login
description: User Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) reported that his Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) became consistently slow within 1-2 minutes after sign-in for the past two days. Task Manager showed Antimalware Service Executable (MsMpEng) using 60-80% CPU immediately after login, and common applications such as Office took 30-60 seconds to open and become usable. The machine is assigned to the Philadelphia office, IP 10.42.17.88. The issue recurred after an earlier partial cleanup performed on 2026-02-05, affecting normal post-login productivity on the endpoint. Marcus reached out via mdelgado@corplabs.com after the problem persisted through a reboot cycle.
observed_errors: MsMpEng (Antimalware Service Executable) CPU spike to 60-80%
root_cause: Endpoint protection scan backlog caused sustained MsMpEng CPU usage immediately after login. The impact was amplified by a resource-heavy startup profile and low available disk space on C:, which contributed to repeated scan pressure and poor application responsiveness.
resolution_steps: Cleared the pending endpoint protection scan backlog on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD (5 queued quick scans) and allowed the antimalware workload to complete a fresh full scan outside the immediate login window during off-hours.

Refreshed endpoint management and protection policy on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD via the Endpoint Management console so the device received the current scan schedule, updated definitions (from 2026-02-03 to 2026-02-07), and corrected policy settings for user mdelgado.
Disabled 8 of 14 nonessential startup items on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD (including third-party updaters and unused collaboration tools) to reduce concurrent CPU load during user sign-in for mdelgado.

title: Internal host svc-payments.internal returns NXDOMAIN for multiple clients
description: Multiple internal users and application hosts were trying to reach the payments service by the hostname svc-payments.internal, but DNS lookups returned NXDOMAIN across several subnets (10.20.0.0/16 and 10.30.0.0/16) while direct access by IP 10.50.12.40 still worked. The issue was first reported by developer Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from her workstation WORKSTATION-MC-DEV in the Arlington office, and subsequently confirmed by app server operators in the same datacenter. The affected clients were all pointed at the primary internal DNS resolver at 10.10.1.5 (dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal). The issue blocked normal name-based connectivity to the svc-payments service in the corporate datacenter, impacting CI/CD pipelines and live payment processing integrations.
observed_errors: Negative cache hit on DNS Resolver
root_cause: The primary internal DNS resolver was serving a stale negative cache entry for svc-payments.internal, causing NXDOMAIN responses even though the A record existed correctly in the Internal DNS Zone.
resolution_steps: Verified that the A record for svc-payments.internal was present and correct in the Internal DNS Zone, including confirming the expected target IP 10.50.12.40 with TTL 300s and zone serial 2026011201 on the authoritative server.

Identified that the primary DNS resolver dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal (10.10.1.5) held a stale negative cache entry for svc-payments.internal that did not match the current zone data — the NXDOMAIN had been cached since approximately 21:28 UTC due to a transient zone transfer hiccup.
Flushed the affected DNS resolver cache on dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal using `rndc flush` to remove the stale NXDOMAIN response for the hostname svc-payments.internal.

Restarted the DNS resolver service (named) on the affected resolver host dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal to ensure fresh zone lookup behavior and clear residual cached state. Performed by David Kowalski (NET-4821).

Validated successful name resolution for svc-payments.internal from multiple client subnets — confirmed correct A record response (10.50.12.40) from Maria Chen's workstation WORKSTATION-MC-DEV (10.20.5.88), Raj Patel's host (10.20.5.102), Lisa Novak's host (10.20.5.110), and application servers on 10.30.x.x. Service was again reachable by hostname.

Added monitoring for abnormal negative cache spikes on dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal via Network Monitoring alerting rules and recommended review of negative caching TTL behavior (currently defaulting to SOA minimum) to reduce recurrence. Notified team lead Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) of resolution and preventive measures.

title: Software Center installation blocked by Endpoint Protection
description: Several users on Windows 10 Enterprise devices in the Engineering group at the Raleigh office were trying to install AcmeApp v4.2 from Software Center, but the install was blocked with a policy deny message and the app was not consistently visible in the Software Center catalog. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com, EMP-40821) and confirmed by at least three other engineers. The blocked task prevented affected users from completing the AcmeApp installation needed on managed endpoints. Endpoint Protection logging on device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.28.44.107) indicated the installer was denied by application approval policy even though device inventory in Intune was current.
observed_errors: Application not listed in Software Center catalog for affected users
root_cause: Endpoint Protection blocked the AcmeApp installer because the application was missing from the Approved Applications policy assigned to affected devices, which prevented the Software Center deployment from being presented and installed successfully.
resolution_steps: Confirmed in Endpoint Protection telemetry that the AcmeApp installer (AcmeAppSetup_v4.2.exe) was being denied as Not Approved under the Approved Applications policy (EP-APCTRL-0087) on endpoints WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC, WORKSTATION-DESK-DO, and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN, rather than failing due to package corruption or device inventory issues.

Reviewed the assigned application approval policy EP-APCTRL-0087 and identified that AcmeApp was missing from the Approved Applications allow list for the affected Engineering user and device scope. Security lead Raj Gupta (rgupta) confirmed the omission was an oversight during the v4.2 release packaging.

Added AcmeApp v4.2 installer hash to the Endpoint Protection Approved Applications policy EP-APCTRL-0087 and saved the updated configuration for the impacted Engineering deployment group. Change approved by rgupta.

Pushed the revised policy to affected endpoints through Intune and forced a policy refresh on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC, WORKSTATION-DESK-DO, and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN so the updated approval state would be received by managed devices.

Refreshed Software Center application visibility and retried the AcmeApp v4.2 installation on affected endpoints. Maria Chen (mchen) confirmed the installer was no longer blocked by policy on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC, and David Okonkwo (dokonkwo) confirmed the same on WORKSTATION-DESK-DO.

Validated that AcmeApp v4.2 installed successfully after the approval update on all three reported devices and that the application became available as expected in Software Center for all impacted Engineering users in the Raleigh office.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Remote users on managed Windows 10 laptops were trying to connect to the corporate network through GlobalProtect VPN from multiple offices. After approving the Okta MFA prompt, the VPN tunnel established briefly and then disconnected within seconds, leaving internal applications such as the intranet, internal Salesforce, and Confluence unreachable. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40821) at the Denver office around 08:15 local time, and subsequently confirmed by additional users in the Austin and Toronto regions. The problem blocked normal remote access to internal resources for the remote_workers group throughout the morning.
observed_errors: IKE negotiation aborted after auth success
root_cause: Expired device certificates on affected endpoints caused GlobalProtect certificate validation to fail immediately after successful Okta MFA, which terminated the VPN tunnel during post-authentication connection setup.
resolution_steps: Validated that affected endpoints including LAPTOP-MC-4082 (maria.chen) and LAPTOP-RP-2197 (raj.patel) had expired device certificates in the local certificate store (expiry date 2026-04-09) and confirmed the failures aligned with the VPN disconnect timing observed in GlobalProtect gateway logs.

Renewed device certificates for affected devices through the Device Certificate Service and re-enrolled endpoints where automatic renewal had not completed successfully. Desktop support analyst Priya Nair (priya.nair@corplabs.com) coordinated re-enrollment for 14 affected machines across Denver, Austin, and Toronto offices.

Pushed an updated GlobalProtect VPN profile to enrolled endpoints via the management console to ensure the current certificate and profile association were used for tunnel establishment. Profile version 4.2.7-r3 was deployed to all affected devices.

Cleared stale VPN profile data on impacted test devices (LAPTOP-MC-4082, LAPTOP-RP-2197), reconnected GlobalProtect, and verified the tunnel remained established after Okta MFA approval for both maria.chen and raj.patel.

Confirmed restored access to internal applications (Intranet, Salesforce, Confluence) after reconnection for all reported users and added device certificate expiry monitoring and alerting in the Device Certificate Service dashboard to reduce the risk of recurrence. Kevin Oduya set threshold alerts at 14 and 7 days before expiry.

title: Users stuck in continuous MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple users in the marketing and sales departments — initially reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and Derek Holloway (EMP-30457) — were unable to sign in to SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Google Workspace, and Confluence through the SSO Portal using Okta federated to Azure AD. After completing or approving MFA in Okta (push notification via Okta Verify), they were immediately returned to another MFA prompt or saw the sign-in rejected with a conditional access deny, preventing access to business applications. The issue affected a cohort of approximately 14 users in the Charlotte office rather than a single account and appeared during normal SSO access beginning around 08:15 UTC. Okta system logs showed successful MFA verification activity while Azure AD conditional access denied the same sign-in attempts, suggesting a policy evaluation mismatch between the two identity layers.
observed_errors: MFA prompt loop observed in browser
Authentication rejected (Azure AD conditional access deny)
Okta audit: MFA enrollment reset succeeded
root_cause: Azure AD Conditional Access policy scope was misaligned with current Okta-sourced group assignments. Users whose MFA enrollment state had recently changed in Okta were authenticating successfully at the Okta layer, but Azure AD evaluated them against incorrect group-based policy membership and denied token issuance, resulting in repeated MFA prompts and blocked application access.
resolution_steps: Reviewed affected user group membership in Okta and Azure AD — specifically the Okta groups 'Okta-Marketing' and 'Okta-Sales' versus the Azure AD group 'SG-SaaS-Marketing-Sales' — and identified that the Azure AD Conditional Access policy 'CA-SaaS-MFA-Required' scope did not match the intended Okta group mapping for the 14 impacted marketing and sales users in the Charlotte office, including rnguyen, dholloway, and mparker.

Updated the Azure AD Conditional Access group-based assignment for policy 'CA-SaaS-MFA-Required' to align with the corrected synced group membership from Okta, ensuring all 14 affected users in 'Okta-Marketing' and 'Okta-Sales' were properly reflected in 'SG-SaaS-Marketing-Sales' so the affected cohort was evaluated against the proper MFA and access policy. Change performed by identity engineer Priya Deshmukh (pdeshmukh).

Performed targeted Okta MFA re-enrollment only for impacted users with stale or recently reset factor state — specifically dholloway, mparker, and two additional users (jcaldwell, tsanchez) — to remove residual enrollment inconsistencies after the policy correction. Re-enrollment was confirmed via Okta admin console.

Validated end-to-end SSO for representative test accounts rnguyen (from WORKSTATION-RN-PC, IP 10.42.16.88) and dholloway (from WORKSTATION-DH-PC, IP 74.112.56.33) by confirming a single MFA challenge completed successfully and access was restored to downstream SaaS applications including Salesforce, Google Workspace, and Confluence.

Monitored Okta audit events and Azure AD sign-in logs for 4 hours after the change window (09:10–13:10 UTC) to confirm that prior conditional access denials stopped for the corrected user cohort. All 14 Charlotte office users showed successful sign-ins with no further MFA loop behavior reported. Ticket closed by Priya Deshmukh and confirmation sent to Rachel Nguyen (rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com).
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — thanks for reporting this. Can you confirm whether affected users loop back to MFA after approving the Okta Verify push prompt, and whether the problem occurs across multiple SaaS apps (Salesforce, Google Workspace, Confluence) or only one application? Also, are the impacted users all signing in from the Charlotte office, or are remote users affected as well? If you can share a couple of affected usernames (e.g., rnguyen, dholloway) that would help us trace the sign-in flow in the logs.

title: Multiple users unable to authenticate to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple employees across the Charlotte office were trying to connect managed Windows, macOS, and iOS devices to the Corporate Wi-Fi (SSID: CorpNet-Secure) starting around 06:30 ET on 2026-05-03, but received authentication failures or joined without usable network access. The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least six other users on the 3rd and 4th floors. Wireless controller WLC-EAST-01.corp.netinfra.local logs showed repeated 802.1X/EAP-TLS failures consistent with an expired RADIUS server certificate on the wireless authentication path. The certificate (CN=wlc-radius.corp.netinfra.local, issued by CorpNet-CA) had expired at midnight UTC on 2026-05-03.
observed_errors: device receives no network access after successful join
root_cause: The wireless controller EAP-TLS certificate expired, causing 802.1X authentication failures and preventing devices from successfully completing NAC-based corporate Wi-Fi access until the certificate and dependent device profiles were updated.
resolution_steps: Renew and install the wireless controller EAP-TLS certificate (CN=wlc-radius.corp.netinfra.local) with the correct trust chain from CorpNet-CA on WLC-EAST-01.corp.netinfra.local, the Corporate Wi-Fi authentication infrastructure. Kevin Marsh (kmarsh@corpinfra.net) performed the certificate renewal and installation.

Validate on the wireless controller WLC-EAST-01 and NAC appliance NAC-EAST-02 that 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentications complete successfully and that authenticated devices receive the expected access policy and full corporate network access. Priya Kapoor confirmed successful test authentications for users mgonzalez and dpham.

Push the updated wireless certificate and current Corporate Wi-Fi profile (CorpNet-Secure) to managed endpoints through Workspace ONE MDM so affected Windows, macOS, and iOS devices trust the renewed authentication path. Approximately 140 devices in the Charlotte office received the updated profile.

Have impacted users forget and re-add the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) if their device still presents the old profile or continues to fail authentication after the MDM update. Users mgonzalez, dpham, and rnakamura were walked through this step directly by the helpdesk.

Provide temporary access through the authenticated guest SSID (CorpNet-Guest-Auth) for business continuity until the profile and certificate rollout is fully applied to all affected devices. Guest credentials were distributed to impacted users including Maria Gonzalez and Derek Pham via their corporate email addresses mgonzalez@corplabs.com and dpham@corplabs.com.

description: I was trying to access corporate resources (SharePoint and Outlook) from my managed iOS 15.4 device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MR) at approximately 13:00 UTC on January 1st, but Conditional Access blocked sign-in for my account m.rossi@corplabs.com because the device was shown as Noncompliant in Intune. Reapplied the encryption-related compliance policy/profile to WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MR so the required compliance setting would be reprocessed by the MDM channel and the encryption signal would be re-evaluated.
Instructed Marco Rossi to restart the iOS device and sign back in to Company Portal with m.rossi@corplabs.com to re-establish the MDM reporting session and submit updated compliance data.

Verified that WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MR reported a current check-in (2026-01-01T13:42:00Z), updated encryption status to compliant, overall ComplianceState changed to Compliant, and m.rossi@corplabs.com was no longer blocked by Conditional Access. title: Print jobs stuck on PrintServer01
description: Users in the Chicago office were trying to print through shared queues hosted on PrintServer01 after a recent printer driver deployment pushed by the IT packaging team. Multiple printers appeared offline and submitted jobs remained stuck in a spooling state, preventing employees from completing normal printing across departments. The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (EMP-40291) from the Finance department and quickly confirmed by additional users. The issue affected the on-premises Windows Server 2019 print server and began after the driver update.
observed_errors: Printer offline - unable to load driver
root_cause: A corrupt printer driver package deployed to PrintServer01 created a hash mismatch and prevented the print subsystem from loading the driver correctly, causing printers to show offline and queued jobs to remain stuck in spooling.
resolution_steps: Removed the corrupt printer driver package from PrintServer01 using Print Management so the failed package was no longer referenced by affected queues. Removal performed by Brian Novak (EMP-50184) under change authorization from Kevin Marsh.
Installed the approved HP Universal Print Driver v3.2.1 from the vendor repository and confirmed the driver package loaded without mismatch errors. Installation validated by bnovak on PrintServer01.
Cleared all stuck print jobs from the affected queues (including 14 jobs from users in Chicago) and restarted the Print Spooler service to reset the print subsystem.

Remapped the impacted printer queues to the newly installed approved driver and verified the printers returned to an online state. Confirmed with Maria Gonzalez and Raj Patel that their workstations could see the printers as online.

Submitted test print jobs through the affected queues from WORKSTATION-PC-MG and WORKSTATION-PC-DL and monitored queue processing for two hours to confirm jobs completed successfully without recurring spool failures. Final confirmation received from dliu at 18:55.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether all affected printers are hosted on PrintServer01 and whether the issue started after the recent driver deployment or only affects a single queue. Also, can you share the hostname of the workstation you were printing from so we can cross-reference spooler logs? — Kevin Marsh, Workplace Services

title: Software Center installation blocked for SalesApp - entitlement missing

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Nightly DataSync integration jobs submitted by the application_support team (contact: r.martinez@corplabs.com) were attempting to send customer records through the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-07) to the downstream API service, but starting around 02:10 UTC on 2025-12-05 the gateway began receiving repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses from the API endpoint and requests exceeded the configured 30 second client timeout. This caused job failures across the DataSync worker pool running on host WORKSTATION-DSYNC-RM, queue growth in the integration worker (queue depth exceeded 4,200 pending messages), and delayed customer data synchronization for the Chicago processing region until retries or manual recovery actions completed. Incident was initially reported by Rafael Martinez (EMP-80241) via the on-call pager.
root_cause: Elevated latency on the downstream API service caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured 30 second timeout, resulting in repeated 504 responses, retry accumulation, and delayed sync processing.
resolution_steps: Correlated the nightly job failure window (02:10–03:45 UTC) with downstream API latency metrics from the Monitoring System and confirmed Integration Gateway requests on igw-prod-east-07 from client IP 10.42.17.93 were timing out at the 30 second threshold during sustained 504 responses — 347 failures logged for service account svc-datasync.

Escalated the incident to the downstream service SRE team (contact: Yuki Tanaka, ytanaka@corplabs.com) for capacity and latency investigation under ticket SRE-4521 and provided timing, error-rate, p95 latency charts, and queue backlog evidence from the Monitoring System covering the 02:10–03:45 UTC window.

Applied a temporary mitigation by increasing the Integration Gateway timeout on igw-prod-east-07 from 30 seconds to 45 seconds to reduce immediate job failures while the downstream latency issue was being investigated. Change applied by agent dkumar and confirmed across all 3 gateway replicas in us-east-1.

Updated the gateway retry policy to exponential backoff with jitter (base interval 2s, max interval 60s, jitter factor 0.5) to reduce retry amplification against the slow downstream API and improve recovery behavior. Configuration change documented by dkumar in the Integration Gateway runbook.

Restarted the integration gateway worker on WORKSTATION-DSYNC-RM to clear 4,200+ stalled requests and allow queued sync jobs to resume processing under the temporary timeout and retry settings. Worker restart performed by Rafael Martinez (EMP-80241) with confirmation from agent dkumar.

Expanded monitoring via the Monitoring System to track end-to-end API latency, 504 error rate, and worker queue depth with alerting thresholds (p95 latency > 10s, 504 rate > 5%, queue depth > 500) so future downstream degradation can be detected and escalated earlier. Alert recipients configured for r.martinez@corplabs.com and powens@corplabs.com.

title: Users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple employees — including Rajesh Menon (rmenon), Carla Diaz (cdiaz), and at least four others in the Denver office — were trying to sign in to SaaS applications such as Salesforce and Confluence through the SSO Portal using Okta with Azure AD conditional access policy evaluation. After successful primary authentication and completing MFA via Okta Verify, they were returned to the MFA challenge screen instead of reaching the target application. Okta audit activity for the affected accounts showed repeated MFA challenges and SAML assertion rejection behavior (SSO_LOGIN_REJECTED_401), preventing users from accessing business applications in the us-east-1 web environment. The issue was first reported by rmenon at approximately 20:45 UTC from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RM (10.42.17.88).
root_cause: Stale MFA enrollments for affected users combined with an Azure AD group membership synchronization delay caused conditional access policy evaluation to mismatch expected app assignment, resulting in repeated MFA re-challenges and rejected assertions after primary SSO authentication.
resolution_steps: Reset MFA enrollments for impacted users (rmenon, cdiaz, tbarker, jflores) in Okta to remove stale factor bindings and require clean re-registration of the active Okta Verify authenticator. Priya Nair (pnair) performed the resets and notified each user via email to complete re-enrollment.

Corrected the Azure AD group synchronization rule for the 'SaaS-AllEmployees-Access' group so user membership was evaluated correctly and without propagation delay for the conditional access and application assignment scope. The sync interval was reduced from 60 minutes to 15 minutes to prevent recurrence.

Revalidated affected users' (rmenon, cdiaz, tbarker, jflores) group membership and conditional access policy targeting after sync correction to confirm they matched the intended access path for Salesforce, Confluence, and the SSO Portal.

Checked authenticator device time on sampled user devices (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RM for rmenon, WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-CD for cdiaz) and instructed users to resync device time via automatic NTP where drift of ~90 seconds was identified on tbarker's mobile authenticator.

Tested fresh SSO sign-in flows for affected users rmenon, cdiaz, tbarker, and jflores from their respective workstations and confirmed they completed MFA once and reached the target applications (Salesforce, Confluence) without looping.

Monitored Okta authentication and SAML assertion logs for 24 hours after the fix and observed successful SSO plus MFA completion without repeat rejects (MFA_PROMPT_LOOP / SSO_LOGIN_REJECTED_401) for the impacted population across the Denver office. No recurrence detected as of 2026-04-04T21:00:00Z.
agent_questions: Hi Rajesh — thanks for the report. title: Internal Web Service TLS outage
description: Internal staff in the Arlington data center were trying to access the Internal Web Service over HTTPS for the internal-service-api and internal-dashboard endpoints (internal-service.company.local), but browsers showed certificate warnings and requests through the F5 load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.company.local) failed TLS negotiation. Users could not reach the service securely, and monitoring reported TLS handshake failures and 502 responses in us-east-1-dc1 after the service certificate passed its expiration on 2025-12-13 without the renewed chain being deployed. Initially reported by Maria Castillo (mcastillo@company.local) from the Finance team, who was unable to load the internal dashboard from her workstation WORKSTATION-MC-FIN.
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal-service.company.local issued by the Internal Certificate Authority expired and the renewed full certificate chain was not deployed to the F5 load balancer, causing TLS handshake rejection and HTTPS outage for the Internal Web Service.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the presented certificate for internal-service.company.local was expired (Not After: 2025-12-13T00:00:00Z) and identified that the active chain on the load balancer lb-prod-east-01.company.local was no longer valid for client trust. Verification performed by Derek Huang (dhuang) from the Arlington NOC.

Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate from the Internal Certificate Authority for the affected service endpoint (CN=internal-service.company.local, SAN: internal-service.company.local, internal-dashboard.company.local). CSR generated by dhuang, approved by Nicole Williams (nwilliams).

Installed the renewed certificate and complete certificate chain on the Internal Web Service endpoint (internal-svc-prod-01.company.local) and reloaded the service TLS configuration. Deployment verified by dhuang via openssl s_client handshake test.

Updated the F5 load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.company.local) to present the renewed certificate chain on VIP 10.50.1.20:443 and reloaded the affected HTTPS virtual service. Confirmed chain validity from client subnet 10.22.14.0/24 by Derek Huang.

Validated successful end-to-end TLS handshakes from client (WORKSTATION-MC-FIN at 10.22.14.87) and monitoring perspectives across regions, and restored certificate expiration alerting to PagerDuty (notifying infra-certs-team@company.local) to prevent recurrence. Maria Castillo and James Okafor confirmed service access restored. Closure approved by Nicole Williams (nwilliams).
agent_questions: Hi Maria — thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether users are seeing browser certificate warnings specifically for internal-service.company.local and whether failures occur only over HTTPS through the load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.company.local). Also, can you confirm if the issue is affecting users in Arlington only or other sites as well? I'm assigning this to our network infrastructure lead, Derek Huang (dhuang), for immediate investigation. You can also reach me at ext. 4127 or nwilliams@company.local if you have additional details.

Retested connectivity on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD for user mdelgado and confirmed stable Wi-Fi association to CorpNet-Secure (assigned IP 10.22.47.133), successful 802.1X authentication via ClearPass, and restored full network access without repeated disconnects over a 30-minute monitoring window. title: Internal hostname svc-db.internal fails DNS resolution
description: Internal application teams were trying to reach the database service by the internal hostname svc-db.internal, but several application pods intermittently failed name resolution and could not connect to the DB. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the platform engineering group in Phoenix. Failures were concentrated on queries served by dns-resolver-01.corp.internal, where monitoring showed repeated NXDOMAIN responses from client hosts including WORKSTATION-LINUX-MD (10.42.17.88). Review of the internal DNS zone found an outdated A record pointing to decommissioned IP 10.20.5.14 instead of the current 10.20.9.42, along with a deprecated zone management policy reference (internal-dns-policy-v1), creating impact for internal-order-service, payment-processor, and reporting-worker in corp-datacenter-1.
observed_errors: DNS lookup timeout (resolver query timed out)
root_cause: Intermittent NXDOMAIN responses were caused by a stale A record for svc-db.internal in the internal DNS zone and a deprecated internal DNS management policy reference that allowed outdated zone data to persist on dns-resolver-01 and dependent resolvers.
resolution_steps: Verified that svc-db.internal had an outdated A record (10.20.5.14, last modified 2025-06-12) in the internal DNS zone and confirmed the currently required target IP 10.20.9.42 with database infrastructure owner Priya Nair (pnair) before making changes.

Updated the A record for svc-db.internal in the internal DNS zone to the correct current IP 10.20.9.42 and reviewed the zone entry metadata and TTL (set to 300s from previous 86400s) under change record CHG-88214.

Replaced the deprecated internal-dns-policy-v1 reference with internal-dns-policy-v2 in the zone management configuration to prevent continued publication of stale record state and ensure automatic zone synchronization across all resolvers.

Flushed cache on dns-resolver-01.corp.internal using `rndc flush` and cleared/propagated cache refresh on dependent resolvers dns-resolver-02 and dns-resolver-03 so fresh zone data would be served immediately across the Phoenix datacenter.

Validated successful hostname resolution from affected application hosts (WORKSTATION-LINUX-MD at 10.42.17.88, app-node-03, app-node-07) and confirmed Network Monitoring no longer observed NXDOMAIN responses for svc-db.internal. Marcus Delgado confirmed internal-order-service, payment-processor, and reporting-worker health checks all passing.

title: Print jobs stuck

observed_errors: Spooler reported 'driver unavailable' for HP Universal driver
Spooler exception entries during driver load

Cleared all 14 stuck jobs from the office-printer-3f queue to remove items submitted against the failed v6.9.0 driver mapping; notified affected users (mdelgado, kmarsh, pnair, and others) to resubmit their print jobs after remediation.
Remapped the office-printer-3f shared printer queue to the newly installed approved HP Universal Print Driver v7.0.1 package and restarted the Print Spooler service on PRNSRV-EAST-01.

Submitted and monitored a test print job from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.42.18.77) to confirm the spooler loaded the v7.0.1 driver correctly, the office-printer-3f queue processed jobs normally, and the printer returned to online status for all impacted Columbus office users in Finance and HR.

Removed 8.3 GB of large temporary files from C:\Users\mpellegrini\AppData\Local\Temp and C:\Windows\Temp and reclaimed disk space (free space from 11% to 19%) to reduce background processing overhead, then monitored for 48 hours and verified CPU stabilized below 25% post-login and app launch times returned to normal (under 3 seconds for Outlook, Chrome, and Teams).

root_cause: Windows Defender endpoint protection full-scan backlog was triggering at user login, and very low free disk space amplified CPU and disk contention, causing post-login performance degradation.

Cleared the queued scan backlog on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR using Remove-MpThreat and reset the scan history, then allowed protection activity to resume under reduced immediate scan concurrency to lower startup resource contention.

Removed temporary files (14.3 GB from Windows Temp, 9.8 GB from SoftwareDistribution\Download) and ran Disk Cleanup on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR to increase available disk space from 7% (17.2 GB) to approximately 20% (48.5 GB), above the internal 15% target threshold.

Updated the endpoint protection policy in Intune for the Philadelphia engineering device group so full scans run during off-hours (2:00 AM local) instead of immediately at user login, preventing future scan backlog pile-ups from blocking post-login productivity.

Forced a device policy refresh on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via Intune sync so the revised Defender schedule and performance-related settings applied immediately without waiting for the next 8-hour check-in cycle.

Validated after login on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR that CPU and disk activity normalized (CPU under 15% within 2 minutes), applications opened in expected time (Outlook in ~20 seconds, Edge in ~5 seconds), and Marcus Reeves confirmed the user experience returned to normal.

description: Finance users in the Charlotte office were trying to print to the shared Finance printer (queue: FIN-HP-4050-Q1) through on-prem print server PRN-PS-01 on Windows Server 2019, but jobs remained stuck in the queue and the queue displayed "Driver unavailable" while the printer appeared offline. root_cause: Corrupted or checksum-mismatched printer driver package on PRN-PS-01 caused the Finance printer queue to lose its valid driver association, triggering spooler errors and repeated job failures.
resolution_steps: Obtain the approved Finance printer driver package (HP Universal Print Driver v6.9.0, approved build hash e81b04…) from the central driver repository and validate that the package checksum and signing status match the approved release before installation on PRN-PS-01. Anita Reeves (areeves) performed the download and verification.

Remove the corrupt driver package from \\PRN-PS-01\DriverStore\HP_UPD_v6.9.0 and reinstall the approved printer driver on PRN-PS-01 using Print Management Console so the queue FIN-HP-4050-Q1 is bound to a valid supported driver. Confirmed new package hash matches approved build.

Remap the Finance printer queue FIN-HP-4050-Q1 to the reinstalled HP Universal Print Driver v6.9.0 and confirm the printer object reports online without the "Driver unavailable" status. Verified queue status shows 'Ready' in Print Management Console.

Run test prints from mgonzalez (WORKSTATION-FIN-MG, 10.42.18.77), dpham (10.42.18.83), and rsimmons through the Finance queue FIN-HP-4050-Q1 and verify jobs pass through the spooler normally without new spooler crashes or repeat queue failures. title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage (INC-CES-0041)
description: Users and automated integrations were trying to reach the internal authentication service at auth.internal.example from the Dallas office, but browsers showed certificate expiration warnings and dependent integration tests failed TLS validation. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@internal.example) from the platform engineering team. The service could not be accessed normally over HTTPS because the presented certificate had passed its validity date (expired 2025-12-20T00:00:00Z) and the load balancer LB-CENTRAL-04.infra.internal was still serving an outdated certificate chain containing the old intermediate CA. Automated health checks from the CI/CD pipeline on host WORKSTATION-BUILD-MD also began failing with SSL errors around the same time.
observed_errors: curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
root_cause: The TLS leaf certificate for auth.internal.example expired on 2025-12-20. A suppressed renewal alert prevented timely renewal response, and the updated certificate chain was not deployed to the load balancer, causing client certificate validation failures and TLS handshake errors.
resolution_steps: Reissued a valid TLS certificate (serial 7B:22:E1:A5, valid 2025-12-20 through 2026-12-20) for auth.internal.example from the internal Certificate Authority (CA-ROOT-CENTRAL.infra.internal). Certificate reissuance was performed by Tomás Rivera (trivera).

Deployed the renewed leaf certificate and full certificate chain — including the current intermediate CA (CN=Internal Issuing CA G3) — to the load balancer LB-CENTRAL-04.infra.internal configuration serving the internal web service on vip 10.200.1.50:443.

Restarted the affected load balancer TLS listener on LB-CENTRAL-04.infra.internal and reloaded the service endpoints so the new certificate chain was actively presented to clients. Reload completed at 2025-12-20T12:05:00Z with no dropped connections.

Validated the endpoint from client and browser perspectives — tested from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN (pnair, 10.42.18.77) and WORKSTATION-BUILD-MD (svc-authtest) — to confirm the certificate dates, hostname match (SAN: auth.internal.example), and full trust chain were correct and TLS handshakes succeeded without errors.

Restored certificate monitoring by having Jayesh Kumar (jkumar) remove the suppression rule SUPP-2025-1110 from the cert-monitor pipeline and added a pre-expiry renewal/runbook check at 60-day and 30-day thresholds to prevent missed renewals. Alert recipients updated to include mdelgado@internal.example and the platform-eng-oncall@internal.example distribution list.

Restored and tested certificate expiry monitoring on cert-mgmt-01.infra.local so alerts trigger to ops-alerts@corplabs.com 30 days before the renewal window closes and renewal job failures are surfaced. Verified alert rule now covers CN=internal.service.local.

title: VPN disconnects
description: Multiple remote users in the Denver and Austin offices on corporate-managed Windows 10 and macOS 12 devices (Intune-enrolled) were trying to connect to the corporate network through GlobalProtect while working remotely. root_cause: Expired device certificates on affected managed endpoints caused GlobalProtect certificate validation to fail after successful Okta MFA, resulting in immediate VPN tunnel teardown.
resolution_steps: Verified the affected endpoints (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN for rnguyen and WORKSTATION-MBP-MD for mdelgado) were presenting expired device certificates during GlobalProtect authentication by correlating client disconnect timing with Device Certificate Service expiry records — rnguyen's cert expired 2026-04-10, mdelgado's expired 2026-04-09.

Issued renewed device certificates for the impacted corporate-managed Windows and macOS endpoints (including those belonging to Rachel Nguyen, EMP-40821, and Marcus Delgado, EMP-40955) through the Device Certificate Service, confirming new validity dates extending to 2027-04-12.

title: Integration Gateway API requests timing out
description: During the nightly customer sync window starting 2025-12-10 03:00 UTC, clients calling the Integration Gateway (gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) experienced intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout errors and failed integration jobs. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, noting that the Customer Sync Service and Billing App feeds were stalling. The issue affected customer data synchronization for dependent applications, with the Monitoring System dashboard showing elevated gateway response times (p95 > 4.2s) and downstream API latency on the Order Fulfillment API. Authentication failures (ERR_AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID) were also observed early in the event around 03:12 UTC, but token rotation on service account svc-custsync only reduced those errors temporarily and did not eliminate the timeout pattern. Downstream host api-orders.corpsync.internal was identified as the slow responder.
root_cause: Primary cause was elevated latency in the downstream API service during the nightly sync window, causing the Integration Gateway to exceed timeout thresholds and return intermittent 504 responses. An authentication issue from an aging or invalid token contributed noise early in the incident, but token rotation only addressed the auth failures and did not resolve the underlying downstream performance bottleneck.
resolution_steps: Validated and rotated the Integration Gateway API token for service account svc-custsync (previous token issued 2025-10-03, expired beyond 60-day validity), then verified client credentials against the gateway auth provider to remove the authentication failure condition (ERR_AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID) observed at the start of the incident. Performed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, E-40291) from the Arlington office.

Cleared the Integration Gateway cache on gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal and confirmed authentication errors dropped from ~38/min to near zero after the credential refresh. Verified via Monitoring System dashboard that no further ERR_AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID events were generated post-rotation.

Adjusted gateway retry and backoff settings (exponential backoff increased from 1s to 3s, max retries set to 5) on gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal to reduce customer sync job failures while downstream latency on api-orders.corpsync.internal remained elevated. Configuration change applied by Priya Nair (pnair) and validated against the Customer Sync Service and Billing App integration feeds.

Correlated gateway 504 errors with increased downstream API response times (p95 4,200ms, peak 6,800ms vs. 2s timeout threshold) on api-orders.corpsync.internal during the nightly sync window (03:00–04:30 UTC) and isolated the remaining issue to downstream Order Fulfillment service performance rather than gateway authentication or rate limiting.

Escalated the incident to the downstream Order Fulfillment service team (contact: Raj Mehta, rmehta@corplabs.com, phone ext. 4782 at the Denver operations center) with logs, distributed traces, and timing correlation for remediation of the latency spike, then placed post-change monitoring in effect via the Monitoring System to confirm timeout stabilization. Escalation tracked by Tom Hargrove (thargrove, E-50134).

Push the updated certificate-backed VPN profile and policy to affected endpoints via the Device Certificate Service and confirm the active profile matches the renewed device certificate thumbprint on each machine (verified via certlm.msc and GlobalProtect Settings > Certificate tab).

Review conditional access and device group assignments for impacted users (rnguyen, mellison, pdeshmukh) in the Okta admin console and correct any mis-mapped devices that could block compliant certificate validation — specifically verify membership in the 'VPN-Managed-Devices' group.

Validate successful reconnection with test users Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen) in Chicago, Mark Ellison (mellison) in London, and Priya Deshmukh (pdeshmukh) in Singapore by confirming the VPN tunnel remains established beyond the previous 10-30 second drop window and that Internal Web Portal, SMB file shares, and corporate intranet are all reachable end-to-end.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Users were trying to access the Internal Web Service (https://appportal.corplabs.internal) through the internal nginx load balancer at lb-web-east.corplabs.internal, but browsers showed expired-certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and dependent clients failed TLS handshakes. root_cause: The Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired, and the renewed certificate chain was not applied on the load balancer. The outage was prolonged because near-expiration certificate monitoring was not active to trigger renewal before the expiry date.

Updated the certificate bundle and intermediate chain on the load balancer lb-web-east.corplabs.internal under /etc/nginx/ssl/, then Raj Patel reloaded the nginx configuration so clients received the corrected chain with the new leaf and current intermediate certificates.

Validated successful TLS handshakes from internal clients in Austin and Raleigh through the load balancer and confirmed browser certificate warnings no longer appeared. Maria Chen verified access from WORKSTATION-MC-4417 at 10.22.45.88 was restored without errors.

Restored and documented certificate-expiry monitoring for CN=appportal.corplabs.internal with 60-day, 30-day, and 7-day alert thresholds sending to infra-certs@corplabs.com, and updated the renewal policy to ensure alerts occur before future certificate expiration. Kevin Marsh confirmed the monitoring rule is active in the platform dashboard.

title: API integration timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Overnight scheduled data synchronization jobs between the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal) and the downstream Inventory API service intermittently failed from approximately 02:00 to 03:30 UTC on 2025-12-02 in us-east-1. The gateway received repeated 504 Gateway Timeout and ETIMEDOUT responses on the /api/v2/inventory/sync endpoint, which delayed application data updates and increased integration job failures. Reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Chicago operations center — internal operations needed the scheduled sync process to complete normally so downstream application records would be current by the start of business.
root_cause: Elevated latency on the downstream service caused API responses to exceed the Integration Gateway timeout window, resulting in intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout errors and failed scheduled sync jobs.
resolution_steps: Correlated the failed sync window (02:00–03:30 UTC) with Integration Gateway latency metrics on igw-prod-east (node 10.42.18.55), Jaeger API traces for the /api/v2/inventory/sync endpoint, and downstream Inventory API endpoint health to confirm the timeout condition was external to the scheduler itself. Analysis performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Escalated the incident to the downstream Inventory API service owners — Rafael Ortega (rortega@corplabs.com, phone 312-555-0147) at the Austin office — with captured request traces, timeout evidence (47 failed jobs, p99 latency 45s), and the affected overnight time window for remediation.

Applied a temporary increase to the Integration Gateway timeout threshold from 30s to 90s on the igw-prod-east configuration (ConfigMap igw-timeout-override) so requests could complete during the period of elevated downstream latency. Change approved by team lead Jenna Whitfield (jwhitfield, EMP-30295).

Adjusted retry and backoff settings on the Integration Gateway — increased max retries from 3 to 5 and exponential backoff base from 1s to 2s — to reduce immediate job failure rates and improve recovery for intermittent downstream slow responses. Configuration deployed to igw-prod-east pods via Helm update.

Re-ran and validated the 47 previously affected synchronization jobs (sync-inv-20251202-0200 through sync-inv-20251202-0330) after downstream latency stabilized at approximately 06:15 UTC, confirming successful completion and normal data propagation to the order-fulfillment application. Validated by Marcus Delgado from the Chicago operations center.

Removed the temporary timeout increase (reverted igw-prod-east ConfigMap to 30s default) after stability was confirmed at 09:00 UTC and kept Monitoring System alerting in place to verify that 504 and timeout rates returned to baseline. Post-incident review scheduled with Rafael Ortega's team for 2025-12-04.

title: Slow Windows laptop after login

title: Print jobs stuck on PDQ-Print-Server
description: Accounting users in the Denver office were trying to print to the shared Accounting_Printer queue (\\PDQ-Print-Server\Accounting_Printer) hosted on PDQ-Print-Server, but jobs submitted by multiple staff—including Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40218) and Derek Huang (dhuang)—remained stuck in the queue with a visible "driver unavailable" state and the printer appearing offline.
