The issue was first reported via phone at ext. 303-555-4187 by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@corplabs.com).
root_cause: Corruption or mismatch in the installed Accounting_Printer driver package on PDQ-Print-Server caused the queue to report driver unavailable, reject queued jobs, and trigger recurring Print Spooler service failures.
resolution_steps: Validate the approved Accounting_Printer driver package version (HP Universal Print Driver v7.1.0) and checksum against the driver currently installed on PDQ-Print-Server (10.40.12.55); Kevin Marsh (kmarsh) confirmed installed version was v7.0.2 with a checksum mismatch.

Remove the corrupted or mismatched printer driver package (v7.0.2) from PDQ-Print-Server and reinstall the approved driver package (v7.1.0) for the affected Accounting_Printer queue using Driver Installer.
Clear all stuck jobs from the Accounting_Printer queue and restart the Print Spooler service on PDQ-Print-Server to reload the corrected v7.1.0 driver.

Run a controlled test print through Accounting_Printer from WORKSTATION-PC-MG (mgonzalez) and WORKSTATION-PC-DH (dhuang) to confirm the queue remains online and no longer returns a driver unavailable condition.

If any clients still reference the unstable mapping, remap users—including rkapoor and other Denver accounting staff—to the refreshed Accounting_Printer queue (\\PDQ-Print-Server\Accounting_Printer) and push the validated v7.1.0 driver through central deployment.

If checksum mismatch or unauthorized package drift was identified, update the Approved Printer Driver Policy so the replacement driver (HP Universal Print Driver v7.1.0) remains the supported baseline; notify kmarsh@corplabs.com for policy documentation.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failures for service.internal.company.com
description: Since about 08:30 UTC on 2026-01-13, several engineers on the platform-services team — initially reported by Raj Patel (rpatel, emp ID E-40291) — intermittently could not resolve service.internal.company.com from the internal network at the Newark datacenter. This prevented applications and command-line access (curl, nslookup, internal CI/CD pipelines) from reaching the service by hostname, even though direct IP connectivity to 10.22.4.87 still worked. Queries from workstation WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-RP (IP 10.10.52.118) against corp-resolver-01 showed the hostname resolving from cache to a deprecated IP address (10.22.4.50), indicating an internal DNS resolver or zone data inconsistency affecting engineering users in the datacenter-nyc environment. The issue was escalated via email to dns-ops@internal.company.com by Raj and confirmed by two additional engineers, Lina Chen and Marco DeSilva.
observed_errors: cached A record served deprecated IP
name resolved to old IP from internal resolver
root_cause: corp-resolver-01 was serving a stale cached A record for service.internal.company.com after the service address had changed, causing intermittent lookups to return a deprecated IP until the resolver cache and zone data were refreshed.
resolution_steps: Confirmed that corp-resolver-01 was returning a cached A record for service.internal.company.com that pointed to the deprecated IP address 10.22.4.50 instead of the current service endpoint 10.22.4.87. Verified by Tomás Rivera (trivera) using dig queries and cross-referenced with reports from rpatel and lchen in the Newark office.
Flushed the stale DNS cache on corp-resolver-01 using rndc flush to remove the outdated resolver entry (10.22.4.50) being served to internal clients on the Engineering VLAN.

Forced a reload of the Internal DNS Zone via rndc reload internal.company.com, validated the authoritative A record for service.internal.company.com was updated to 10.22.4.87 by Priya Nair (pnair), and removed the stale record (10.22.4.50) from zone data.

Ensured the zone serial was advanced from 2026011301 to 2026011302 to reflect the corrected record set so downstream resolvers including corp-resolver-01 would pick up the updated address on next refresh cycle.

Verified successful resolution to the updated IP 10.22.4.87 from Network Monitoring dashboards and multiple client hosts — including WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-RP (rpatel, 10.10.52.118) and lchen's workstation (10.10.52.134) — then monitored for recurrence over a 30-minute window and confirmed stable propagation across all Newark datacenter resolvers before closing the incident.

title: Intermittent internal DNS resolution failures for internal services
description: Internal services intermittently fail to resolve internal hostnames needed by the HR Portal (hrportal.corp.eastnet.local), Payroll API (payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local), and Internal Inventory Service (inventory.corp.eastnet.local) in the on-premises us-east-1 environment at the Newark data center. Application calls sometimes return NXDOMAIN, time out, or resolve to an older IP (10.40.2.17 instead of the current 10.40.5.33) depending on resolver location and timing. The inconsistent behavior is preventing internal-services users and application nodes from reliably reaching internal endpoints by name. Reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) from the Infrastructure Operations team. The reporter did not provide a complete hostname list or precise failure timestamps, which limited scope validation.
observed_errors: stale address observed in resolver cache
root_cause: Intermittent resolution was most consistent with inconsistent internal DNS pathing: one or more resolvers had stale cached records while conditional forwarding or zone delegation for the affected internal zone was not consistently returning authoritative answers. This caused different resolvers to return NXDOMAIN, timeouts, or outdated addresses for the same hostname until cache and forwarder configuration were corrected.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the affected internal DNS zone records on DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 for the corp.eastnet.local zone, validated current A records (hrportal → 10.40.5.33, payroll-api → 10.40.5.41, inventory → 10.40.5.52) and TTL values (300s), and corrected stale record data where resolver responses did not match the authoritative zone.

Verified conditional forwarder and zone routing configuration between internal resolvers DNS-RES-EAST-01 / DNS-RES-EAST-02 and the authoritative DNS server DNS-AUTH-EAST-01, then added the missing forwarder path on DNS-RES-EAST-02 for the corp.eastnet.local namespace.
Flushed DNS cache on impacted internal resolvers DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02 (dnscmd /clearcache) and repeated lookups to remove stale answers (10.40.2.17) previously being served from cache.

Retested name resolution from multiple resolver paths and client locations — including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88, mdelgado), APPNODE-EAST-04, and APPNODE-EAST-07 — using repeated nslookup/dig queries to confirm the same current address was returned consistently for all three affected service hostnames.

Enabled follow-up monitoring via Network Monitoring for internal name resolution on the corp.eastnet.local zone so future NXDOMAIN, timeout, or stale-answer patterns can be correlated with affected hostnames and timing if the issue recurs. Notified Marcus Delgado (mdelgado), Janelle Torres (jtorres), and Raj Mehta (rmehta) of the resolution.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please provide any affected internal hostnames (e.g., hrportal.corp.eastnet.local, payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local), approximate failure times, and whether the NXDOMAIN or timeout behavior changes by site or application server so we can compare resolver paths. Also, can you confirm which client machines or app servers you've tested from? If you have nslookup or dig output from WORKSTATION-PC-MD or any of the app nodes, please attach those as well. — Priya Nair, Network Engineering

title: Software Center blocks AccountingApp install after prior fix

root_cause: AccountingApp deployment was targeted based on entitlement membership that was not correctly reflected on the device record, and the endpoint had stale management inventory/policy data. This caused Software Center policy evaluation to continue failing the entitlement check even after the initial access change.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the required AccountingApp entitlement assignment for mreyes (EMP-90214) and corrected targeting so the managed device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR was included in the appropriate SWDeploy-AccountingApp-Eng entitlement group.
Triggered an immediate Intune device sync for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (IP 10.42.17.88) to refresh policy and group membership data on the endpoint, performed by Priya Nambiar.
Forced a Software Center/SCCM machine policy and inventory evaluation cycle on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR so the client would recalculate available application deployments for mreyes.
Reviewed endpoint protection/application approval settings for AccountingApp by Kevin Tran and verified no active protection rule was denying the approved installer on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR.

Validated that AccountingApp became visible and installable in Software Center on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR for Marcus Reyes (mreyes), confirmed the Install button was active, and completed a successful installation test. Notified user at mreyes@corplabs.com of resolution.

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve
description: Users and monitoring in the Newark region were trying to reach the Internal App Service by the hostname internal-app.service.local, but since about 06:15 UTC on 2026-01-15 the name intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or timed out from the internal DNS resolver cluster (resolver-01.dns.corp.internal / resolver-02.dns.corp.internal). This prevented the Internal Portal and dependent application calls from reaching the service endpoint by name and caused multi-tier application errors. Initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com, ext. 4417) from the DevOps team, and corroborated by alerts from Network Monitoring dashboards. Affected users include members of the platform engineering and QA groups working from the Newark office.
observed_errors: stale A record returned by resolver-01
root_cause: Internal DNS resolvers served stale cache data for internal-app.service.local, including an outdated A record pointing to a decommissioned IP, while TTL mismatch between the authoritative zone and resolver cache allowed the incorrect response to persist intermittently across resolver-01 and resolver-02.
resolution_steps: Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone entry on ns-auth-01.dns.corp.internal for internal-app.service.local and confirmed the A record was already updated to the current service IP 10.40.2.30; corrected the residual TTL value from 86400 to 300 seconds to match policy.

Flushed cached DNS entries on resolver-01.dns.corp.internal and resolver-02.dns.corp.internal using rndc flush to remove the stale record (10.40.1.15) and clear intermittent NXDOMAIN and timeout responses affecting users in the Newark region.
Restarted the DNS resolver service (named) on resolver-01.dns.corp.internal where persistent cached data was observed to ensure fresh zone data was served and no in-memory stale entries remained.

Validated name resolution from multiple internal clients — including Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.22.4.87), the QA jump host at 10.22.6.50, and Network Monitoring probes in Newark and Ashburn — and confirmed queries returned the corrected A record (10.40.2.30) consistently.

Adjusted the internal TTL policy for service records to 300 seconds on ns-auth-01.dns.corp.internal and aligned resolver caching behavior (max-cache-ttl) on resolver-01 and resolver-02 to reduce the chance of prolonged stale responses. Change documented by Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo) and reviewed by Priya Nair.

title: Users stuck in MFA prompt loop during SSO login — Engineering group
description: Engineering users (approximately 35 members of the ENG-CORE group) were trying to sign in through the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com to reach Salesforce, Gmail, and other SaaS applications, but were repeatedly returned to MFA challenges instead of completing login. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) at around 15:10 UTC and quickly confirmed by several other engineers in the Austin office. The issue began after the 09:00 UTC scheduled identity configuration change (CHG-20260410-017) and blocked affected users from accessing core web applications needed for normal work. Initial reports came in via Slack from team lead Derek Owens.
root_cause: A conditional access configuration mismatch introduced by an Azure AD group claim mapping change caused Engineering users to be evaluated with an incorrect MFA state. That mismatch exposed stale MFA enrollments in Okta, resulting in repeated MFA challenges and an SSO login loop.
resolution_steps: Corrected the Azure AD conditional access group claim mapping in policy 'ENG-SaaS-MFA-v2' so Engineering group membership (ENG-CORE) was evaluated against the intended policy scope, reverting the erroneous change made by admin jnelson at 09:12 UTC.

Reviewed affected policy assignments in Azure AD and Okta and confirmed the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) and downstream SaaS applications (Salesforce, Gmail, Jira) were no longer triggering the incorrect MFA decision path for Engineering users. Validated by agent Priya Laghari (plaghari).

Performed a bulk MFA unenroll/reset for 35 affected Engineering users in Okta (ENG-CORE group, Austin office) to remove stale factor enrollments contributing to the challenge loop. Reset executed by plaghari using Okta Admin Console.

Required impacted users to re-enroll MFA factors in Okta Verify and verified fresh enrollment status after reset. Confirmation emails sent to all affected users including mchen@corplabs.com and dowens@corplabs.com with re-enrollment instructions.

Validated successful end-to-end SSO login for pilot users rkapoor and mchen, then the wider Engineering group (35 users), to confirm access to Salesforce and Gmail without repeated MFA prompts. All users confirmed working by 17:45 UTC.

Documented the identity policy correction in CHG-20260410-017 post-incident notes and notified Identity Support lead Priya Laghari and Engineering stakeholders including team lead Derek Owens (dowens@corplabs.com, phone 512-555-0174) of the completed remediation and re-enrollment requirement.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive from the mapped network path \\FS-FIN-01.corplabs.internal\Finance$ after a recent group membership update. Windows prompted for credentials and then returned Access Denied (0x80070005), preventing me from listing or opening the Finance department folder needed for normal work. My username is rgarcia and my workstation is WORKSTATION-PC-RG. Directory checks showed I was already in the Finance_SharedDrive AD group (CN=rgarcia,OU=Finance Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal), but access to the file server path still failed. I need this resolved urgently as quarter-end reporting is due this week. My employee ID is EMP-40821 and I can be reached at rgarcia@corplabs.com or ext 4-7193.
observed_errors: NTFS explicit deny ACE observed in audit
root_cause: Access was blocked by NTFS permissions on the Finance department folder, where an explicit deny ACE and broken inheritance overrode the allow permissions granted through the Finance_SharedDrive AD group. The issue was not caused by missing group membership; it was caused by conflicting folder ACL configuration on the file server.
resolution_steps: Confirmed rgarcia's membership in the Finance_SharedDrive AD security group (CN=rgarcia,OU=Finance Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) and verified replication had completed across all domain controllers so directory entitlement was current.

Reviewed the Finance folder ACLs on FS-FIN-01.corplabs.internal, specifically \Finance$\Department_Reports, identified an explicit deny ACE and inheritance inconsistency affecting the target path, and removed the deny condition from the folder permissions.

Restored the intended permission inheritance on the Department_Reports folder and reapplied the correct allow access (Read/Write) for the Finance_SharedDrive group, ensuring all subfolders inherited the corrected permissions.
Cleared rgarcia's cached network credentials on WORKSTATION-PC-RG using 'cmdkey /delete:FS-FIN-01.corplabs.internal' and had the F: drive remapped so the client reconnected with a fresh access token.

Retested access from WORKSTATION-PC-RG (IP 10.22.14.87) to the current Finance shared drive path \\FS-FIN-01.corplabs.internal\Finance$\Department_Reports and confirmed rgarcia could open and list the folder without receiving Access Denied events. Rosa Garcia confirmed normal access was restored.
agent_questions: Hi Rosa, thanks for reporting this. Please sign out of WORKSTATION-PC-RG and back in, then retry the current Finance shared drive path \\FS-FIN-01.corplabs.internal\Finance$ instead of any saved shortcut. Let us know whether it still prompts for credentials and returns Access Denied. If the issue persists, please also try accessing from a different machine if one is available at the Austin office. — Kevin Marsh, Service Desk

title: Software Center installation blocked by policy entitlement

My name is Derek Lewis (employee ID EMP-90234) and I'm based in the Charlotte office. My device IP is 10.42.18.77.

resolution_steps: Verified in Intune that the endpoint WORKSTATION-DL-4417 (IP 10.42.18.77, user dlewis / Derek Lewis, EMP-90234) was enrolled and healthy but not assigned to the application's required entitlement group APP-AdobeCC-Marketing, matching the Software Center policy failure.

agent_questions: Hi Derek, please confirm whether the application (Adobe Creative Cloud) is missing from Software Center entirely on WORKSTATION-DL-4417 or appears and then fails with a policy or entitlement message when you try to install it. Also, can you confirm your username so I can check entitlement group membership? This is Agent Rachel Nguyen, ticket INC-SIB-0052.

title: Users receive 'No network access'
description: Multiple Sales users on Windows 10 laptops in the Denver office were able to join the Corp-WiFi SSID but then received "No network access" and could not reach intranet or other internal resources. The issue was first reported by Maria Castillo (EMP-40291) and subsequently confirmed by at least four other users in the same region. The issue began after a recent certificate rotation window on 2026-05-01. Client-side logs on affected machines such as WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC showed 802.1X authentication failures and EAP-TLS certificate validation errors, indicating wireless association succeeded but network authentication was being rejected by the backend wireless and NAC infrastructure.
observed_errors: Device receives no network access after joining SSID
root_cause: The Wireless Controller certificate used for 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication had expired, causing certificate validation to fail and Network Access Control to reject authenticated wireless sessions.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the Wireless Controller certificate had expired and renewed the certificate for CN=corp-wlc.corplabs.internal with the correct trust chain for EAP-TLS authentication; renewal was performed by Raj Patel (rpatel) using the internal PKI and validated against the enterprise root CA.

Deployed the renewed certificate to all affected wireless controllers including WLC-DENVER-01 and WLC-DENVER-02 and validated the controllers were presenting the updated certificate during 802.1X authentication.

Removed the temporary NAC exception that had been applied as a workaround for the Sales user group (mcastillo, jnorris, tgarcia) after certificate renewal was completed and full EAP-TLS authentication was restored.

Had affected users including Maria Castillo (mcastillo), Jake Norris (jnorris), and Teresa Garcia (tgarcia) forget and reconnect to the Corp-WiFi SSID so their devices established a fresh 802.1X session against the renewed controller certificate.

Monitored Wireless Controller and NAC authentication logs to verify successful EAP-TLS validation and normal policy assignment for previously affected devices, confirming all three users in the Denver office were authenticating cleanly with no further certificate validation errors.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outage
description: Internal users and automated monitors at the Denver data center were trying to reach the Internal Web Service endpoint (internalweb.corplabs.internal) over TLS, but the endpoint began presenting certificate warnings and failing health checks overnight starting around 03:45 UTC on 2025-12-22. Clients reported ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and TLS handshakes failed across multiple paths, which made the service unavailable to dependent internal applications including the payroll portal and inventory management system. The issue was first flagged by automated Nagios checks and then confirmed by infrastructure operator Marcus Ellison (mellison@corplabs.com) who was on-call. The outage persisted until the certificate and load balancer chain were corrected.
root_cause: The Internal Web Service leaf TLS certificate expired, and after the initial renewal attempt the updated certificate chain was not fully deployed on the Load Balancer. Missing or ineffective certificate renewal alerting allowed the expiry to occur unnoticed and delayed correction of the full chain configuration.
resolution_steps: Renew the expired TLS certificate (serial 4A:9C:03:FF, CN=internalweb.corplabs.internal) with the internal Certificate Authority and obtain the replacement leaf certificate required for the Internal Web Service endpoint. Renewal request submitted by Priya Nagarajan (E-40821) and approved via the certificate management workflow.

Deploy the renewed leaf certificate to the Internal Web Service host and verify the presented certificate matches the expected service name (internalweb.corplabs.internal) and validity period (new Not After: 2026-12-22). Confirmed via openssl s_client direct connection from WORKSTATION-DELL-ME by Marcus Ellison.

Update the Load Balancer (LB-CENTRAL-02.corplabs.internal) TLS configuration with the correct certificate chain, including the renewed CorpLabs Intermediate CA G3 certificate, and reload the TLS listener so clients receive the full valid chain. Configuration change performed by David Kowalski (dkowalski) at 05:18 UTC and verified.

Perform end-to-end TLS validation from representative clients (WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-DK at the Denver facility, monitoring host MON-CENTRAL-01, and client IP 10.42.17.85) and automated monitoring paths to confirm certificate warnings and handshake failures are fully cleared across all routing paths.

Restore and tighten certificate expiry monitoring and renewal alert thresholds (rule cert-expiry-notify-001, re-enabled by Anita Reyes) so future renewals are detected at 30, 14, and 7 days before the certificate reaches expiration. Added secondary notification channel to the infrastructure-ops Slack channel and email distribution list (infra-ops@corplabs.com) to prevent single-point-of-failure in alerting.

title: Device marked Noncompliant (missing encryption) — Conditional Access blocks access
description: I (Rachel Nguyen, emp ID EMP-40821) on an Intune-managed Windows device (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-RN) was blocked from accessing Exchange Online because Conditional Access required a compliant device. Company Portal showed the device as Noncompliant after a recent policy review, even though I reported the device had been online and recently synced from the Arlington office. The immediate impact was loss of access to protected Microsoft 365 resources needed for normal work in the Marketing department.
observed_errors: Compliance state: Noncompliant (reported in Company Portal)
Conditional Access blocked sign-in to Exchange Online
root_cause: BitLocker/device encryption on the endpoint was suspended or otherwise not in an active protected state, causing the encryption compliance requirement to fail and Conditional Access to block access.
resolution_steps: Confirmed local BitLocker status on device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN via remote PowerShell (manage-bde -status C:) and identified that protection was suspended rather than missing due to stale reporting. Agent Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) coordinated with Rachel Nguyen to perform the remediation.

Re-enabled BitLocker protection on WORKSTATION-DELL-RN by running 'manage-bde -protectors -enable C:' and verified the encryption state returned to healthy on the endpoint. Protection status confirmed as 'Protection On' after the command completed.

Triggered a device sync from Company Portal on WORKSTATION-DELL-RN and confirmed Intune marked the device Compliant again within approximately 5 minutes. Validated that Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) could successfully sign in to Exchange Online without Conditional Access blocks. Ticket closed by agent mdelgado.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, we can see the device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN (IP 10.42.18.97) is marked Noncompliant in Intune under your account rnguyen@corplabs.com. Please confirm whether Company Portal also shows an encryption-related compliance issue and whether the device has been online recently.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal service payroll-svc
description: Finance users in the Charlotte office were trying to reach payroll-svc.internal.corp this morning, but the internal service hostname intermittently failed to resolve from the primary on-prem DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.internal.corp, 10.40.2.10). Some lookups returned NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL, while direct access by IP (10.40.50.22) still worked, blocking normal access to the payroll service by name. The issue was first reported by Maria Espinoza (mespinoza, EMP-90412) via the Finance team channel. Investigation showed the primary resolver was intermittently serving a stale A record (pointing to decommissioned address 10.40.50.18) that did not match the current authoritative internal zone data on ns-auth-01.internal.corp.
root_cause: Primary on-prem DNS resolver cache retained and intermittently served a stale A record for payroll-svc.internal.corp that no longer matched the authoritative internal zone, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL and failed name resolution.
resolution_steps: Compared responses from the primary resolver dns-resolver-01.internal.corp (10.40.2.10) and the authoritative internal DNS server ns-auth-01.internal.corp to confirm the resolver was returning stale data (10.40.50.18) for payroll-svc.internal.corp instead of the current record (10.40.50.22).
Cleared cached DNS entries on the primary resolver dns-resolver-01.internal.corp using rndc flush to remove the outdated A record (10.40.50.18) from cache. Executed by ktran at 01:38 UTC.

Forced a reload of the authoritative internal zone on ns-auth-01.internal.corp using rndc reload to ensure the current payroll-svc.internal.corp record (10.40.50.22, zone serial 2026011502) was being served consistently.

Restarted the named service on the primary resolver dns-resolver-01.internal.corp (systemctl restart named) to reset resolver state and eliminate lingering stale cache behavior. Service confirmed healthy via rndc status.

Reduced the TTL for the affected A record from 86400s to 300s (5 minutes) and adjusted DNS caching policy for critical internal services in the internal.corp zone to reduce stale-serving windows during future record changes. Change documented under CHG-44821.

Validated successful name resolution with nslookup/dig from multiple sites — WORKSTATION-PC-ME (10.40.11.87, Charlotte) and WORKSTATION-PC-JW (10.40.12.44, Raleigh) — and confirmed Network Monitoring alerts cleared after fresh responses matched the authoritative zone. Maria Espinoza and James Whitfield confirmed payroll-svc.internal.corp was loading reliably by hostname.

title: Software Center installation blocked by entitlement check
description: I was trying to install AppX from Software Center on my corporate Windows 10 PC (hostname WORKSTATION-PC-MR, IP 10.42.17.88), but the application was not available as expected and the install attempt failed with an entitlement check error. A transient Endpoint Protection block also interfered with the installer until it was cleared.

title: Multiple users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple Engineering users in the Austin office were trying to access Salesforce and Gmail through the corporate SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com), but after successful primary SSO sign-in they were repeatedly returned to the Okta MFA challenge. Users including Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) and Derek Patel (dpatel) reported that approving Okta Verify push notifications or entering TOTP codes on both mobile and laptop did not complete login, blocking access to all downstream SaaS applications. access_denied / invalid_grant observed in Okta logs
root_cause: Stale Okta MFA enrollments and prior device registrations caused MFA token invalidation after SSO, resulting in repeated challenge loops instead of successful token issuance to downstream applications.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Okta authentication logs for affected users (rng0042, dpatel, twong, kfisher) and confirmed repeated MFA token invalidation (access_denied / invalid_grant) during post-SSO access attempts to Salesforce and Gmail.

Reset MFA enrollment for the four affected users in Okta Admin Console to remove stale factor and device registration state. Bulk reset was authorized by identity team lead Sandra Liu (sliu@corplabs.com).

Had users re-enroll their Okta Verify authenticator application and complete a fresh MFA push verification. Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) and Derek Patel (dpatel) confirmed successful re-enrollment from their respective workstations.

Validated that all four users could complete SSO once and successfully reach Salesforce and Gmail without returning to the MFA prompt. Rachel Nguyen confirmed access from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and Derek Patel from WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-DP.

Updated the Identity Support playbook to include a factor enrollment health check (enrollment age > 12 months flag) when users report repeated MFA prompt loops, and notified Marcus Webb (mwebb@corplabs.com) that all affected Engineering team members in Austin have been restored.

title: Expired TLS certificate causing internal web service TLS failures and browser warnings
description: Internal users were trying to access the Internal Web Service over HTTPS at https://internal-web.svc.corp, but browsers displayed certificate warnings and the service could not be reached securely. Multiple reports came in from the Chicago office starting around 16:45 UTC, initially filed by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@corplabs.com). Users saw NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID in Chrome and Firefox, and dependent connections through the load balancer (LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal) recorded TLS handshake failures. The issue affected the internal-web service running in Kubernetes namespace prod-web in us-east-1 after the deployed certificate for internal-web.svc.corp (serial 4A:F2:9C:01) expired at 2025-12-20T02:00Z and the updated certificate chain was not present on the load balancer. Ticket initially triaged by helpdesk agent rkapoor (emp ID EMP-40821).
observed_errors: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal-web.svc.corp expired on the load balancer, and the required updated certificate chain was not deployed, causing client certificate validation failures and backend TLS handshake errors.
resolution_steps: Reissue a valid TLS certificate for internal-web.svc.corp through the internal Certificate Authority (CA-EAST-01.corplabs.internal) with a current validity period (2025-12-20 to 2026-12-20) and correct subject alternative names (internal-web.svc.corp, *.internal-web.svc.corp). Certificate reissuance performed by phwang on the CA Team.

Deploy the renewed certificate and the full updated certificate chain (including CorpLabs Issuing CA G3 intermediate) to the load balancer LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal certificate store, ensuring the chain order is correct and no expired intermediate certificate remains attached. Deployment executed by jnelson.

Reload or restart the affected TLS listener on load balancer LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal so the new certificate bundle is actively served to clients. Listener restart confirmed by jnelson at 2025-12-20T18:05Z.

Validate HTTPS access to the service from a client perspective (tested from WORKSTATION-DELL-MG at 10.42.18.77 by mgonzalez and from Austin office workstation WORKSTATION-HP-DL at 10.44.6.22 by dlopez) and confirm browser warnings and load balancer TLS handshake failures are no longer occurring.

Restore and verify certificate renewal monitoring and alerting for the service in cert-management-service (rule cert-renew-internal-web re-enabled by rkapoor) so future renewals are detected at least 30 days before expiration. Alert notification configured to email phwang@corplabs.com and the infra-alerts distribution list.

title: Print jobs stuck on PS-PRINT01
description: Several Finance users in the Newark office were trying to print to the shared Finance printer queue (\\PS-PRINT01\FIN-HP-4050) hosted on PS-PRINT01, but submitted jobs stayed at 0% in the queue and the printer appeared offline from their workstations. The issue was first reported by Maria Castillo (emp ID FIN-20483) around 18:45 UTC. observed_errors: Spooler event: driver failed to initialize
root_cause: Corruption in the installed HP Universal Printing driver on PS-PRINT01 prevented the Print Spooler from loading the driver for the Finance queue, causing jobs to remain stuck at 0% and the printer to appear offline to users.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Finance print queue \\PS-PRINT01\FIN-HP-4050 and confirmed 17 jobs were stuck at 0% while PS-PRINT01 logged repeated HP Universal Printing driver load failures (Event ID 372). Affected users included mcastillo, ryuen, and pdeshmukh in the Newark Finance group.

Cleared the 17 stuck print jobs and restarted the Print Spooler service on PS-PRINT01 to remove transient queue state before driver remediation. Verified spooler restarted cleanly but new submissions still failed.

Reinstalled the approved HP Universal Printing driver package v7.1.0.25 from the corporate driver repository (\\DRV-REPO01\Approved\HP-UPD) on PS-PRINT01 to replace the corrupt driver files, restoring correct hpuni*.dll hashes.

Remapped the Finance printer queue \\PS-PRINT01\FIN-HP-4050 to the refreshed driver instance and verified the queue was online after spooler restart. Confirmed driver loaded without errors in spooler log.

Sent a test print from Maria Castillo's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC (10.42.18.77) and from Robert Yuen's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-RY, then monitored the queue for 30 minutes to confirm jobs processed normally without additional driver initialization failures. Notified all affected Finance users via email that printing was restored.

Validated Marcus Hoffmann's Conditional Access group membership (Remote Workforce — EMEA) in Okta and confirmed no access policy issue was blocking the post-authentication VPN session for user mhoffmann.

Tested a new VPN connection from WORKSTATION-DELL-MH (client IP 192.168.1.47) after certificate renewal and profile refresh. Application launch times >30s for Outlook and Word
Disk free space ~8% on C: drive
root_cause: Endpoint protection full-scan backlog running at login, combined with multiple resource-heavy startup items and critically low free disk space on the C: drive, caused sustained post-login CPU contention and slow application launches.

Disabled two nonessential startup items — OneDrive auto-sync (High impact) and Dell SupportAssist updater (High impact) — via Task Manager Startup tab on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and rebooted to reduce startup contention for m.reeves.

Refreshed device and endpoint policy via Endpoint Management console (gpupdate /force) so the system did not immediately restart the same heavy scan state after cleanup; confirmed policy sync completed successfully for m.reeves' device.

Verified CPU returned to normal idle behavior (3–5%) after login on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and confirmed Outlook launch time improved to ~4 seconds and Word to ~3 seconds — normal user-acceptable performance. Notified Marcus Reeves at m.reeves@corplabs.com that the issue is resolved.

title: Outlook clients not syncing mail after recent policy push
description: Multiple users in the Charlotte and Frankfurt offices were trying to access current email from Outlook Desktop and Outlook Mobile after a morning device compliance policy update pushed at approximately 06:45 UTC, but mailbox sync stopped, Outlook showed "Disconnected," and mobile mail updates stalled. The issue was first reported by Maria Castillo (emp ID: EMP-40291) from Sales and quickly confirmed across managed Windows 10 and iOS devices, blocking normal email access for Sales and Field Engineering users. Exchange Online diagnostics indicated repeated EWS HTTP 429 throttling on affected mailboxes while Intune showed affected devices—including WORKSTATION-MC-D14 and several iOS handsets—in a non-compliant state following the policy revision.
observed_errors: Mail sync stalled / MAPI/HTTP sync failures
root_cause: A recent device compliance policy push left some managed endpoints in a non-compliant state while several affected Outlook clients also had stale local profiles. The compliance block disrupted normal mobile and client access patterns, and repeated retry behavior contributed to Exchange Online EWS throttling (HTTP 429), resulting in disconnected Outlook sessions and stalled mailbox synchronization.

title: Cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi (CorpNet) — authentication failed
description: User Daniel Reeves (dreeves@corplabs.com, EMP-40821) reported being unable to connect a managed macOS 12.6 MacBook (hostname: MACBOOK-DREEVES) to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet) from the Manhattan office. resolution_steps: Confirmed the active RADIUS/Wireless Controller certificate (CN=radius.corplabs.internal, serial 4A:7F:0C:B2) had expired on 2026-05-04 and was being presented during CorpNet 802.1X authentication attempts, causing Access-Reject for users including dreeves and mchang.

Completed the planned certificate renewal and rollout across all affected wireless controllers and RADIUS services in the Manhattan office so all CorpNet authentication paths used the renewed certificate chain.

Refreshed client connectivity by instructing impacted users — including Daniel Reeves (dreeves) and Monica Chang (mchang) — to forget and rejoin CorpNet or receive the updated wireless profile through device management.

Validated successful reconnection on MACBOOK-DREEVES (user dreeves, IP 10.42.17.112) and reviewed post-change RADIUS authentication logs to confirm certificate-related Access-Reject failures had cleared for all previously affected Engineering group clients.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failure for AppTeam
description: AppTeam engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: E-40291) reported that two application hosts (APPNODE-PRD-01 and APPNODE-PRD-02) in the corp-datacenter-1 on-prem environment at the Phoenix facility were unable to reliably reach the internal API endpoint api.internal.corp. Over roughly the last two hours, DNS lookups intermittently failed with NXDOMAIN when the hosts queried the corporate DNS resolver at 10.12.4.10, while a public resolver (8.8.8.8) returned valid A records for the same name. This inconsistency prevented the application cluster from reliably resolving the internal endpoint by name and created intermittent service reachability failures impacting downstream batch processing. No recent zone-file change was confirmed at intake, and initial resolver logs were not attached. Priya can be reached at priya.nair@corplabs.com or ext 4-7183 for follow-up.
root_cause: Internal DNS resolution for api.internal.corp was impacted by stale or incorrect resolver-side handling of the zone, most likely a missing or incorrect conditional forwarder and/or cached negative response on the corporate resolver path. The symptom pattern of intermittent NXDOMAIN from the internal resolver while another resolver returned A records is consistent with resolver configuration or cache state rather than an application issue.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone on authoritative nameserver ns1.internal.corp (10.12.4.20) and confirmed the expected A record for api.internal.corp (10.20.50.12) and its TTL of 300 seconds were present and current.

Corrected the resolver path for the internal.corp zone by adding the missing conditional forwarder configuration on the corporate DNS resolver 10.12.4.10, pointing internal.corp queries to the authoritative nameserver ns1.internal.corp (10.12.4.20) to handle affected app-server queries.

Cleared stale DNS cache entries, including any negative cached NXDOMAIN responses for api.internal.corp, on the affected internal resolver 10.12.4.10 using `rndc flush` and instructed cache flush (`systemd-resolve --flush-caches`) on the impacted application hosts APPNODE-PRD-01 and APPNODE-PRD-02.

Re-ran name resolution tests from the affected hosts APPNODE-PRD-01 (10.20.31.44) and APPNODE-PRD-02 (10.20.31.45) against the corporate resolver 10.12.4.10 and confirmed api.internal.corp returned the expected A record (10.20.50.12) instead of NXDOMAIN.

Validated repeat queries after cache refresh from both application hosts and user workstation WORKSTATION-PNAIR to confirm resolution consistency across the Phoenix datacenter environment, and closed the incident after intermittent lookup failures were no longer reproducible over a 30-minute monitoring window.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please run `dig @10.12.4.10 api.internal.corp A` from both APPNODE-PRD-01 (10.20.31.44) and APPNODE-PRD-02 (10.20.31.45), attach /etc/resolv.conf from both affected hosts, and confirm whether the NXDOMAIN response is coming only from the internal resolver path. Also, can you verify whether your teammate Raj Menon on the AppTeam cluster sees the same behavior from his workstation WORKSTATION-RM-PC? Please send results to dns-ops@corplabs.com so we can correlate. — Kevin Albrecht, Network Operations

title: Print jobs stuck: corrupt printer driver on Print Server causing queue failures
