title: Expired TLS certificate on internal web service causing TLS outage
description: Internal users in the Arlington office were trying to access internal-websvc over HTTPS, but beginning around 2025-12-22 09:34 UTC the browser showed certificate date warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and dependent clients could not complete TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@example.corp) from the internal-dev team. The F5 load balancer LB-01 for internal-websvc.example.corp presented an expired certificate, blocking normal secure access to the internal service until the renewed certificate and full chain were deployed. Multiple teams including build automation and QA were affected as their CI pipelines depend on internal-websvc endpoints.
root_cause: The TLS certificate presented by LB-01 for internal-websvc.example.corp expired at 2025-12-22 09:30 UTC. Renewal alerting did not trigger as expected, and although a renewed certificate was available from the CA, the updated full certificate chain was not deployed to the load balancer before expiration.
resolution_steps: Retrieved the renewed TLS certificate (serial 6D:01:AF:55:C3:28:9E:17) for internal-websvc.example.corp from the internal Certificate Authority (CorpCA) distribution share and verified it matched the intended service endpoint SAN entries. Verification performed by Raj Patel (rpatel).

Installed the renewed certificate and updated the full certificate chain (root + intermediate CorpCA-Intermediate-G2) on LB-01 by importing the new bundle into the F5 certificate store and updating the SSL profile 'clientssl-internal-websvc' so the load balancer no longer presented the expired certificate.

Reloaded the load balancer TLS configuration on LB-01 via iControl REST API to activate the new certificate binding for the internal-websvc listener (VS-WEBSVC-PROD). Confirmed the new certificate serial 6D:01:AF:55:C3:28:9E:17 was being presented on the VIP 10.200.5.60:443.

Validated successful TLS handshakes from internal client WORKSTATION-MCHEN-04 (10.42.17.88) and load balancer perspectives using openssl s_client. Confirmed certificate warnings no longer appeared for internal users including Maria Chen and the QA team in the Arlington office. Browser and curl tests returned valid certificate chain with notAfter=Dec 22 09:30:00 2026 GMT.

Cleared related monitoring alerts in internal-monitoring, re-enabled the 'cert-expiry-warning-30d' alert rule, restored certificate renewal alerting to cert-ops-alerts@example.corp, and documented follow-up actions to audit the svc-certrenew deployment pipeline authentication (fix HTTP 401 against LB-01 API) and add post-renewal deployment verification checks. Diana Torres (dtorres) assigned as owner for the follow-up task TASK-CES-0052.

title: Integration Gateway: API timeouts
description: Scheduled nightly data sync jobs through the Integration Gateway began failing around 03:10 UTC on 2025-12-06 in us-east-1. The affected integration, managed by service account svc-datasync-prod (employee ID EMP-40821), showed elevated API latency with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and preceding 401 Unauthorized errors from the API service endpoint at api-gateway-east.corplabs.internal. This blocked the nightly synchronization workflow for the data-sync-service until authentication was restored and the gateway could complete API calls successfully. Issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Denver integration operations team.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway service account token expired, and the scheduled rotation job did not refresh the credential in time, causing authentication failures that cascaded into integration call timeouts.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration service account token for svc-datasync-prod (EMP-40821) had expired at 2025-12-06T03:00:00Z and confirmed the active credential in the secrets vault (secret/prod/datasync/api-token) no longer matched a usable API token. Verification performed by Rafael Ortiz (rortiz) from the platform engineering team.

Rotated the expired API service token for the svc-datasync-prod integration account and updated the centralized secrets vault entry (secret/prod/datasync/api-token) with the new credential. New token issued with a 90-day TTL and confirmed valid against api-gateway-east.corplabs.internal.

Restarted the Integration Gateway service on INTGW-PROD-01.corplabs.internal (pod intgw-prod-deployment-7c4d9 in the eks-prod-east cluster) so the application reloaded the refreshed secret and stopped sending unauthorized requests.

Re-ran the failed nightly sync workflow (job data-sync-nightly-20251206) and verified the integration completed successfully without further 401 or 504 errors. Confirmation provided by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) from the Denver operations team at 17:45 UTC.

Adjusted the credential rotation schedule from 90-day to 60-day intervals with a 7-day pre-expiry warning alert, and updated retry/backoff settings (max retries from 3 to 5, exponential backoff ceiling raised to 60s) to reduce the risk of future token-expiry-related timeout failures. Changes reviewed by Priya Nair (pnair) and committed to the infrastructure-as-code repository.
agent_questions: Reviewing the nightly sync failure window now. I can see the alerts originated from host INTGW-PROD-01.corplabs.internal in us-east-1. Please confirm whether there were any recent credential, secret rotation, or integration account changes to the svc-datasync-prod service account before the 03:10 UTC failures started. Also, Marcus — was anyone else on the Denver team aware of pending vault secret expirations?

title: Intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal host 'app-db.internal' from one client subnet
description: Users on the 10.20.30.0/24 internal subnet at the Denver office reported intermittent inability to reach the internal application database host app-db.internal under corp.local, while teams on other networks (e.g., 10.20.40.0/24) reported mixed results. The initial report came from Maria Castillo (emp ID E-20487) who noticed that her workstation WORKSTATION-MC-7741 could not connect to internal services that depend on name resolution. The failure affected access to internal services used by the Internal Apps group, but the reporting context was limited and did not confirm whether the issue was caused by missing DNS data, stale resolver answers, or client path differences. Diagnostics focused on comparing resolver behavior with the authoritative internal DNS service and checking whether cache handling changed the outcome.
root_cause: Suspected misconfiguration or instability in the corporate resolver path for the internal zone caused intermittent SERVFAIL responses even though the authoritative corp.local records were healthy.
resolution_steps: Escalate to the DNS or network infrastructure team (contact: Raj Patel, rpatel, phone 512-555-0173) to review conditional forwarding, recursion behavior, and resolver health for the affected internal zone path on resolver 10.20.30.2 serving the Denver 10.20.30.0/24 subnet.

Capture resolver logs on 10.20.30.2 and compare behavior on the impacted resolver against a known-good corporate resolver (e.g., 10.20.40.2) during repeated test queries for app-db.internal and other corp.local hostnames, documenting SERVFAIL frequency and forwarding latency.

As an interim workaround, direct affected clients or dependent services to a known-good internal resolver (10.20.40.2) where permitted — Maria Castillo (mccastillo) on WORKSTATION-MC-7741 and other impacted users on 10.20.30.0/24 should update their DNS settings accordingly — then retest hostname resolution and application connectivity to app-db.internal (expected A record 10.50.10.22).
agent_questions: Please confirm the DNS resolver IP used by a client on 10.20.30.0/24 (e.g., Maria Castillo's workstation at 10.20.30.114) and whether dig for app-db.internal returns NXDOMAIN consistently from that subnet while succeeding from a known-good subnet such as 10.20.40.0/24. If possible, run the test from WORKSTATION-MC-7741 and share the output. You can reach me at dns-ops@corplabs.com or contact Raj Patel (rpatel) on the network team for assistance.

title: Software Center installation blocked - entitlement missing
description: I was trying to install FinanceApp from Software Center on my managed Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-MR), but the install was blocked and the application was not visible in the catalog. Client logging showed PolicyCheckFailed during the install attempt, preventing me from obtaining the required finance application through the normal self-service process. My username is mreeves and I'm based out of the Philadelphia office. Please advise on next steps.
root_cause: User was not a member of the FinanceApp entitlement group required for Intune/Software Center application assignment, so policy evaluation failed and the app was not offered in the catalog.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Software Center and client-side policy behavior on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (IP 10.42.17.88) to confirm the install request from mreeves was failing during application policy evaluation with a PolicyCheckFailed condition.
Checked the FinanceApp deployment assignment in Intune and confirmed the affected user mreeves (EMP-90274) was missing from the required FinanceApp_Entitled entitlement group.
Added user mreeves to the FinanceApp_Entitled group so the application assignment would apply to the user as intended. Change performed by agent Derek Huang and verified in Intune portal.
Triggered a device inventory refresh and Software Center policy sync on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR to accelerate receipt of the updated app entitlement and catalog targeting for mreeves.

Verified the FinanceApp assignment became available to WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, then had Marcus Reeves retry the installation and confirm the application installed successfully. User confirmed via email at mreeves@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus Reeves, can you confirm whether FinanceApp is missing from the Software Center catalog entirely on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and whether the client log consistently shows PolicyCheckFailed when you try to install it? I can see your account mreeves is associated with the Finance-Staff group — I'll begin checking the Intune assignment targeting in the meantime.

title: VPN disconnects
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 21H2 laptop (WORKSTATION-LP-MGARCIA) at the Frankfurt office. My username is mgarcia and I authenticate via Okta MFA push to my phone. The Okta MFA approval succeeded, but the VPN tunnel disconnected within about 10 seconds after authentication and internal resources such as the intranet (https://intranet.corplabs.com) and file shares (\\fs-emea-01.corplabs.internal\shared) became unreachable. My client IP before the drop was 10.47.132.88. The issue recurred after a recent device certificate renewal pushed by the Device Certificate Service, indicating the certificate update alone did not correct the client profile state. I need VPN access restored urgently for a project deadline — please contact me at maria.garcia@corplabs.com or ext 4471 if needed.
root_cause: GlobalProtect client retained a stale VPN profile after device certificate renewal, causing a mismatch between the renewed certificate and active VPN profile and terminating the tunnel immediately after successful MFA.
resolution_steps: Removed the stale GlobalProtect VPN profile (dated 2026-02-11) from the affected endpoint WORKSTATION-LP-MGARCIA so the client no longer attempted to use outdated post-renewal settings that referenced the previous certificate thumbprint.

Forced a fresh GlobalProtect profile download from the management plane via gw-emea.vpn.corplabs.com to restore the current gateway and certificate mapping on WORKSTATION-LP-MGARCIA, ensuring the profile now referenced the renewed device certificate issued 2026-04-15.

Re-enrolled WORKSTATION-LP-MGARCIA through the Device Certificate Service to ensure the renewed device certificate was correctly associated with the newly applied VPN profile and that the certificate binding was validated end-to-end.

Restarted the GlobalProtect connection flow on WORKSTATION-LP-MGARCIA and user mgarcia completed Okta MFA push approval to confirm the tunnel no longer disconnected after authentication; the tunnel remained stable and the assigned IP 10.47.132.88 persisted.

Validated sustained VPN connectivity for mgarcia over a 30-minute observation window and confirmed Maria Garcia could again access internal applications including the intranet (https://intranet.corplabs.com) and file shares (\\fs-emea-01.corplabs.internal\shared) from the Frankfurt office.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — thanks for reporting this. I'm picking this up as your assigned agent. Can you please confirm whether the Okta push notification on your device is approved successfully and whether GlobalProtect drops before login completes or only after the VPN status shows 'Connected'? Also, could you verify the hostname of the laptop you're connecting from (I see WORKSTATION-LP-MGARCIA in the asset register) and confirm your employee ID so I can cross-reference your Okta sign-on logs? You can reach me at r.okonkwo@corplabs.com if you have questions.

title: Orders sync failing
description: Scheduled order-sync processing (job: order-sync-prod-batch-7a) to the external API through the Integration Gateway began failing around 2025-12-12 03:40 UTC with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (order-processing team lead) after downstream order data failed to appear in the external fulfillment system. Retries are not draining the backlog — queue depth reached ~4,200 pending records on pod order-sync-worker-6d8f4 in us-east-1. Impact is limited by manual retry handling initiated by mdelgado from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (10.42.18.93), but the sync workflow remains blocked until gateway timeout behavior, token validity, and possible downstream latency or rate limiting are verified. Contact: mdelgado@corplabs.com / ext 4-7831.
root_cause: Primary cause remains unconfirmed because Integration Gateway logs for the failure window and token rotation history were not provided. Current evidence supports an upstream integration timeout condition affecting outbound calls from the Integration Gateway to the API Service, with the most likely contributors being expired integration credentials, downstream API latency beyond the configured timeout window, or API rate limiting during the 03:30-04:00 UTC period.
resolution_steps: Collect and review Integration Gateway logs from node igw-prod-east-01 for 2025-12-12 03:30–04:00 UTC to identify whether the 504 responses align to authentication failures (HTTP 401/403), rate-limit behavior (HTTP 429), or sustained upstream latency exceeding the 30-second timeout threshold. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) to coordinate log extraction with the platform team.

Validate the integration token (credential ID: cred-ordersync-ext-2025) used by service account svc-ordersync and compare its rotation or expiry history to the incident start time at 03:40 UTC; rotate the credential immediately via the secrets vault if it is expired or was changed without corresponding gateway configuration updates on igw-prod-east-01.

If credentials are valid, review gateway and downstream API latency during the incident window using Monitoring System traces for pod order-sync-worker-6d8f4 (IP 10.42.18.107) and confirm whether response times exceeded the current order-sync timeout threshold of 30 seconds.

Check for rate-limit (HTTP 429) or retry-exhaustion indicators in igw-prod-east-01 gateway records and, if present, reduce burst behavior by tuning order-sync retry intervals from the current 5-second fixed delay to an exponential backoff policy (initial 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled) rather than increasing immediate retry count.

After evidence is collected, rerun the failed synchronization backlog (~4,200 pending records) in controlled batches of 200 from pod order-sync-worker-6d8f4 and escalate to the downstream API team (contact: Ramon Ortiz, rortiz@corplabs.com) if 504 behavior persists with valid credentials and normal request volume.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — this is Priya Nair from Application Support. Please provide Integration Gateway logs from gateway node igw-prod-east-01 for the 03:30–04:00 UTC window, and confirm whether the API token (credential ID: cred-ordersync-ext-2025) was rotated or if request volume increased during that window. We need to separate timeout, auth, and rate-limit causes. Also, can you verify from your end whether the service account svc-ordersync shows any recent credential changes in the vault? You can reach me at pnair@corplabs.com or ext 4-2209.

title: Print jobs stuck on server PS-PRINT01
description: Office users in the Columbus branch reported that printing to the shared HP LaserJet on PS-PRINT01 was failing even though the printer was visible and accepting submissions. The issue was first reported by Diana Nakamura (dnakamura, EMP-40821) and confirmed by several colleagues on the 4th floor. Jobs entered the shared queue but did not complete, and some users received access-related printing errors instead of the earlier offline behavior. The issue affected normal document printing through the server-hosted queue and appeared limited to processing on the print server rather than workstation connectivity. Diana's workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DN at 10.42.18.77 could see the printer but jobs never printed.
observed_errors: EventID 7011: Service timeout while waiting for Print Spooler
root_cause: Incorrect permissions on the affected shared printer queue or associated spool directory on PS-PRINT01 prevented the Print Spooler from processing submitted jobs.
resolution_steps: Review the affected printer queue security settings and spool folder (C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS) NTFS permissions on PS-PRINT01 for the svc-printspooler service account and authenticated users. Trevor Chen (tchen, EMP-30294) confirmed the ACLs were modified by a recent GPO push.

Restore the standard print queue and spool directory permissions from the approved server baseline, granting svc-printspooler full control and authenticated users print access. Applied by tchen on PS-PRINT01.

Restart the Print Spooler service on PS-PRINT01 and submit test print jobs from impacted users dnakamura (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DN), mreilly (WORKSTATION-PC-MR), and pokonkwo to verify jobs complete without access errors. All three users confirmed successful printing after the fix.
agent_questions: Hi Diana — please confirm whether all users printing through PS-PRINT01 are seeing jobs stuck in queue or driver unavailable errors, and whether the printer appears offline from their PCs. Can you also check if your colleague Marcus Reilly (mreilly) on the same floor is experiencing the same behavior? You can reach me at t.chen@corplabs.com or ext 4-7183 if needed.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive from my Windows 10 client (WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES, IP 10.22.47.118) using the mapped network path \\Shared\\Finance. Windows prompted for credentials and then returned "Access is denied," preventing access to Finance files. My username is mreeves and I reported membership in the FINANCE_USERS AD group, but access still failed, indicating a likely mismatch between group-based entitlement and the file server folder ACL. I need this resolved urgently as quarter-end reporting deadlines are approaching.
root_cause: NTFS permissions on \\Shared\\Finance were misconfigured: the FINANCE_USERS Active Directory group was not present on the folder ACL, likely due to broken or removed permission inheritance. The user's group membership was valid, but the file server ACL did not grant the expected access, which caused the credential prompt and access denied response.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Finance share NTFS permissions on FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal and confirmed the FINANCE_USERS group was missing from the \\Shared\\Finance folder ACL despite valid AD membership for mreeves (employee ID EMP-20418).

Restored the intended permission inheritance or reapplied the approved Finance folder ACL so that FINANCE_USERS was included with the correct access rights (Read/Write). Change performed by file services admin nwilliams in the Charlotte office.
Validated that share and NTFS permissions were aligned on FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal and that no explicit deny entry or broken inheritance continued to block access for FINANCE_USERS members.

Cleared any cached Windows credentials and removed the stale mapped drive connection on the user's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES (IP 10.22.47.118), then remapped \\Shared\\Finance using net use commands executed by mreeves.

Retested access with the user mreeves after the ACL correction and confirmed the Finance shared drive opened successfully without prompting again for credentials. Marcus Reeves confirmed via email at mreeves@corplabs.com that all Finance files were accessible.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm whether you are opening the current \\Shared\\Finance path and whether the credential prompt still appears after disconnecting and remapping the drive. Also, can you verify you're logged in as mreeves on WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES and not using any alternate credentials? I've assigned this to our file services team in Charlotte for further review if needed.

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed on corporate device
description: A corporate Windows 10 21H2 laptop, WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (asset tag PC-1234), assigned to Marco Hoffmann (emp ID EMP-90214) in the Frankfurt office, was flagged noncompliant in Intune because disk encryption was not fully compliant. I could not complete required corporate compliance checks because BitLocker protection showed as suspended and the management service did not have an escrowed recovery key available for support recovery. The device was enrolled under the user account mhoffmann and had IP 10.42.17.88 at the time of enrollment. Enrollment evidence indicated the issue started during initial device enrollment when recovery key backup failed with error 0x87D1FDE8.
root_cause: BitLocker recovery key escrow failed during initial MDM enrollment, leaving the device with a protector present but no recovery key recorded in the Device Compliance Service, while BitLocker protection remained suspended.
resolution_steps: Confirmed TPM 2.0 availability and existing BitLocker protector state on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (PC-1234, user mhoffmann, EMP-90214), then verified the device was receiving the assigned encryption policy EMEA-Sales-Encryption-v3 in Intune.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH using manage-bde -protectors -delete C: followed by manage-bde -protectors -add C: -RecoveryPassword, and triggered a fresh recovery key backup to the Device Compliance Service to replace the missing escrow record for mhoffmann.

Forced an Intune/Windows MDM sync from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (IP 10.42.17.88) via Company Portal so the updated protector and escrow status were reported to compliance services. Sync completed successfully at 2026-01-17T18:38Z.

Validated that the new recovery key was visible in the Device Compliance Service under Marco Hoffmann's device record (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH) and available for support recovery operations. Confirmed with agent Lukas Brandt (lbrandt@corplabs.com) that the key was accessible.

Re-enabled BitLocker protection on the OS drive C: using manage-bde -protectors -enable C:, verified encryption protection was active (AES-256, full volume), and confirmed the device returned to compliant status in Intune. Notified Marco Hoffmann at marco.hoffmann@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: We confirmed Intune shows device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (PC-1234), registered to mhoffmann, as noncompliant for encryption. The Intune device record lists the primary user as Marco Hoffmann (marco.hoffmann@corplabs.com). Can you confirm whether this is the same corporate laptop PC-1234 and whether any recent enrollment or reset activity occurred before the compliance failure appeared?

title: Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway with conflicting token/latency evidence
description: Scheduled internal batch jobs using the Integration Gateway (gateway cluster igw-prod-east-01) began failing intermittently after a recent deploy (build 4.7.2-rc3, deployed 2025-12-04T03:45Z), causing delayed data synchronization and missed downstream deliveries over an approximately 3-hour window starting around 04:00 UTC. The issue was reported by Marcus Ellison (mellison@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta data operations team, who noticed that several overnight ETL batches tied to service account svc-batch-integ failed to complete. Gateway monitoring showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses aligned with elevated downstream service latency on the Order Fulfillment API endpoint (/api/v2/orders/sync). Some client traces from host WORKSTATION-BATCH-ME also showed 401 Unauthorized responses, indicating a secondary token validity issue that complicated diagnosis.
root_cause: Primary cause was elevated downstream service latency causing the Integration Gateway to exceed its timeout window and return intermittent 504 responses after the deploy. A secondary expired or stale API token condition was also present on some client calls, producing intermittent 401 errors, but this was not the dominant driver of the batch failure spike.
resolution_steps: Validated the failure window (04:00–07:00 UTC) against Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-01) and downstream Order Fulfillment API latency metrics in the Monitoring System to confirm the timeout pattern was primarily latency-driven (p99 >12s vs. 5s gateway timeout) rather than a full authentication outage.

Rotated the integration API token for service account svc-batch-integ to remove the intermittent expired or stale credential condition seen in client traces from 10.42.18.77 (WORKSTATION-BATCH-ME), and updated the credential in the gateway's secret store.

Increased Integration Gateway retry count from 2 to 4 and adjusted exponential backoff settings (initial delay from 500ms to 1500ms, max delay from 3s to 10s) on igw-prod-east-01 so transient downstream latency spikes would not immediately fail scheduled batch requests.

Cleared the gateway request queue (approximately 180 backed-up requests) and restarted the affected gateway pod igw-worker-7b4c to remove backed-up requests created during the latency spike. Darren Cho from the platform team confirmed pod health post-restart.

Escalated the downstream latency condition to the Downstream Service Team (contact: Raj Patel, rpatel@corplabs.com) with aligned gateway logs from igw-prod-east-01 and Monitoring System performance evidence for service-side remediation, while keeping monitoring alerts in place to verify timeout reduction after the gateway changes. Follow-up review scheduled for 2025-12-05.
agent_questions: We are seeing both 504 timeout spikes at the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-01) and some 401 responses in client traces originating from 10.42.18.77. Can you confirm whether failures started after the 4.7.2-rc3 deploy at 03:45 UTC and whether all batches are affected or only a subset of integrations? We'd also like to know if the service account svc-batch-integ credentials were refreshed as part of the deployment. — Priya Nair, Application Support

title: account locked after repeated failed sign-ins from mobile device
description: I was trying to sign in to corporate resources after a recent password change on 2025-11-19, including access through the Password Reset Portal and SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com), but remained blocked because my Active Directory account (jmartinez) showed as locked. Password reset attempts appeared to complete successfully, yet repeated failed sign-in attempts from my corporate iPhone continued to trigger lockout and prevent access. My employee ID is E-40821 and I'm based out of the Raleigh office. Please help — I have a deployment deadline this morning.
platform: On-prem Active Directory with Azure AD Connect
observed_errors: Event ID 4740 - A user account was locked out.
Authentication failure entries from mobile device (multiple invalid credential attempts)
SSO error: token rejected after password change (transient)
root_cause: Cached credentials on a corporate mobile device continued submitting stale authentication attempts after the user's password change, which repeatedly failed and triggered the Active Directory lockout policy before the new password could be used successfully.
resolution_steps: Reviewed AD lockout events (Event ID 4740) on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal for the jmartinez account and confirmed the repeated failed authentication source was the user's corporate mobile device IPHONE-JMARTINEZ (IP 10.42.17.88) with cached credentials submitting 23 invalid attempts.

Unlocked the jmartinez Active Directory account (CN=jmartinez,OU=Engineering,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) via ADUC to clear the lockout condition and restore eligibility for authentication. Performed by Rachel Kim (rkim) on the identity team.

Issued a fresh password reset token through the Password Reset Portal and confirmed Jorge Martinez completed a new password reset for jmartinez@corplabs.com so the current credential state was known and valid across on-prem AD and Azure AD Connect.

Instructed Jorge to remove and re-add the corporate account on IPHONE-JMARTINEZ (Outlook, Teams) and re-enroll SSO at https://sso.corplabs.com to clear stale cached credentials and tokens. Walked through steps over phone at 972-555-0148.

Monitored authentication activity for jmartinez after the reset and mobile remediation from 06:42Z to 08:42Z on 2025-11-20 and confirmed no further failed attempts or additional lockouts were recorded on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal.
agent_questions: Hi Jorge, thanks for reaching out. After your recent password change, do you still have your corporate account (jmartinez@corplabs.com) configured on a mobile device such as Outlook, Teams, or other collaboration apps that may be using the old password? I can see lockout events on your account originating from a device registered as IPHONE-JMARTINEZ. Could you confirm whether that's your phone?

title: Users unable to connect to Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Employees across the Arlington corporate office were unable to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) using 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) at approximately 06:45 UTC on 2026-05-05. Client devices showed certificate-related authentication failures — specifically 'certificate expired' and 'secure connection failed' prompts — and users were left without network access after attempting to connect. The problem affected broad office connectivity across floors 2–5 until wireless authentication certificates issued by the internal CA (ca-pki.corplabs.internal) were renewed and controller profiles corrected.
observed_errors: RADIUS: TLS handshake failed due to expired certificate
root_cause: The certificate used for wireless 802.1X authentication had expired, causing TLS validation failures between the wireless infrastructure and RADIUS authentication flow and blocking EAP-TLS authentication for Corporate Wi-Fi clients.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the expired certificate (CN=wifi-auth.corplabs.internal, expired 2026-05-04T23:59:59Z) in the wireless authentication path on radius01.corplabs.internal and installed a valid signed replacement certificate issued by ca-pki.corplabs.internal to restore successful 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication. Initial temporary certificate applied by Raj Patel (rpatel) at 07:32 UTC.

Updated the Wireless Controller (WLC-ARLINGTON-01) TLS profile to reference the active replacement certificate and aligned the controller configuration with the corrected authentication chain, verified by rpatel and confirmed via test association from WORKSTATION-RPATEL-L14.

Cleared stale authentication sessions on radius01.corplabs.internal and restarted the affected 802.1X/authentication services on the RADIUS server so new client attempts would use the updated certificate. Confirmed session table cleared of 47 stale entries.

Validated the full certificate chain (root CA → intermediate → wifi-auth.corplabs.internal) and revocation settings on ca-pki.corplabs.internal, then confirmed successful authentications in RADIUS and controller logs with test devices including WORKSTATION-MCHEN-T14 (user mchen, IP reassigned 10.22.4.118) and WORKSTATION-DKOW-X1 (user dkowalski).

Coordinated follow-up certificate distribution and client re-enrollment where needed through MDM endpoint management to ensure affected devices across the Arlington office trust and use the renewed wireless certificate. Notified impacted users including Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) and David Kowalski (dkowalski@corplabs.com) via email with reconnection instructions.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether multiple users across the Arlington office are failing to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) and whether devices show any 802.1X or certificate-related message during connection. If possible, can you share a screenshot or the exact error text from your device (hostname if available)? Also, are users on both Windows and macOS affected, or only one platform?

title: account locked after repeated mobile sign-in failures
description: I (Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-40291) was trying to sign in to the SSO Portal from my corporate iPhone after attempting a password reset earlier the same day. I initiated the reset from the Password Reset Portal around 3:45 PM, but when I returned to complete it the portal reported that the token was expired. Subsequent sign-in attempts from my device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) at IP 10.42.18.77 returned an 'ERROR_ACCOUNT_LOCKED' message. This prevented access to all SSO-protected applications — including CRM and email — until the AD lockout on my account (mdelgado) was cleared and the mobile device stopped sending stale cached credentials.
root_cause: Active Directory lockout policy was triggered by repeated failed authentication attempts from stale cached credentials on the user's corporate mobile device, and the earlier password reset token had expired before the reset was completed.
resolution_steps: Unlocked the Active Directory account for mdelgado (CN=mdelgado,OU=Sales,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and confirmed the lockout counter was reset to zero. Performed by agent Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen).

Issued a new password reset token (TKN-88467) through the Password Reset Portal for mdelgado and verified the user could successfully complete the password reset at 22:53 UTC. New password propagated to all domain controllers within 60 seconds.

Had Marcus Delgado remove saved credentials on the mobile device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) and reconfigure the SSO-related sign-in profile for Outlook and Teams so the device no longer submitted outdated credentials to https://sso.corplabs.com.

Validated in AD authentication logs that the corporate mobile device at IP 10.42.18.77 (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) was the sole source of the repeated failures and disabled the legacy cached authentication path on that device by enforcing modern authentication via MDM policy.

Monitored authentication activity for mdelgado from 23:00 UTC through 2025-11-23T02:00 UTC after remediation and confirmed no additional failed sign-in bursts or lockout events occurred. Case closed and user Marcus Delgado notified at marcus.delgado@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — thanks for reaching out. Please confirm whether you retried sign-in from your corporate mobile device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) after the reset attempt, and whether any mail or collaboration apps on that device (e.g., Outlook, Teams) still had the old password saved under your account mdelgado. Also, can you confirm you were connecting from the Charlotte office Wi-Fi or over cellular? This will help us trace the lockout source in the AD logs.

title: Print jobs stuck on Floor 2 printer
description: Users on Floor 2 at the Manhattan office were trying to print to the shared HP M477 queue (\\PRINTSRV-NYC-02\Floor2-HPM477) from their workstations, but jobs submitted by staff including Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) remained at 0% on the Windows Server 2016 print server and the printer appeared offline after a recent driver update pushed on 2026-03-03. A spooler restart and queue clear performed by desktop support tech Raj Patel provided only temporary relief, and the issue returned within 24 hours, blocking normal office printing for approximately 30 staff members using the shared queue on the second floor.
root_cause: The shared Floor 2 printer queue remained mapped to a stale driver GUID after the recent driver change, while the installed printer driver package was corrupt or not the approved version. This caused print spooler crashes, driver load failures, and jobs to stall at 0% with the printer showing offline.
resolution_steps: Removed the incorrect or corrupt printer driver package (HP Universal Print Driver v6.5.0, GUID {4A3B21CF-8E7D-4F12-9C6A-1D5E0F3B7A82}) from the print server PRINTSRV-NYC-02 and reinstalled the approved HP Universal Driver version 6.8 using the package from the corporate driver repository.
Remapped the Floor 2 HP M477 shared queue (\\PRINTSRV-NYC-02\Floor2-HPM477) to the current driver GUID so the queue referenced the correct v6.8 driver package, verified by Lisa Nakamura (lnakamura).

Cleared 14 stalled jobs from the affected print queue (submissions from mchen, dokonkwo, rpatel, and others) and restarted the Print Spooler service on PRINTSRV-NYC-02 to restore normal queue processing.

Validated that the spooler remained stable on PRINTSRV-NYC-02 and that a test print submitted by Raj Patel from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP moved through the queue without new crash events or retry loops; confirmed with Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) and David Okonkwo that their workstations could print successfully.

Updated the approved printer driver deployment policy in the print management console so future driver refreshes push the corrected HP Universal Driver v6.8 package and do not revert the Floor2-HPM477 queue to the older GUID mapping; change documented by Lisa Nakamura (E-50891) in the Workplace Services change log.

title: VPN disconnects
description: I'm Rachel Nguyen (employee ID MKT-40218) from the Marketing team, working remotely from Portland. I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my Windows 10 managed laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) at IP 10.42.88.115 in order to reach internal resources including the HR portal, intranet, and Salesforce. After approving the Okta MFA prompt on my phone, the VPN session authenticated briefly and then disconnected immediately, causing repeated MFA prompts and complete loss of access to internal applications. My username is rnguyen and I've been unable to work for the past hour.
root_cause: The endpoint's device certificate had expired, so GlobalProtect failed the post-MFA TLS handshake and tore down the VPN tunnel even though Okta MFA approval succeeded.
resolution_steps: Validated in GlobalProtect gateway logs on gw-west-02.corp.internal that the disconnect for user rnguyen (source IP 73.189.22.64, device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) occurred after successful Okta MFA and that the TLS handshake failure referenced an expired endpoint device certificate (serial 4A:7F:C2:91:0B, expired 2026-04-15).

Renewed the affected endpoint's device certificate on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN through the Device Certificate Service so the certificate presented to the VPN gateway was valid again. New certificate issued with NotAfter=2027-04-17. Renewal performed remotely by Priya Desai (desktop support).

Refreshed the GlobalProtect VPN profile on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN for user rnguyen and cleared the stale enrolled certificate association so the client used the renewed certificate for tunnel establishment.

Retested the VPN connection from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (IP 73.189.22.64) and confirmed the tunnel stayed established after Okta MFA approval. TLS handshake completed successfully with the renewed device certificate.
Verified that Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen) could reach internal applications including the HR portal, intranet, and Salesforce over the restored VPN session from Portland.

Updated the device certificate auto-renewal policy to trigger renewal 30 days before expiration and added an offline-device retry mechanism to reduce the chance of future certificate-expiration disconnects. Notified Kevin Marsh to monitor for similar cases in the Marketing group.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, thanks for reaching out. I'm Kevin Marsh from the service desk. Could you please confirm whether the Okta MFA prompt is approved successfully before the VPN disconnects, and whether the drop happens immediately after approval? Also, can you confirm you're connecting from your assigned device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN using your rnguyen account? I'd like to cross-reference the GlobalProtect gateway logs with your session.

title: Laptop running slowly
description: User Marcus Delgado (emp ID EMP-40291) reported that his managed Windows 10 corporate laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) became very slow immediately after sign-in following a morning policy push on 2026-02-05. CPU usage rose to about 90% within a minute of login on IP 10.22.47.118, Outlook, Chrome, and Windows Explorer took 30-60 seconds to open, and normal post-login work was significantly delayed. Marcus is based out of the Charlotte office in the Sales - Mobile Workforce group. Impact appeared limited to the affected endpoint and was associated with recently applied startup and device policy changes pushed via Intune.
observed_errors: CPU 92% shortly after user login (observed via Task Manager)
Multiple startup processes with elevated CPU
root_cause: A recently applied startup application policy introduced or re-enabled multiple resource-heavy startup items and service activity at user logon, causing sustained CPU contention and delayed application launches.
resolution_steps: Reviewed active startup processes and svchost-hosted service activity after login on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD (user mdelgado, IP 10.22.47.118) to confirm policy-related CPU contention on the affected laptop, identifying IntuneManagementExtension.exe, duplicate OneDrive sync triggers, and telemetry collectors as primary offenders.

Disabled non-essential startup items on Marcus Delgado's user profile (mdelgado) to reduce immediate post-login CPU load and restore usability, removing redundant telemetry collectors and a duplicate OneDrive sync task introduced by the policy.

Triggered a device policy refresh from Intune on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD so the endpoint would receive the latest managed configuration state and reconcile with the corrected Corporate Startup Application Policy.

Updated the Corporate Startup Application Policy in Intune to remove unapproved or unnecessary startup entries (including duplicate sync triggers and redundant telemetry agents) that were contributing to high CPU after sign-in across the Sales - Mobile Workforce device group.

Rebooted the laptop WORKSTATION-DELL-MD and validated that CPU utilization dropped below 20% after login and application launch times returned to normal levels (Outlook: ~3.5s, Chrome: ~2s, Explorer: immediate).

Scheduled follow-up cleanup for the broader Charlotte Sales device group and advised Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) to report any recurrence after future policy deployments; ticket escalation contact is Kevin Pratt (kpratt@corplabs.com, ext. 4782).

title: Outlook desktop shows 'Disconnected' and mobile email stopped syncing
description: I was trying to access corporate email from Outlook on my Windows 10 desktop (WORKSTATION-DSKTP-MR) and from my managed iPhone, but desktop Outlook showed a 'Disconnected' state and the mobile client stopped receiving new mail for about 48 hours starting around February 14th. New messages remained available in Exchange Online webmail at https://outlook.office365.com, indicating the mailbox for mreeves@corplabs.com was reachable while local Outlook connectivity or device sync/compliance was preventing normal client synchronization. This blocked normal email access outside OWA for me, Marcus Reeves, a Corporate Sales user based in the Charlotte office. My employee ID is E-50821 and my desk phone is (704) 555-3198 if anyone needs to reach me directly.
root_cause: Exchange Online mailbox service was healthy because new mail was visible in OWA, while both Outlook desktop and mobile sync were stale. The most likely cause is endpoint-side client sync failure affecting Outlook profile state and mobile device partnership/compliance rather than a server-side mailbox outage; evidence remains incomplete because requested compliance and sync-state confirmation was not provided.
resolution_steps: Verified the mailbox for mreeves@corplabs.com was accessible and updating in Exchange Online webmail (https://outlook.office365.com), which isolated the issue away from a full mailbox outage or credential failure for employee E-50821.

Directed Marcus Reeves to review mobile device management and Intune compliance status for the affected iPhone and remediate any non-compliant state (e.g., pending OS update or expired compliance policy) before retesting mail sync. Provided contact for Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) on the MDM team for assistance.
Advised clearing and re-establishing the affected mobile mail ActiveSync partnership or re-adding the mreeves@corplabs.com mailbox on the mobile device after Intune compliance was confirmed healthy.

Advised testing Outlook connection behavior on WORKSTATION-DSKTP-MR in a clean Outlook profile (Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles > Add) to rule out a stale cached profile causing the desktop client to remain in 'Disconnected' state.

Provided next-step guidance that if Intune compliance was healthy and a clean Outlook profile on WORKSTATION-DSKTP-MR restored sync for mreeves@corplabs.com, the old Outlook profile should remain replaced; otherwise the ticket should be routed to Priya Nair or the Exchange administration team for deeper ActiveSync mobile partnership or endpoint review.

Also, can you verify that you're signing in with mreeves@corplabs.com and that no password change occurred recently? Your device IP 10.42.18.77 shows as active on the network, so connectivity to Exchange Online should be available.

title: Intermittent corporate Wi‑Fi access after certificate expiry
description: Multiple corporate employees in the Raleigh office (Building A) and a subset of remote users were unable to join or stay connected to the Corp-WiFi SSID on managed laptops, phones, and BYOD devices. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) and confirmed by several colleagues on the 3rd floor. Devices associated to the wireless network but then showed 802.1X authentication failed, EAP failure code 23, or no network access after connection. Affected devices included WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (Maria's ThinkPad, IP 10.22.8.114) and at least four other endpoints. The issue began during the wireless certificate expiry window on the WLC-BLDGA-01.corp.local controller and blocked normal corporate network access for on-site and remote staff.
root_cause: Expired RADIUS/WLAN certificate on the wireless controller caused 802.1X/EAP authentication failures; a subset of endpoints also retained stale cached Wi-Fi profiles or trust state until the profile was removed and re-enrolled.
resolution_steps: Renewed and correctly bound the expired RADIUS/WLAN certificate (CN=wlc-bldga-01.corp.local, serial 4A:7C:9E:01) on WLC-BLDGA-01.corp.local used for Corp-WiFi 802.1X authentication. The new certificate was issued by CorpLabs-CA with a 2-year validity period. Work performed by Kevin Briggs (kbriggs).

Restarted WLAN services on WLC-BLDGA-01.corp.local at 09:52 UTC so the controller presented the renewed certificate to new authentication requests. Verified the new certificate thumbprint was active on all WLAN interfaces serving the Raleigh Building A APs.

Validated that ClearPass NAC/controller authentication attempts were succeeding again by monitoring live sessions for mchen, dpatel, and other affected users, confirming that devices could authenticate and receive normal Corp-Employee network access policy assignment.

Removed stale wireless profiles on remaining impacted devices (including IPHONE-MCHEN and three BYOD tablets) by having users forget Corp-WiFi and reconnect, then re-enrolled devices that still failed due to cached profile or certificate trust state through the ClearPass onboarding portal. Confirmed full restoration with Maria Chen and Derek Patel.

Implemented certificate expiry monitoring on WLC-BLDGA-01.corp.local via the existing Nagios alerting framework with 30-day and 7-day advance warnings sent to the Raleigh network team distribution list (netops-raleigh@corplabs.com), and scheduled automated certificate rotation through CorpLabs-CA to prevent recurrence of controller-side authentication failures.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm you are connecting to Corp-WiFi and whether the device reports authentication failed or connects briefly with no network access. Can you also confirm the hostname of your laptop? We are reviewing the controller certificate status on WLC-BLDGA-01.corp.local and pulling 802.1X authentication logs from ClearPass NAC for your account (username: mchen). We've also asked Kevin Briggs from the Raleigh network team to check the local AP cluster.

title: Internal DNS names failing to resolve from corporate resolver
description: Internal users and dependent services across the Denver office were trying to resolve hostnames under corp.local through the corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local, 10.20.1.10), but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or outdated A records instead of the current internal addresses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Ellison (EMP-40821) from the infrastructure team, who noticed that internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local were unreachable by name from his workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.20.44.87). Monitoring indicated the authoritative internal DNS servers (ns1-auth.corp.local, ns2-auth.corp.local) had updated records while the corporate resolver continued serving stale cached responses from corp-dc-1. Several other users including Priya Nagarajan also confirmed intermittent failures from their machines.
root_cause: Corporate DNS resolver cache contained stale internal A records and continued serving outdated answers after authoritative corp.local zone records had been updated.
resolution_steps: Flushed the stale cache entries on the primary corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) using rndc flush to remove outdated A records (e.g., 10.10.10.5) being returned for affected corp.local hosts including internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local.

Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone contents on ns1-auth.corp.local and ns2-auth.corp.local for impacted records and confirmed the current addresses (10.20.30.15, 10.20.30.22, 10.20.30.40) were correct on the authoritative servers. SOA serial and zone transfer status validated between both authoritative nodes.

Adjusted TTL values for the affected zone records from 86400 seconds (24 hours) to 3600 seconds (1 hour) to reduce the likelihood and duration of long-lived stale cache entries after future record changes. Change approved by Raj Mehta and applied to the corp.local zone on ns1-auth.corp.local.

Validated name resolution from representative clients — Marcus Ellison's workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.20.44.87) and Priya Nagarajan's workstation WORKSTATION-HP-PN (10.20.44.93) — and Network Monitoring paths to confirm the resolver now returned the same current addresses as the authoritative servers. All three affected service endpoints confirmed reachable by FQDN.

Documented the cache validation and flush procedure (rndc flush on dns-resolver-01.corp.local) in the DNS support playbook and continued post-change monitoring via Network Monitoring for 48 hours for recurrence. Sent closure notification to mellison@corpnet.com and pnagarajan@corpnet.com confirming resolution.
agent_questions: Comparing affected corp.local lookups between the corporate resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) and authoritative DNS servers (ns1-auth.corp.local, ns2-auth.corp.local) now. Running nslookup and dig queries for internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local from Marcus Ellison's workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME at 10.20.44.87 and from the Network Monitoring probe in Denver. Need to confirm whether failures are stale answers at the resolver or missing records in the internal zone. — Raj Mehta, Network Engineering

title: Outlook desktop stopped syncing
description: After a local profile restore earlier this morning on my workstation (WORKSTATION-DELL-MR), I could no longer receive current mailbox updates in Outlook for Windows. My Exchange Online web access at https://outlook.office365.com showed new messages normally under my account mreeves@corplabs.com, but the desktop client displayed a Disconnected state and stopped updating folders. Mobile sync on my iPhone was intermittent and the device was flagged noncompliant in Intune, blocking normal email use from the desktop client. This is impacting my ability to respond to customers from the Austin office. — Marcus Reeves (EMP-40821)
observed_errors: Autodiscover 401 authentication failures in client logs
Sync timeouts reported in client (no specific error code)
root_cause: Stale Outlook profile data and cached Autodiscover configuration on the restored Windows client caused authentication failures (Autodiscover 401) and left Outlook bound to an outdated local profile GUID; device compliance state also needed remediation before sync fully stabilized.
resolution_steps: Created a new Outlook mail profile on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and re-added Marcus Reeves' Exchange Online account (mreeves@corplabs.com) to replace the stale restored profile containing outdated GUID B7E3A1D4-9F02-4C88-A6D1-3E7F50C812AA.

Removed the local OST file (mreeves@corplabs.com.ost) from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Outlook and cleared cached Autodiscover settings from the registry so Outlook could rebuild mailbox data and service discovery from a clean state.

Validated mailbox health for mreeves@corplabs.com in Exchange Online admin center and confirmed new mail was present in OWA, isolating the issue to the client and local configuration on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR.

Checked the device status for IPHONE-MR-SYNC in Intune, remediated compliance state by triggering a fresh compliance evaluation, and verified the managed device was marked compliant for user mreeves@corplabs.com.

Updated the client's Autodiscover policy reference on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR from the legacy policy entry to AutodiscoverPolicy_v2 and confirmed Outlook reconnected successfully with a valid authentication token for mreeves@corplabs.com.

Tested send/receive on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR after profile recreation and cache reset, confirming the Outlook connection state returned to Connected and new mailbox items synchronized to the desktop client. Marcus Reeves confirmed full functionality restored at 04:38 UTC. Ticket closed by Priya Nair.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm whether new mail is visible in Outlook on the web (https://outlook.office365.com) for your account mreeves@corplabs.com, and whether the desktop client changed behavior after any recent local restore, profile change, or device action on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR. Also, can you confirm the IP address you're connecting from so we can check network-level blocks?

title: account locked after repeated failed sign-ins
description: I (Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-50821) was trying to sign in to the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com after resetting my password through the Password Reset Portal about an hour earlier. Instead of gaining access, I continued to receive ACCOUNT_LOCKED messaging after multiple failed sign-in attempts from my workstation (WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD, IP 10.42.17.88) and my iPhone. The issue affected a hybrid identity path between on-prem Active Directory and the cloud SSO platform. I also reported that my mobile device kept prompting with the old cached password, preventing successful authentication. I'm based in the Charlotte office on the Sales team and need access restored urgently for a client demo tomorrow morning.
root_cause: The account was locked by Active Directory after repeated failed sign-in attempts from a mobile device using stale cached credentials. At the same time, the prior self-service password reset token had expired or not fully propagated, which delayed the password reset state reaching the SSO platform and left the user unable to authenticate until the lockout and token state were corrected.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the authentication issue for Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, E-50821) and manually unlocked the user's Active Directory account on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal to clear the active lockout condition (triggered by 14 failed attempts from IP 10.42.19.203) and reset the lockout counter to zero.

Validated the password reset state in the Password Reset Portal for mdelgado, cleared the expired reset token (originally issued at 17:58 UTC, TTL exceeded), and issued a new valid reset token so the password change could be accepted and propagated correctly to directory-backed services.

Forced synchronization between Active Directory and the SSO connector to push the updated credential state and unlock status for mdelgado to the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com; confirmed propagation completed within 90 seconds.

Advised Marcus Delgado to remove saved or cached credentials from his iPhone's mail and Outlook apps so the device would stop submitting the old password and triggering additional failed sign-in attempts against the mdelgado account.

Monitored authentication activity for mdelgado after the corrective actions for 30 minutes and confirmed successful sign-in from WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD (IP 10.42.17.88) at 19:42 UTC without continued lockout events. Case closed by agent Priya Nair.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reaching out. Can you confirm whether your mobile device (iPhone) is still prompting for sign-in using the old password flow? Also, can you check whether the password reset confirmation email sent to m.delgado@corplabs.com showed any token expiry details? We'd like to match that against the lockout activity we're seeing on your AD account (CN=mdelgado,OU=Sales,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) so we can isolate the source of the repeated failed attempts.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Internal developers on the Platform Engineering team were trying to access the internal API at https://internal.example.corp/v2/services over HTTPS, but browsers began showing certificate warnings and automated clients (including CI/CD pipelines running on WORKSTATION-BUILD-MK) started failing TLS handshakes at approximately 07:15 UTC on 2025-12-20. The affected endpoint was internal.example.corp behind load balancer LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp, which made the internal web service unreachable over TLS and blocked normal API calls for the entire Arlington development group. Monitoring did not alert before the outage — the certificate-management-service renewal job configured by r.navarro had not fired its 30-day pre-expiry notification. Renewal response was delayed until developer Priya Chandrasekaran (emp ID EMP-40821) reported the issue and the expired certificate being served by the load balancer was confirmed by the infrastructure team.
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.example.corp expired at 2025-12-20T07:15Z, and the renewed certificate was not applied to the load balancer. The load balancer continued serving an expired certificate chain, while certificate expiry alerting and renewal verification did not provide advance warning.
resolution_steps: Obtained a renewed TLS certificate for internal.example.corp (new serial 6F:AA:12:5D:CC:08) from the internal Certificate Authority managed via certificate-management-service, verified by Rafael Navarro (r.navarro), before restoring service.

Uploaded the replacement server certificate (serial 6F:AA:12:5D:CC:08) and full intermediate chain (issuer CN=ExampleCorp Internal CA) to load balancer LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp so clients would receive a complete, valid chain.
Reloaded the load balancer LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp configuration and confirmed the new certificate binding was active on the HTTPS listener (port 443) for internal.example.corp traffic.

Validated the fix from the endpoint by running `openssl s_client -connect internal.example.corp:443` from WORKSTATION-BUILD-MK (10.22.17.94) and confirming the served certificate dates (notAfter=Dec 20 07:15:00 2026 GMT) and successful TLS handshakes without certificate warnings. Priya Chandrasekaran confirmed API access was restored.

Re-enabled and tested certificate expiry monitoring in certificate-management-service, restoring the 30-day pre-expiry notification to infra-certs@example.corp and r.navarro. Added renewal verification checks to confirm deployment to LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp completes successfully, so future expirations trigger escalation before service impact.
agent_questions: Thanks Priya. This is Rafael Navarro from Infrastructure. Please confirm the hostname is internal.example.corp and provide the certificate details currently served by the load balancer LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp, including any visible expiry date from an `openssl s_client -connect internal.example.corp:443` check. Also, can you confirm whether the issue is isolated to your workstation or if other team members (e.g., d.kim or j.whitfield) are also seeing the same warnings? I'm pulling up the certificate-management-service renewal logs now.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Users and internal service clients were trying to reach https://internal.example.corp, but beginning around 08:20 UTC on 2025-12-14 the endpoint started returning browser certificate warnings and TLS handshake failures. The issue was first reported by Priya Nair (priya.nair@example.corp) from the Austin office, who noticed ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID when accessing the portal from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN. Affected users across the internal developers and services group could not safely open the internal web service, and dependent API clients saw HTTPS failures across multiple zones (us-central-1a, us-central-1b, us-central-1c). The issue impacted the internal web service behind the load balancer (lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp) after the service certificate expired and the load balancer continued presenting an outdated certificate chain. Ticket escalated by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40821) from the infrastructure operations team.
observed_errors: 502 via load balancer when TLS negotiation fails
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.example.corp expired, and the load balancer continued serving a stale certificate chain. Certificate renewal alerting was not active, so the expiration was not detected and remediated before client TLS validation began failing.
resolution_steps: Issued a new TLS certificate for internal.example.corp (new serial 7B:22:AF:01:CC:D4:90:E3, valid until 2026-12-14) through the Certificate Authority, requested by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, E-40821), before restoring production traffic handling.

Installed the renewed certificate on the Internal Web Service application nodes in us-central-1a/1b/1c and verified via openssl s_client that the local service presented the expected certificate for the endpoint name internal.example.corp with the updated serial and validity dates.

Updated the Load Balancer lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp to use the renewed certificate and full intermediate chain (leaf + intermediate CA), then rolled the configuration across all LB nodes in us-central-1 to remove the stale chain. Configuration change executed by Jenna Whitfield (jwhitfield) from the network_team.

Validated end-to-end TLS negotiation from multiple zones (us-central-1a, 1b, 1c) and from client IPs including 10.42.17.88 (Priya Nair, Austin) and 10.42.22.105 (Tomás Reyes, API integrations). Confirmed browser warnings and API client handshake failures were no longer occurring. Service restored at approximately 11:15 UTC.

Restored certificate renewal alerting in the Certificate Management platform for internal.example.corp with a 30-day and 7-day pre-expiry notification threshold, subscribed to mdelgado@example.corp and infra-ops@example.corp, and added recurring certificate health checks so future expirations are detected before the renewal window closes.
agent_questions: Can you confirm whether users are seeing browser certificate warnings (e.g., ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) versus a generic application error, and whether API clients are failing during TLS handshake or after connection establishment? Also, could you verify whether the issue is isolated to a specific zone or affects all zones behind lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp? Please share any screenshots or client-side error output if available. — Marcus Delgado, Infrastructure Operations

title: Laptop running slowly after login
description: User Rachel Simmons (emp ID E-40821) reports that her managed Windows 10 corporate laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS) becomes very slow and briefly unresponsive immediately after sign-in. Task Manager showed sustained high CPU and disk activity, applications including Outlook and Chrome opened slowly, and the issue began after a recent endpoint policy push on 2026-02-02. The slowdown affected normal post-login work during the first several minutes of each session. User is based in the Charlotte office and contacted the service desk after the problem persisted for multiple days. Her username is rsimmons and the device IP is 10.42.17.88.
observed_errors: High disk I/O during initial login period
root_cause: A recently applied startup-related endpoint protection policy caused Microsoft Defender (msmpeng.exe) to trigger full-engine scans at user login. The resulting queued scan backlog drove sustained CPU and disk I/O utilization, which delayed application launches and degraded system responsiveness.
resolution_steps: Validated that Microsoft Defender full-engine scans were launching at login on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS (user rsimmons) and identified a backlog of 7 queued scans consuming up to 88% CPU and sustaining disk queue length of 4.2, accounting for most available CPU and disk resources.
Cleared the 7 pending endpoint protection scan backlog entries on the affected laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS to stop repeated scan execution during the login window.
Paused the immediate scheduled full-engine scan and adjusted the full scan schedule to run at 02:00 local time so it would not trigger at user sign-in for rsimmons' device.

Disabled non-essential startup items (OneDrive sync, Teams auto-launch helper, Cortana background task) and refreshed the StartupAppManagementPolicy via Endpoint Management console to reduce competing startup workload after login on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS.

Removed 6.3 GB of temporary files from C:\Users\rsimmons\AppData\Local\Temp and reclaimed local disk space (free space increased from 11.4 GB to 17.7 GB) to reduce disk contention and improve application launch performance.

Refreshed device policy on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS after the changes and confirmed post-login CPU behavior normalized to below 20% within 2 minutes. Outlook and Chrome opened within expected time. Notified Rachel Simmons at rsimmons@corplabs.com that the issue is resolved.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outage — resolved
description: Users in the Austin office were trying to access the Internal Web Service (https://internal-web.corplabs.com) and dependent internal API endpoints, but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and automated health checks failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the DevOps team at approximately 15:45 UTC on 2025-12-14. The service began presenting an expired or incomplete certificate chain after a renewal was performed at the internal Certificate Authority without fully updating the HAProxy load balancer configuration on LB-FRONT-01. This blocked normal HTTPS access for internal users across the Austin and Denver locations and caused the incident to reappear after the initial partial fix attempted by the on-call engineer.
root_cause: The TLS certificate was renewed at the Certificate Authority, but the full certificate chain was not deployed to the HAProxy load balancer serving the Internal Web Service. As a result, some clients continued to receive an expired or incomplete chain, and existing renewal monitoring did not detect the missing chain deployment step, allowing the outage to recur after the first remediation attempt.
resolution_steps: Renew the Internal Web Service TLS certificate (CN=internal-web.corplabs.com) with the internal Certificate Authority and retrieve the complete server certificate and intermediate certificate chain (DigiCert SHA2 Extended Validation Server CA). Renewal performed by rgarcia from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RG.

Upload and bind the full certificate chain (leaf + intermediate PEM bundle) to the HAProxy load balancer configuration on LB-FRONT-01 at /etc/haproxy/certs/internal-web.pem for the affected Internal Web Service virtual host (internal-web.corplabs.com) and dependent API endpoint (api.internal.corplabs.com). Deployment executed by James Whitfield (jwhitfield).

Restart or reload HAProxy worker processes on LB-FRONT-01 via 'systemctl reload haproxy' so the new certificate bundle is actively served on all frontend endpoints. Reload confirmed successful with no dropped connections at 16:52 UTC.

Validate the presented certificate, expiration (2026-12-14), SAN coverage (internal-web.corplabs.com, api.internal.corplabs.com), and full trust chain from internal client perspectives (tested from 10.28.51.19 by mchen and 10.28.44.73 by rgarcia) to confirm successful TLS handshakes with no warnings.

Re-enable and tighten Nagios certificate monitoring to alert on both certificate expiration risk (30-day and 14-day thresholds) and cases where renewal occurred but chain deployment on LB-FRONT-01 is incomplete. Added new check_ssl_chain post-renewal validation rule. Monitoring update performed by Lisa Novak (lnovak, phone ext 512-555-0147).

title: MFA prompt loop and SSO login rejections affecting Okta/Azure AD users
description: Multiple users were trying to sign in to Salesforce, G Suite, and Confluence through the Okta SSO portal (https://sso.meridiantech.com) backed by Azure AD, but after entering primary credentials they were repeatedly returned to MFA and then received SSO login rejected errors. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least six other members of the AllEmployees group in the Charlotte office. The issue began after a conditional access policy update pushed on 2026-04-06 and blocked access to SaaS applications for members of the AllEmployees group. Evidence showed the failure was not single-cause: some users recovered after MFA factor reset, while others still failed due to device time drift and conditional access scope mismatches.
observed_errors: MFA prompt loop detected in Okta logs
root_cause: Primary root cause was an overly strict group-based Azure AD conditional access location check introduced during a recent policy update, which caused repeated authentication denials during the Okta/Azure AD sign-in flow. A secondary contributing condition affected a subset of users whose authenticator devices had clock drift greater than five minutes, and a smaller subset had stale MFA enrollments that temporarily improved after factor reset.
resolution_steps: Reviewed affected user scope against the updated group-based conditional access policy (CA-LOC-2026-04) and identified the location-based rule as the common denial condition in Azure AD sign-in results. Users ranguyen, dkowalski, mbell, and pdeshmukh were confirmed as impacted within the AllEmployees group at the Charlotte office.

Modified the conditional access assignment for the AllEmployees group to remove the overly strict location check (CA-LOC-2026-04) that was incorrectly rejecting valid SSO sessions originating from Charlotte office IP ranges (10.42.18.0/24). Change was approved by security lead Tom Hargrove (thargrove).
Reset MFA enrollment for users whose existing factor state was stale or inconsistent — specifically ranguyen and dkowalski — so they could re-register a valid active Okta Verify factor.

Instructed affected users (mbell and pdeshmukh) to resync authenticator application time via Settings > Time Correction in the Okta Verify app, and correct device clock settings on endpoints showing more than five minutes of drift. Marcus Bell's device WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MB was confirmed resynced.

Validated post-change sign-ins through the Okta to Azure AD flow for all four affected users (ranguyen, dkowalski, mbell, pdeshmukh) and monitored authentication logs for 24 hours to confirm prompt loops and SSO rejections stopped across the affected application set (Salesforce, G Suite, Confluence). No further denials observed after 2026-04-08T01:45:00Z.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied for user to Engineering shared drive
description: I was trying to open the Engineering shared drive at \\corpshare\Engineering\Team Folder from a mapped drive (Z:) on my domain-joined Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES) while on the corporate LAN at the Denver office. My username is mreeves and my employee ID is ENG-40821.
