I reached out to my manager, Patricia Langford (plangford@corplabs.com), who confirmed the rest of the team had no issues.
root_cause: The user's Active Directory account was not a member of the Engineering_Shared_Access security group required for the share, and the Team Folder had broken NTFS inheritance with an explicit deny entry contributing to the access failure.
resolution_steps: Validated that the user mreeves (employee ID ENG-40821) was missing membership in the Engineering_Shared_Access Active Directory security group required for access to the Engineering shared drive.
Reviewed the share and NTFS permissions on \\corpshare\Engineering\Team Folder and identified broken inheritance with an explicit deny entry affecting access behavior for the mreeves account.
Added the user mreeves to the Engineering_Shared_Access group and restored NTFS permission inheritance on the Team Folder, removing the explicit deny condition. Change performed by agent dhuang.

Had the user log off and back on to refresh Kerberos and SMB access tokens on WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES (IP 10.22.47.118), then remapped the network drive to the current shared path \\corpshare\Engineering\Team Folder as drive Z:.
Verified the user Marcus Reeves (mreeves) could open the folder and confirmed read/write access to the Engineering share was restored. User confirmed via email at mreeves@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, please confirm whether you are opening \\corpshare\Engineering\Team Folder directly and whether coworkers in Engineering can still access it. Also let us know if the mapped drive is prompting for credentials or only showing an access denied message. Could you also confirm your workstation hostname and IP address so we can check connectivity logs? This is Agent Derek Huang following up on your ticket.

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve
description: Multiple internal users and monitoring systems reported intermittent DNS resolution failures for api.service.corp.local after an A-record change in the internal corp.local zone. The issue was initially flagged by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corp.local) from the internal services team and corroborated by automated health checks on host WORKSTATION-MDLG-PC. Clients attempting to reach the internal api.service endpoint from the Portland datacenter saw NXDOMAIN responses, stale name resolution to the previous IP (10.42.16.55), or occasional DNS lookup timeouts, preventing reliable access to the service by hostname. Impact was limited to internal service discovery and resolver behavior in the us-west-1 datacenter environment following the recent record update. Approximately 14 users across the infrastructure and platform engineering groups were affected.
observed_errors: resolver returned stale A record (old IP) for api.service.corp.local
DNS query timeouts reported by clients during intermittent periods
root_cause: Primary internal DNS resolver continued serving a stale cached response for api.service.corp.local after the A-record was updated in the internal zone, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and old-IP answers until cache was cleared and TTL behavior normalized.
resolution_steps: Queried the affected hostname api.service.corp.local against the internal resolver dns-resolver-01.corp.local from Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-MDLG-PC (10.42.8.103) and confirmed inconsistent responses including NXDOMAIN and the previous A record value 10.42.16.55.

Verified the corp.local zone data on the authoritative side (dns-auth-01.corp.local, zone serial 2026010602) contained the updated A record for api.service.corp.local pointing to 10.42.17.20 and reviewed the record TTL (originally 3600s).
Flushed the primary DNS resolver cache on dns-resolver-01.corp.local using rndc flush to remove the stale cached entry (10.42.16.55) being served to internal clients across the Portland datacenter.

Temporarily lowered the TTL for the affected A record from 3600s to 300s to reduce propagation delay and minimize reuse of stale cached data during validation period; change applied by Priya Nair (pnair).

Retested name resolution from monitoring host mon-agent-04 and multiple internal clients including WORKSTATION-MDLG-PC (mdelgado) and Raj Okonkwo's session (rokonkwo) to confirm api.service.corp.local consistently resolved to the updated IP address 10.42.17.20.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether api.service.corp.local is failing for all internal users or only specific hosts in the Portland datacenter, and whether clients are seeing NXDOMAIN or an old IP (10.42.16.55) after the recent DNS record update. Can you also verify from your workstation (WORKSTATION-MDLG-PC, IP 10.42.8.103) whether nslookup against the primary resolver at dns-resolver-01.corp.local returns the stale address or times out? — Priya Nair, Network Operations

title: Internal hostnames intermittently failing to resolve from DNS resolver
description: Internal users and monitoring in the Charlotte office intermittently failed to reach services by name under corp.local because the internal resolver bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) returned NXDOMAIN or a stale A record for service1.corp.local. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40291) from the internal-ops team after the deployment dashboard on his workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD could not connect to service1.corp.local. The authoritative internal DNS zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local already contained the correct current address (10.50.12.88), so applications depending on internal hostname resolution were intermittently unable to connect until resolver cache and configuration state were corrected.
observed_errors: cached old A record returned by resolver
root_cause: bind-resolver-01 was serving stale cached DNS data for corp.local due to an outdated DNS update policy reference and cache entries that were not invalidated after the authoritative record changed, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and old A record responses despite the authoritative zone being correct.
resolution_steps: Verified the authoritative corp.local zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local contained the correct A record (10.50.12.88) for service1.corp.local and corrected the record where needed so the source of truth matched the intended service IP.

Reviewed the resolver configuration on bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) and updated the outdated DNS update policy reference in /etc/bind/named.conf.options contributing to stale response behavior, as identified by Priya Nair.
Flushed the DNS cache on bind-resolver-01 via rndc flush and restarted the named service to remove stale NXDOMAIN and old A record entries (10.50.12.60) for service1.corp.local.

Queried service1.corp.local from the resolver and from affected internal hosts — including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (mdelgado, 10.20.41.77) and trivera's workstation (10.20.41.93) — to confirm the resolver now returned the same current address 10.50.12.88 as the authoritative zone.

Confirmed dependent service checks and Network Monitoring alerts cleared after cache refresh and configuration correction, with hostname resolution for service1.corp.local remaining stable across all queried clients in the Charlotte office.
agent_questions: We are comparing answers from bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) against the authoritative corp.local zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local to confirm whether the issue is with the source record or stale resolver data for service1.corp.local. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) reported that his workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD at 10.20.41.77 was receiving NXDOMAIN responses when querying the hostname. Network engineer Priya Nair is leading the investigation.

title: Software Center install blocked by Endpoint Protection — reopened then resolved
description: I was trying to install AcmeApp v4.2 from Software Center on my Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-MKT-RGARCIA), but the install was blocked with the message "blocked by Endpoint Protection." observed_errors: Installation blocked by Endpoint Protection policy
Software Center shows 'blocked by Endpoint Protection'

Validated deployment targeting and added user rgarcia's device WORKSTATION-MKT-RGARCIA to the App_Acme_Entitlements group to correct the missing software entitlement assignment for employee E-40291.

Forced an Intune device inventory and policy sync on WORKSTATION-MKT-RGARCIA (IP 10.47.83.112) to refresh stale device state and update the endpoint's assignment and protection evaluation. Post-sync last check-in updated to 2026-03-24T17:48:00Z.

Retried the Software Center deployment on WORKSTATION-MKT-RGARCIA after sync completion and confirmed AcmeApp v4.2 installed successfully on the affected device. User rgarcia (Rosa Garcia) verified the application launched without issues from the Portland office.
agent_questions: Hi Rosa, I reviewed the deployment targeting for AcmeApp v4.2 on your device WORKSTATION-MKT-RGARCIA (IP 10.47.83.112) and need to confirm whether Software Center still shows AcmeApp as blocked after a Company Portal sync. title: Laptop slow after login
description: My corporate Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, IP 10.28.44.117) becomes very slow immediately after login following a recent policy refresh pushed on 2026-01-30. Outlook, Chrome, and Teams take 30-60 seconds to open, CPU remains around 40-70% for several minutes, and the C: drive has very limited free disk space (~18 GB of 256 GB). The slowdown persists after reboot and is affecting my normal post-login work on the managed laptop. I need this resolved urgently as I have client presentations this week. — Marcus Reeves, Sales East, emp ID S-40281
observed_errors: High CPU from MsMpEng after login
root_cause: A recently refreshed startup policy triggered multiple resource-heavy login tasks while Microsoft Defender (MsMpEng) had an active scan backlog, and the endpoint had only about 8% free disk space. The combination caused sustained CPU and disk IO contention immediately after login, delaying application launches and overall responsiveness.

Refresh the device policy from Endpoint Management for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and roll back or adjust the GPO startup policy applied 2026-01-30 that introduced excessive post-login activity; confirm with Darren Cho (dcho) that the revised policy no longer triggers concurrent heavy startup tasks.

Clear the Microsoft Defender scan backlog (14 queued items since 2026-01-28) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR through centralized management and reschedule full or intensive scans for off-hours (after 20:00 EST) to reduce business-hour CPU impact for user mreeves.

Perform disk cleanup on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR to remove temporary files, Windows Update cache, and browser caches, reclaiming space so the C: drive returns to a healthier free-space threshold (target >15%) and reduces disk IO contention.

Validate after remediation that CPU utilization on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR drops to normal (<15%) within a few minutes of login for mreeves and that Outlook, Chrome, and Teams open within expected time (<10 seconds). Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com) to confirm resolution via ticket update or phone at 215-555-0194.

title: Laptop slow

CPU remains elevated around 80-95% with MsMpEng.exe consuming most resources, causing Microsoft Office apps (Outlook, Excel) and Edge to open very slowly or hang. Disabled 6 non-essential startup items (including OneDrive sync, Teams auto-start, and Adobe Updater) and removed 4.2 GB of temporary files from C:\Users\mreeves\AppData\Local\Temp to reduce additional startup load and improve login-time responsiveness.

Monitored WORKSTATION-DELL-MR for approximately 30 minutes after remediation and verified CPU normalized to 8-12% idle and affected applications (Outlook, Excel, Edge) opened within normal time (under 5 seconds each). title: Intermittent disconnects from Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Users in the Portland office (Building C, 3rd floor) reported that managed Windows 10 laptops could join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-5G) but were repeatedly dropped shortly after connecting, interrupting access to internal applications such as Salesforce and the corporate intranet. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (EMP-40291) around 19:15 UTC on 2026-05-11 and quickly confirmed by several other Sales team members on the same floor. Reports were concentrated to that single location and a narrow time window rather than all wireless users globally. Some users, including Derek Holloway, could reconnect briefly before being disconnected again within 2–5 minutes.
observed_errors: No IP address assigned after join
root_cause: Wireless access point or controller radio instability in the affected area caused repeated client deauthentication and session drops after otherwise successful Wi-Fi authentication.
resolution_steps: Escalate to the wireless infrastructure team (network engineer Raj Kapoor, rkapoor@corplabs.com) to remediate the unstable APs AP-PDX-3F-04 and AP-PDX-3F-06 or controller radio conditions affecting the Portland Building C 3rd floor.

Remove or restart the affected APs (AP-PDX-3F-04 and AP-PDX-3F-06) from service as needed and correct the underlying controller or RF issue on WLC-PDX-01.corp.internal causing repeated deauth events. Raj Kapoor disabled both APs and rebalanced 3rd-floor clients to adjacent healthy APs while scheduling hardware replacement.

Verify clients in the affected Portland 3rd-floor location can stay associated and maintain normal network access without repeated disconnects. Confirmed with Maria Chen (mchen), Derek Holloway (dholloway), and Priya Nair (pnair) that their laptops maintained stable Wi-Fi connectivity for over 30 minutes after the AP remediation, with no further deauth events observed in controller logs.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts during nightly sync
description: During the nightly DataSync App synchronization through the Integration Gateway, multiple API calls initiated by the ETL service account (svc-datasync-etl) to the downstream API exceeded the 30-second timeout window and some requests returned HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout. The overnight batch job (job ID: SYNC-BATCH-20251207-0200) could not complete successfully, causing delayed data availability for downstream consumers in us-east-1 on the EKS-hosted integration path. Reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40291) from the Richmond ETL Operations team. Immediate token rotation provided only intermittent improvement, while monitoring during the same job window showed elevated downstream service latency as the main blocker rather than an authentication failure. The integration pod running on host WORKSTATION-ETLNODE-MD logged repeated connection timeouts starting at approximately 02:05 UTC.
root_cause: downstream service latency during the nightly sync window caused requests to exceed the Integration Gateway timeout threshold
resolution_steps: Validated that the Integration Gateway token for svc-datasync-etl was not the primary fault domain after rotation produced only intermittent improvement and logs showed no token-expiry events. Confirmed with Priya Nair (pnair) that authentication was healthy across the gateway cluster.

Adjusted the nightly integration retry behavior to use exponential backoff (initial interval 5s, max 3 retries, backoff multiplier 2x) and aligned the temporary request timeout increase from 30s to 60s to better tolerate transient latency spikes during batch processing on job SYNC-BATCH configuration.

Correlated failed job batches (SYNC-BATCH-20251207-0200) with elevated downstream p95/p99 response times (38s/47.2s) and HTTP 504 timeout behavior during the same overnight window (02:00–04:30 UTC) to isolate the issue to downstream service performance. Analysis led by Tomás Herrera (therrera) using the Monitoring System latency dashboards.

Opened and tracked a priority escalation (ESC-DS-1207) with the downstream service team contact Kenji Watanabe (kwatanabe) for latency mitigation during the nightly processing window and requested targeted remediation and ETA. Marcus Delgado (E-40291) added as stakeholder on the escalation ticket.

Continued end-to-end monitoring of job completion, timeout frequency, and downstream latency metrics via the Monitoring System to confirm recovery and verify that nightly synchronization returned to expected processing windows. Alerts configured to notify m.delgado@corplabs.com and the ETL Operations channel if p99 latency exceeds 25s during the sync window.

title: account locked after password change
description: After a scheduled password change on 2025-11-19, I (emp ID E-20487) could still sign in from my desktop (WORKSTATION-MBP-RCHEN) but could not complete SSO authentication on my iOS mobile device (IPHONE-RCHEN-14). resolution_steps: Reviewed Active Directory lockout events on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal to confirm the failed authentication source was the user's corporate mobile device (IPHONE-RCHEN-14, IP 10.42.18.97) rather than the desktop session on WORKSTATION-MBP-RCHEN.
Unlocked the user's account (rchen) in Active Directory via the identity_team (Marcus Webb) after confirming the lockout was caused by repeated stale credential submissions from the mobile device.
Issued a new password reset token (RST-88501) through the Password Reset Portal and verified that the token was active and accepted for account rachel.chen@corplabs.com.
Guided the user to remove saved credentials and clear cached sign-in data on the mobile device (IPHONE-RCHEN-14) before retrying SSO authentication at https://sso.corplabs.com.
Had the user re-authenticate on mobile with the updated password and confirmed successful SSO sign-in on IPHONE-RCHEN-14 without new lockout events for account rchen.

Monitored lockout counters on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal for 30 minutes to verify that no device or service continued submitting invalid credentials for rchen; Priya Nair confirmed all clear at 01:25 UTC.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm whether the failed sign-ins are only on the phone (IPHONE-RCHEN-14) and whether the issue started immediately after the scheduled password change or after using the self-service reset at https://passwordreset.corplabs.com. title: High CPU and slow startup on Windows laptop
description: Marcus Delgado (EMP-40291) on a corporate Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) reported severe slowness immediately after login. Applications including Outlook, Edge, and Salesforce Desktop Connector took several minutes to open, CPU remained sustained at 85-95%, and the device fan ran continuously. root_cause: Sustained post-login performance degradation was caused by a Microsoft Defender scan backlog running during user logon together with multiple heavy startup applications enforced or enabled on the device, with low C: drive free space further increasing CPU and disk contention.

title: Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired causing TLS failures
description: Internal users and automation were trying to reach internal-api.company.local through the HAProxy load balancer (LB-HAPROXY-EAST-01), but browsers showed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and health checks began failing around 2025-12-15 09:12 UTC. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Denver office, who noticed that TLS connections to the internal API could not be established from his workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD. This impacted the internal-devs group and dependent CI/CD jobs until the expired certificate and chain on the load balancer were corrected. The ticket was escalated to infra-certs@techsphere.net for immediate remediation.
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal-api.company.local expired on 2025-12-15 and the renewed certificate chain had not been deployed to the HAProxy load balancer before expiration. Certificate monitoring and renewal alerting for this endpoint were missing or ineffective, allowing the service to continue presenting an expired certificate.
resolution_steps: Validated that the certificate presented for internal-api.company.local on the HAProxy TLS termination point (LB-HAPROXY-EAST-01) was expired and matched the reported browser and health-check failures seen by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) from 10.42.17.88 and Rachel Ito (rito) from 10.42.19.204.

Requested and issued a renewed TLS certificate for CN=internal-api.company.local from the internal Certificate Authority. Certificate request submitted by Priya Nambiar (pnambiar, EMP-55193) and approved through the standard CA workflow.

Updated the HAProxy load balancer (LB-HAPROXY-EAST-01) with the renewed server certificate, private key, and intermediate certificate chain for the affected listener serving internal-api.company.local.
Restarted or reloaded HAProxy TLS termination on LB-HAPROXY-EAST-01 so the new certificate bundle was actively presented to clients. Reload performed by pnambiar at 10:08 UTC.

Confirmed successful TLS handshakes and removal of certificate warnings from monitoring nodes and client access paths, including verification from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (10.42.17.88) and WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-RI (10.42.19.204) in the Denver and Portland offices respectively.

Re-enabled and tuned certificate expiration monitoring to alert the infrastructure team (infra-certs@techsphere.net) at least 30 days before expiry for this endpoint. Alert ownership assigned to Priya Nambiar (pnambiar) with escalation to the broader infrastructure group.
agent_questions: Can you confirm whether the expired certificate is being presented by the load balancer or the backend service, and share the certificate chain or CN seen at the endpoint? We've looped in infra-certs@techsphere.net and network engineer Priya Nambiar (username: pnambiar) to assist with diagnostics. Please also confirm the client IP and hostname you're connecting from.

title: Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway to downstream API
description: Scheduled integration jobs and live API calls from Integration Gateway v3.2 in us-east-1 began failing after about 03:10 UTC on 2025-12-11 with 504 Gateway Timeout responses and elevated downstream latency. The issue was first reported by integration admin rchandra (Rajesh Chandra, emp ID EMP-40821) from the Arlington office, who noticed that the nightly order-sync job and real-time inventory push to the downstream Fulfillment API were returning ERR_API_TIMEOUT. Retries were exhausted after the default 3-attempt cycle, delaying data synchronization across dependent systems and preventing normal API integration processing until the downstream performance issue was corrected. Alerts were firing on the Monitoring System dashboard for gateway node igw-east-node04 (10.42.18.77) and the issue was visible from the submitter's workstation WORKSTATION-RCHANDRA at 10.200.5.34.
root_cause: A downstream API database query became slow during the incident window, increasing response latency beyond the Integration Gateway timeout threshold and causing repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and retry exhaustion.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Integration Gateway logs on igw-east-node04 (10.42.18.77) and Monitoring System dashboards to confirm the failure pattern, showing 47 failed jobs with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and a sustained downstream latency spike (p99 peaking at 18.4 s) between approximately 03:10 and 03:30 UTC. Initial triage was performed by agent mtovar (Maria Tovar).

Validated that the issue was not caused by authentication failures by checking request behavior for service account svc-igw-fulfillment and confirming the symptom pattern was timeout-related (504/ERR_API_TIMEOUT) rather than token rejection (401/403). The bearer token was confirmed valid through 2026-03-15.

Escalated the incident to the downstream Fulfillment API team lead Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) with timing, latency, and 504 evidence from the Monitoring System so they could investigate backend performance during the affected window.

The downstream Fulfillment API team, led by Priya Nair, identified and remediated a slow database query (full table scan on order_items due to a missing index after a recent schema migration) on their PostgreSQL backend that was causing the response-time degradation and intermittent 504 errors. The fix was applied at approximately 03:28 UTC.

Updated the Integration Gateway per-request timeout from 10 seconds to 30 seconds on igw-east-node04 and adjusted retry/backoff settings (max retries increased from 3 to 5, exponential backoff base from 2 s to 4 s) to better tolerate short-lived latency spikes without immediately exhausting retries. Change was applied by rchandra per change request CR-20251211-088.

Monitored gateway and downstream metrics via the Monitoring System for 24 hours after the fix, confirmed latency returned to the ~1.2 s baseline, and verified scheduled jobs resumed without further timeout spikes. Final confirmation received from Rajesh Chandra (rchandra@corplabs.com) at the Arlington office on 2025-12-12.

title: Integration Gateway outbound API requests timing out across environments
description: Multiple application teams (including the Order Processing and Inventory Sync groups managed by Priya Venkatesh) were trying to complete scheduled data syncs through the Integration Gateway, but outbound calls to the third-party API (vendor endpoint: api.partnerlogistics.com) began timing out after peak traffic this morning. Monitoring dashboards on the us-east-1 cluster and gateway logs from node igw-pod-07.integration.corplabs.internal showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses, elevated downstream latency (upstream_latency_ms>2000), and TokenExpiredError events starting around 08:15 UTC. The issue was first reported by rchandra@corplabs.com and affected multiple environments (staging and production), blocking normal integration job completion until gateway authentication was restored. Ticket raised on behalf of the integration-team user group by Marcus Ellison (EMP-40821).
root_cause: An expired API token on the Integration Gateway caused authentication failures during outbound calls to the downstream third-party API. Repeated token refresh failures left the gateway using invalid credentials, which increased latency and resulted in 504 timeouts for scheduled integration jobs.
resolution_steps: Validated that outbound request failures aligned with token expiry on the svc-igw-sync service account and repeated token refresh errors in Integration Gateway logs (igw-pod-07.integration.corplabs.internal), with initial report from rchandra@corplabs.com.

Rotated the expired API token used by the Integration Gateway service account svc-igw-sync for downstream third-party API authentication via the API Service secrets vault; rotation performed by Marcus Ellison (EMP-40821).

Restarted all Integration Gateway pods in us-east-1 and cleared cached credentials so all gateway instances loaded the updated token for svc-igw-sync; verified pod health on the Monitoring System dashboard.

Verified successful token refresh behavior for svc-igw-sync and confirmed authenticated outbound API requests completed without timeout errors; Priya Venkatesh and David Kowalski (EMP-55934) confirmed their respective OrderSync-Prod and InventoryPull-Staging jobs resumed successfully.

Adjusted retry and backoff settings (max_retries=5, initial_backoff=500ms, backoff_multiplier=2) on the Integration Gateway to reduce integration job failures during future token refresh windows and monitored request latency on the Monitoring System until normal operation was restored; also scheduled a review of the API Service credential rotator to prevent silent refresh failures.

title: Outlook mailboxes not syncing (desktop and mobile) for multiple users
description: Multiple users across the Sales and Field Ops OUs reported that Outlook on Windows and Outlook on iOS stopped syncing after the weekend Microsoft 365 tenant maintenance window (Feb 7–8). Desktop clients for users including Rachel Moreno (rmoreno@corplabs.com), David Huang (dhuang), and at least five others showed a Disconnected state in the Outlook status bar. Mobile devices — primarily iPhones enrolled via MDM — stopped receiving new mail entirely. Mailbox folders and last-synced timestamps remained stale, blocking normal email and calendar updates for affected staff in the Denver and Austin offices. The issue was first flagged by Rachel Moreno (EMP-40821) on Monday morning and escalated after additional reports came in from Field Ops.
observed_errors: Sync error 0x80190194 observed in client logs
root_cause: Mailbox sync failures were caused by a combination of stale Outlook cached profiles/OST data on affected desktops and an outdated legacy-block rule in the MDM sync policy that interfered with mobile synchronization after the tenant maintenance window.
resolution_steps: Validated the issue scope across affected users — Rachel Moreno (rmoreno, EMP-40821), David Huang (dhuang, EMP-40955), Tina Nguyen (tnguyen, EMP-41102), Mark Salazar (msalazar, EMP-41230), and three additional Field Ops staff — and confirmed Outlook desktop clients were showing Disconnected while mobile mailboxes had stalled last-sync timestamps since approximately 2026-02-07T23:00Z.

Tested sync behavior with a clean Outlook profile on WORKSTATION-RM2041 (rmoreno), then rebuilt affected Outlook profiles and removed stale OST cache files on impacted Windows endpoints including WORKSTATION-RM2041 and WORKSTATION-DH1587 for all seven affected users.

Reviewed impacted mobile mailbox partnerships for rmoreno, dhuang, tnguyen, and msalazar, cleared stale mobile sync partnerships that had been inactive since the maintenance window, and re-established device synchronization for all affected users' iOS devices.

Updated the MDM sync policy to remove the outdated legacy-block rule (MDM-LB-0044) that was preventing compliant current iOS 14 clients from syncing correctly after maintenance. The rule had originally targeted decommissioned iOS 12 endpoints but was incorrectly matching current devices post-tenant update.

Forced a full mailbox resynchronization for all affected accounts and verified that desktop Outlook connectivity on WORKSTATION-RM2041, WORKSTATION-DH1587, and other endpoints, mobile mail delivery, and calendar/item updates resumed normally across both the Denver and Austin offices. Confirmation received from Rachel Moreno and David Huang that sync is fully operational.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether Outlook on Windows shows Disconnected or Trying to connect for the affected users, and whether mobile mail stopped updating for the same accounts (e.g., rmoreno, dhuang, tnguyen) after the weekend maintenance window. Also, can you verify whether the issue is limited to the Denver and Austin offices or if other locations are impacted?

title: Outlook desktop not syncing mailbox (profile mismatch)
description: I'm Marcus Reeves (employee ID EMP-40291) from the Columbus office. I was trying to use the Outlook desktop client on my workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (IP 10.42.18.77) running Windows 10, but the mailbox for mreeves@corplabs.com stopped updating this morning and Outlook showed a Disconnected state. New mail continued to arrive on the mobile client, indicating the Exchange Online mailbox itself remained available while the desktop client could not synchronize. The issue blocked normal desktop email access and was consistent with a local Outlook profile or OST cache problem rather than a service-side outage.
root_cause: Stale Outlook desktop profile with a profile token mismatch and corrupted local OST cache caused the client to disconnect from Exchange Online and stop synchronizing the mailbox.
resolution_steps: Confirmed Exchange Online service health and mailbox connectivity for mreeves@corplabs.com were normal to rule out a server-side outage before making client changes on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR.
Removed the existing Outlook profile for mreeves on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR after exporting and preserving the required mailbox configuration details and local signatures.

Deleted the affected local OST cache file at C:\Users\mreeves\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\mreeves@corplabs.com.ost associated with the stale Outlook profile to clear the sync corruption and checksum mismatch condition.
Created a new Outlook profile on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and re-added Marcus Reeves' Exchange Online account (mreeves@corplabs.com) so authentication and mailbox mapping could be rebuilt cleanly.
Allowed Outlook to complete a full mailbox resynchronization on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and verified the client returned to a connected state with current mailbox updates for mreeves@corplabs.com.

Advised Marcus Reeves to re-authenticate on mobile only if any residual sync artifacts appeared, though desktop synchronization on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR was confirmed restored. Contact Denise Cho at dcho@corplabs.com if issues recur.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, this is Denise Cho from the service desk. Please confirm whether Outlook on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR shows Disconnected or Working Offline, and whether new mail is still arriving on Outlook mobile or webmail at mreeves@corplabs.com so we can determine if this is client-only. Could you also confirm your current IP address so we can check network routing?

title: Print jobs stuck on PS-Print01
description: Multiple Finance users in the Charlotte office were trying to print to the shared HP-LaserJet queue (\\PS-Print01\HP-LJ-FIN-3F) on print server PS-Print01, but jobs remained stuck at 0% and the printer appeared offline. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least four other Finance team members. The problem began after a scheduled OEM printer driver update pushed on 2026-02-26 and blocked normal printing for the entire Finance group. Server-side spooler logs on PS-Print01 showed repeated OEM driver package load failures (error 0x80070057) during queue processing, and the Print Management Console flagged the queue as degraded.
observed_errors: Spooler: DriverLoadFailure - OEM driver package returned error 0x80070057
Print jobs stuck at 0% in HP-LaserJet queue
root_cause: Approved HP printer driver on PS-Print01 became corrupted or improperly registered after the recent OEM driver update, causing the spooler to fail loading the driver and leaving the HP-LaserJet queue stalled.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the HP-LaserJet queue (\\PS-Print01\HP-LJ-FIN-3F) and spooler error history on PS-Print01 to confirm 23 jobs were stalled due to OEM driver load failures (error 0x80070057) affecting Finance users including rnguyen, thadley, and mparker.

Removed the affected HP Universal Print Driver v7.2.1 driver association from the PS-Print01 driver store and reinstalled the approved HP driver package (v7.1.8) from the approved driver repository (\\filesvr-east\DriverRepo\HP) on PS-Print01.
Remapped the Finance HP-LaserJet shared queue (\\PS-Print01\HP-LJ-FIN-3F) to the reinstalled approved driver package v7.1.8, verifying correct driver binding in Print Management Console.

Cleared the 23 stuck print jobs from the queue and restarted the Print Spooler service on PS-Print01 to reload the corrected driver. Notified affected Finance users via email to resubmit their print jobs.

Submitted validation prints from two Finance endpoints — WORKSTATION-RN-PC04 (rnguyen) and WORKSTATION-TH-PC09 (thadley) — and monitored queue processing for 30 minutes to confirm jobs completed successfully without additional driver load errors. Confirmed with Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) that normal printing was restored for the Charlotte Finance team.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether all Finance users printing to the HP-LaserJet queue (\\PS-Print01\HP-LJ-FIN-3F) are seeing jobs remain at 0% or the printer showing offline. Can you also verify this started after the driver update pushed on 2026-02-26? If possible, please share the hostnames of any affected workstations so we can cross-check spooler client logs. You can reach me at d.kowalski@corplabs.com or ext. 4417.

title: Device marked Noncompliant in Intune
description: I (Marco Bellini, emp ID EMP-40821) with an iOS 15.7 device (hostname IPHONE-MBELLINI) in the Sales group at the Milan office was blocked from accessing Exchange Online because Conditional Access evaluated the device as Noncompliant in Intune. The device, connecting from IP 10.42.17.88, had not checked in for about 36 hours, and after a forced sync the check-in timestamp updated but the encryption compliance signal still showed as not reported, preventing email access. My account is mbellini@corplabs.com and I need email restored urgently for client meetings.
observed_errors: Conditional Access blocked sign-in to Exchange Online
root_cause: iOS device compliance remained noncompliant because the required encryption status signal was not being reported to Intune even after check-in, so Conditional Access continued to treat the device as noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Forced an Intune sync on device IPHONE-MBELLINI and confirmed the device resumed recent check-in with the management service (last sync updated to 2025-12-30T03:30Z).
Reviewed the failing compliance signal for user mbellini (EMP-40821) and verified the only blocking condition was encryption status remaining unreported on the iOS device.
Re-applied the encryption compliance requirement to IPHONE-MBELLINI and instructed Marco Bellini to enable device encryption, reboot the iPhone, and run a manual sync from Company Portal.
Triggered a manual compliance re-evaluation after the post-reboot sync so Intune could ingest the updated encryption state for device IPHONE-MBELLINI.

Applied a 24-hour Conditional Access exception (approved by Priya Nair) to restore critical Exchange Online access for mbellini@corplabs.com while the device completed remediation, then removed the exception after compliance was updated.
agent_questions: Hi Marco — we forced an Intune sync on device IPHONE-MBELLINI (serial registered to user mbellini) and the device is checking in again, but encryption still shows as not reported. Please confirm whether device encryption is enabled on the iPhone and whether you can open Company Portal to run a manual sync after a reboot. I've also looped in our endpoint lead, Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com), in case we need to escalate the compliance policy review.

title: VPN disconnects after Okta MFA approval — device certificate expired
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 11 laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MK) at the Frankfurt office while working remotely. My username is mkowalski and I authenticate via Okta MFA linked to mkowalski@corplabs.com. The Okta MFA approval succeeded, but the VPN tunnel disconnected immediately after authentication and internal applications (SharePoint and Jira) remained unreachable. The incident was reopened because the problem returned after an earlier certificate rotation performed on 2026-04-14, indicating the prior fix did not fully address device certificate and profile state on the endpoint. My manager, Petra Lindgren, asked me to raise this again as it is blocking sprint work.
root_cause: Expired device certificate on the endpoint, combined with a stale GlobalProtect profile, caused the VPN tunnel to terminate after successful Okta SAML authentication.
resolution_steps: Validated that the endpoint device certificate (CN=mkowalski, issued to WORKSTATION-DELL-MK) had expired on 2026-04-19 and renewed the certificate via Device Certificate Service on the affected laptop.
Refreshed the GlobalProtect VPN profile on WORKSTATION-DELL-MK to remove stale profile data and the outdated certificate thumbprint tied to the expired certificate state from the April 14 rotation.

Had user mkowalski re-authenticate through Okta MFA (mkowalski@corplabs.com) and establish a new GlobalProtect session using the renewed device certificate; tunnel connected successfully from client IP 10.47.83.112.

Confirmed restored access to internal resources, including SharePoint and Jira, after the VPN tunnel remained connected for 15+ minutes under observation. Notified manager Petra Lindgren that the issue was resolved.

Documented the certificate expiry timeline (issued 2025-04-19, expired 2026-04-19, renewed 2026-04-21) and advised follow-up monitoring for 48 hours to verify the issue does not recur. Set a calendar reminder for mkowalski and desktop support to proactively renew the certificate 30 days before next expiry.
agent_questions: Hi Marek, thanks for reaching out. Could you please confirm whether Okta MFA completes successfully before the VPN disconnects? Also, after the drop, are internal apps like SharePoint or Jira still unreachable? I can see your device WORKSTATION-DELL-MK (IP 10.47.83.112) attempted a tunnel connection at 18:08 UTC — I'd like to correlate that with your experience. Please also confirm your employee ID (I have E-40291 on file) so I can pull the correct device enrollment record.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive for user
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive at \\fileserver01\\Finance from my corp-joined Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-PC-MR) using mapped drive F:. My username is mreeves and I'm based in the Portland office. The share returned an Access Denied error while other network shares like \\fileserver01\\General remained accessible, preventing me from opening Finance department files needed for end-of-quarter reconciliation work. Investigation showed the issue was limited to my Finance share entitlement rather than a general file server or workstation connectivity problem. My manager, Dana Whitfield (dwhitfield@corplabs.com), can confirm I should have access to this share.
root_cause: User account was not a member of the AD security group that grants access to the Finance shared drive, so the user's current SMB/Kerberos access token did not include the required entitlement.
resolution_steps: Verified the Finance share and NTFS permissions on \\fileserver01\\Finance to confirm access is granted through the approved AD security group (FIN_Share_Access) rather than direct user permissions. Share-level and NTFS ACLs were consistent and correctly referenced the group.

Confirmed the affected user account mreeves (employee ID EMP-20418, Marcus Reeves) was missing from the FIN_Share_Access Active Directory security group that controls access to the Finance shared drive. The omission appears to have occurred during the user's recent departmental transfer from Operations to Finance.

Added the user account mreeves to the FIN_Share_Access security group in Active Directory in line with the approved access model for the share, with approval confirmed by Finance manager Dana Whitfield (dwhitfield@corplabs.com, ext. 503-555-0147).
Had user Marcus Reeves refresh their security token by signing out and back in on WORKSTATION-PC-MR, with guidance that 'klist purge' could also be used to clear stale Kerberos tickets if needed.

Retested access to \\fileserver01\\Finance from WORKSTATION-PC-MR (IP 10.42.18.97) after group membership update and token refresh and confirmed user mreeves could open the Finance folder and read/write files successfully.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm whether only the Finance mapped drive (F:) is failing and whether you can still open other shared folders such as \\fileserver01\\General or \\fileserver01\\HR from your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MR. Also, can you confirm your client IP address so I can cross-reference the file server access logs?

title: Device noncompliant for BitLocker — Intune shows conflicting state
description: User Marcus Delgado (EMP-40291) from the Arlington sales office brought his company-managed Windows 11 Enterprise endpoint (hostname: WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) forward for encryption compliance review because Company Portal listed disk encryption as noncompliant. During troubleshooting, local checks on the device (IP 10.42.17.88) showed BitLocker prerequisites were in place and Intune policy delivery looked normal, but support still could not locate an escrowed recovery key for the machine in Microsoft Endpoint Manager. The lack of escrowed key visibility prevented standard recovery support and kept the device from satisfying corporate compliance requirements under the Sales user group encryption baseline.
observed_errors: Device marked noncompliant for encryption in Device Compliance
root_cause: BitLocker recovery key escrow failed or never completed for the existing protector even though TPM readiness and Intune policy delivery were functioning normally.
resolution_steps: Verified that WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (user: Marcus Delgado, mdelgado, EMP-40291) was receiving the correct disk encryption policy (Sales-Encryption-Baseline) via Intune and confirmed the existing TPM 2.0-backed protector was healthy before changing any key material.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD using 'manage-bde -protectors -delete C: -type RecoveryPassword' followed by 'Add-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C: -RecoveryPasswordProtector', then initiated a fresh backup of the new key to the Azure AD management service via 'BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector'.

Ran a follow-up Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD, confirmed the new recovery key was visible to support in the Endpoint Manager recovery key blade, and validated that Device Compliance Service updated the encryption compliance status to compliant for mdelgado's device. Notified Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, this is Priya Nair from desktop support. Could you please confirm whether BitLocker shows any protectors locally on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD by running 'manage-bde -protectors -get C:' in an elevated prompt? Also, can you check whether a recovery key is visible in Endpoint Manager for this laptop under your device listing (mdelgado@corplabs.com)?

title: Account locked after repeated failed sign-ins
description: I was trying to sign in to the corporate SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com from my iPhone (iOS 15) but my account (username: mreeves) became locked after repeated failed authentication attempts. I had changed my password last week but the phone still had the old one saved in the Mail and Outlook apps. I started a password reset through the Password Reset Portal, but by the time I got to the final step the reset token had already expired, so I could not regain access to SSO and was completely blocked from normal account access. This is urgent because I'm traveling to the Charlotte office for a client meeting tomorrow morning and need access to my email and CRM. My employee ID is E-50274 if that helps look me up.
root_cause: The Active Directory lockout policy was triggered by repeated failed sign-in attempts from the user's mobile device, which was continuing to use cached stale credentials. Recovery was delayed because the password reset token issued through the Password Reset Portal expired before the reset could be completed and propagated.
resolution_steps: Reviewed account lockout events (Event ID 4740) on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal for account CN=mreeves,OU=Sales,DC=corplabs,DC=internal and confirmed the repeated failed authentication source was the user's mobile device IPHONE-MREEVES (IP 10.42.88.17) using cached stale credentials in Outlook and iOS Mail.
Unlocked the Active Directory account for mreeves via the AD Admin Console on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and reset the lockout counters (badPwdCount) to restore eligibility for authentication.

Guided Marcus Reeves through clearing saved credentials and active session tokens on device IPHONE-MREEVES — removed stored passwords from Outlook and iOS Mail — and instructed the user to reauthenticate with current credentials only.

Issued a new password reset token (RST-88455) through the Password Reset Portal to marcus.reeves@corplabs.com and had the user complete the password reset within the 30-minute token window before expiry.

Verified successful sign-in by mreeves to the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com at 19:01 UTC after the reset, and monitored AD authentication logs on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal for an additional 30 minutes to confirm no further failed attempts and that the lockout condition did not recur.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, we can see that the account mreeves is currently locked in Active Directory. Our logs show multiple failed sign-in attempts originating from IP 10.42.88.17. Are you still signed in on your mobile device or any mail apps (Outlook, native iOS Mail), and does the Password Reset Portal at https://passwordreset.corplabs.com show any specific message when you try to reset? Also, can you confirm the device hostname — does it show as IPHONE-MREEVES in your settings?

title: Windows laptop very slow
description: My managed Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DL-RMORALES, asset tag DL-EME-04821) is consistently sluggish after sign-in, with Outlook, Chrome, and File Explorer taking noticeably longer than normal to open during the first several minutes of use. The slowdown affects general desktop responsiveness and delays normal work, but I cannot identify a specific application failure. Initial symptoms point to endpoint performance degradation during the post-login period on this device. My employee ID is E50274 — please use that for any asset lookups. I'm based out of the Frankfurt office in the Sales group.
observed_errors: CPU usage > 90% within 2 minutes of login
Applications taking 20-60 seconds to become responsive
root_cause: Critically low available disk space combined with excessive temporary file accumulation caused ongoing disk contention and degraded laptop performance after login.
resolution_steps: Removed temporary files from C:\Users\rmorales\AppData\Local\Temp (24.3 GB) and C:\Windows\Temp (14.1 GB), cleared local browser caches for Chrome and Edge, and reclaimed 41.6 GB on the system drive of WORKSTATION-DL-RMORALES.

Reviewed large local file consumers using WinDirStat and identified an additional 8.2 GB of obsolete Sales Tool export CSVs under C:\Users\rmorales\Documents\Exports; moved these to the user's OneDrive archive and deleted nonessential local copies to restore healthy free space (now 52.1 GB available on C:\).

Validated after logoff and logon by user Ricardo Morales that disk response improved (disk queue length dropped to 0.3 avg) and common applications — Outlook, Chrome, File Explorer, and Internal Sales Tool — opened within normal timeframes (Outlook in 7 seconds, Chrome in 4 seconds). Confirmed with Ricardo via rmorales@corplabs.com that performance was back to normal.
agent_questions: Hi Ricardo, can you confirm whether the slowness on WORKSTATION-DL-RMORALES starts immediately after sign-in and whether Task Manager shows high CPU or disk usage while Outlook and Chrome are opening? Also, could you verify your current IP so I can pull the latest endpoint telemetry? I see your device last checked in from 10.47.83.112.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: Managed Windows 10 Enterprise device WORKSTATION-SALES-MR (asset tag sales-laptop-23), assigned to Marcus Reilly (emp ID E-40291) in the Dallas office, Azure AD joined and enrolled in Intune, was reported noncompliant for disk encryption. User mreilly@corplabs.com contacted the helpdesk after noticing BitLocker was not enabled under Windows Settings > Device Encryption. Intune compliance dashboard for device IP 10.47.83.112 showed encryption status 'Not Enabled', and support could not locate a recovery key in Azure AD for this device. This blocked confirmation of endpoint encryption compliance for the Sales I team and required validation of TPM readiness, policy delivery, and recovery key escrow before the device could be cleared.
root_cause: BitLocker could not complete initial enablement because the TPM protector was not initialized during provisioning. After the protector issue was corrected, recovery key escrow to Azure AD did not occur automatically, leaving Intune and Azure AD in an inconsistent state until the recovery key was manually re-escrowed and verified.
resolution_steps: Confirmed TPM availability on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR via tpm.msc (status: 'The TPM is ready for use') and initialized the TPM-based BitLocker protector using 'manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm' so the system could start encryption on the C: volume.

Reapplied the assigned BitLocker policy (profile 'Corp-Encrypt-Win10-Standard') from Intune and forced a device sync via Company Portal on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR to ensure the endpoint received the active encryption configuration. Sync completed at 2026-01-25T01:02:00Z.

Started BitLocker encryption on C: and verified from the local device status ('manage-bde -status C:') that protection had moved from 'Not Enabled' to 'Encryption In Progress' and then 'Protection On — Fully Encrypted' on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR.

Forced recovery key backup via 'BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C:' after encryption policy application when the key was not initially visible in Azure AD for mreilly's device. Event log confirmed successful escrow.

title: Laptop slow after login
description: I have a Windows 10 Pro laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag EP-4821) assigned to Marcus Reilly (mreilly, employee ID EMP-90274) in the Columbus office becoming extremely slow within minutes after sign-in for the past two days. root_cause: Queued full-system scans in the endpoint protection client after a recent update created a scan backlog that ran immediately after login and drove sustained CPU utilization above normal levels.
resolution_steps: Reviewed post-login resource utilization on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (mreilly, IP 10.42.18.107) via Endpoint Management telemetry and confirmed EPProtectionService.exe was responsible for the sustained CPU spike exceeding 90%.

Cleared the queued Endpoint Protection Client full-system scan backlog (3 pending scans since 2026-02-04) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR to stop repeated immediate scan execution after sign-in for user mreilly.
Paused and rescheduled immediate full-system scans to run daily at 12:30 AM EST during off-peak hours to prevent heavy startup impact on Marcus Reilly's user session during business hours.

Removed approximately 8 GB of temporary files from C:\Windows\Temp and C:\Users\mreilly\AppData\Local\Temp to improve available disk space from ~6 GB to ~14 GB and reduce additional performance overhead.

Disabled one unnecessary startup application (OneDrive auto-sync at login) and refreshed the device policy via the Endpoint Management console so the updated scan schedule and endpoint settings were applied to WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR.

Validated that CPU usage on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR returned to normal (~8% idle) and application launch responsiveness improved to under 2 seconds after remediation. Confirmed with Marcus Reilly via email at mreilly@corplabs.com that performance was satisfactory.

title: Print jobs stuck on PRN-Q2

Restarted the Print Spooler service on PRN-SRV01 to reload the corrected driver package and restore normal queue processing for all mapped Accounting workstations.

title: Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired, causing TLS warnings and service unavailability
description: Users were trying to access the internal web service at internal.websvc.corp starting around 2025-12-18 08:12 UTC, but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and TLS connections failed. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) from the Chicago office, who noticed the certificate warning while accessing the HR onboarding portal served behind internal.websvc.corp. Internal health checks running from health-checker on the Kubernetes cluster in us-east-1 also began returning 502 errors on TLS backend probes, preventing normal access to the service from inside the network. The load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.infra.corp) was still presenting a stale certificate bundle with an incomplete chain, which compounded the issue until both the certificate and chain were corrected.
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.websvc.corp expired, and the load balancer continued serving the old certificate with an incomplete chain. In parallel, the certificate expiry monitoring threshold was misconfigured, so the renewal alert did not fire before expiration.
resolution_steps: Issued a replacement TLS certificate for internal.websvc.corp (new serial 5B:8D:4E:A2, valid 2025-12-18 to 2026-12-17) from the internal Certificate Authority (CorpCA) before returning the service to production traffic. Certificate request submitted by Samantha Liu (sliu@corp.internal).

Deployed the renewed certificate to the internal web service endpoint running on the Kubernetes cluster in us-east-1 and verified that the presented certificate matched the service hostname internal.websvc.corp with correct SAN entries. Deployment confirmed by ops engineer Samantha Liu.

Updated the full certificate chain on lb-prod-east-01.infra.corp, replacing the stale certificate bundle (dated 2024-12-15) with the new chain including the renewed CorpCA Intermediate G2, and reloaded the TLS process so the new chain was actively served to all client connections.

Corrected the CertWatch certificate expiry monitoring threshold from 0 days to the org-standard 30 days for internal.websvc.corp and validated that renewal and expiry alerts would trigger with sufficient lead time before future expirations. Alert recipient list updated to include rpatel@corp.internal and sliu@corp.internal.

Confirmed successful TLS handshakes and healthy probe results from multiple internal regions (us-east-1, us-west-2), including verification from monitoring nodes at 10.22.50.88 and 10.34.12.55, then updated the certificate rotation runbook to include chain validation during deployment and mandatory post-deployment verification from at least two network zones.
agent_questions: Hi team — can you run an openssl s_client check against internal.websvc.corp:443 and share the certificate details including expiration date and SAN entries? Also, please confirm whether lb-prod-east-01.infra.corp has the updated full chain deployed, and check with Raj Patel (rpatel@corp.internal) on the infrastructure monitoring side whether any certificate expiry alerts fired before the outage window. We need to understand if the CertWatch alerting threshold was set correctly.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts during nightly sync — expired token and stale
description: Nightly DataSync jobs initiated by the Application Support team to the ThirdParty API (partner endpoint: api.thirdparty.io/v2/sync) began failing at approximately 02:00 UTC during the scheduled sync window on 2025-12-11, with repeated Integration Gateway timeouts and HTTP 504 responses logged against the production gateway cluster igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal. The downstream data synchronization was delayed by over four hours, reducing data availability for morning reporting in the Dallas office. Initial triage by Marcus Ellison (emp ID: E-40821) tied the failures to token validation errors on the Integration Gateway while processing high-volume sync traffic in the AKS-hosted production environment (namespace: datasync-prod). The issue was reported by Priya Venkatesh via the Application Support queue after automated Monitoring System alerts fired on her dashboard.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway was configured with a deprecated authentication policy that referenced expired client credentials. During nightly sync load, token validation failed, causing authenticated requests to stall and return repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses until the token and policy were corrected.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token used by the Integration Gateway service account datasync-svc-prod, issued new client credentials via the corporate credential vault, and validated successful token issuance against igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal. Rotation performed by Raj Anand (ranand@corpsync.com).

Deployed the replacement gateway authentication policy 'IGW-Auth-Policy-v2' to the datasync-prod namespace and removed the deprecated 'IGW-Auth-Policy-v1' policy reference that pointed to expired credentials. Change approved by Marcus Ellison under CHG-88214.

Cleared stale authentication state on the gateway pod igw-datasync-7b4f9 and verified the updated policy 'IGW-Auth-Policy-v2' was active across all replicas in the affected AKS deployment (datasync-prod namespace, 3 replicas confirmed).

Validated retry and backoff behavior for the nightly DataSync job — adjusted exponential backoff from 5s/10s/20s to 10s/30s/60s with jitter to reduce burst retries during transient authentication failures, and confirmed configuration via the Integration Gateway admin console.

Confirmed successful end-to-end sync execution in the nightly window (02:00–02:47 UTC on 2025-12-12) with zero 504 errors, and updated Monitoring System alerting rules to trigger on token validation failures within 5 minutes and to warn 7 days before credential expiration for datasync-svc-prod. Alert recipients updated to include pvenkatesh@corpsync.com and mellison@corpsync.com.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether the nightly failures are limited to the Integration Gateway path (specifically the igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal cluster) and whether any recent auth policy or credential changes were made before the 504 spikes started around 02:00 UTC. Also, can you verify whether the service account datasync-svc-prod was recently modified in the credential vault? We want to rule out any upstream changes before diving deeper. — Marcus Ellison

title: Outlook not syncing on mobile and desktop

Removed and re-added the mreeves@caboratech.com mailbox on the iPhone's Outlook Mobile app to refresh the sync partnership and force a new authenticated connection to Exchange Online, clearing the stale mobile sync state.

Rebuilt the Outlook desktop profile on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR under the mreeves Windows account to replace the stale client configuration that was presenting intermittent 'Disconnected' status, allowing a fresh OST cache and autodiscover negotiation.

Reopened Outlook on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and confirmed the mreeves@caboratech.com mailbox reconnected and resumed normal folder synchronization on both desktop and mobile after profile recreation and mobile account refresh. title: API timeouts causing nightly sync failures

The Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal) showed increased API latency and authentication failures logged under service account svc-reporting-sync, which blocked scheduled sync jobs and delayed downstream reporting data availability for the Reporting Team managed by Priya Nambiar. title: Expired TLS certificate causing internal web service TLS failures and browser warnings
description: Users and internal monitoring were trying to reach the internal web service at internal.example.corp, but beginning around 2025-12-22T08:12Z the site presented an expired TLS certificate. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Austin office, who noticed browser warnings when accessing the portal. Browsers showed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and backend integrations failed TLS handshakes through the F5 load balancer (vip-prod-f5-01.infra.example.corp), blocking normal access to the service for all internal employees until the renewed certificate and full chain were deployed correctly. Ticket submitted on behalf of the affected user group by jgarcia@example.corp.
platform: On-prem F5 Load Balancer and internal web VM pool
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.example.corp expired because the renewed certificate was not installed on the load balancer, and the presented certificate chain was incomplete due to a missing intermediate.
resolution_steps: Validated the renewed certificate from the Certificate Authority portal, including subject CN=internal.example.corp / SAN: internal.example.corp, DNS:internal.example.corp, validity period 2025-12-15 through 2026-12-15, and required intermediate chain files (DigiCert SHA2 Secure Server CA). Validation performed by Robert Niles (rniles).

Installed the renewed server certificate and full intermediate chain on the F5 load balancer (vip-prod-f5-01.infra.example.corp) SSL profile clientssl-internal-web that terminates TLS for the internal web service VM pool. Deployment executed by rniles from management IP 10.42.1.5.

Reloaded and applied the updated load balancer configuration via tmsh so clients received the new certificate chain instead of the expired certificate. Configuration change logged and confirmed by Robert Niles at 2025-12-22T16:15Z.

Verified successful TLS negotiation from client and service perspectives by confirming the endpoint no longer returned NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and backend handshake failures stopped. title: Print jobs stuck on PrintServer1 — driver unavailable
description: Engineering users at the Frankfurt office were trying to print to shared printer queue PRT-ENG-03 through PrintServer1, but submitted jobs remained stuck in the queue and the printer appeared offline. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Reinhardt (emp ID E-20481) who noticed his 47-page technical drawing batch had not printed after 20 minutes. Print processing on the Windows Server 2019 print server was blocked because the server reported the HP printer driver as unavailable during job handling, preventing Engineering from completing normal printing tasks. At least six users on the 3rd-floor Engineering wing were affected.
root_cause: A corrupt and outdated HP printer driver package on PrintServer1, combined with a stale queue-to-driver mapping for PRT-ENG-03, caused the Windows Print Spooler to fail driver validation and reject driver loading, leaving jobs stuck in the queue.
resolution_steps: Validated that PRT-ENG-03 on PrintServer1 (10.40.12.5) was bound to an older HP driver package (v4.2.1) and confirmed driver load failures in the server event logs, affecting users mreinhardt, losman, and tfrey in the Frankfurt Engineering group.

Removed the failed/corrupt driver package v4.2.1 from the PrintServer1 driver store and reinstalled the approved HP Universal driver v6 on PrintServer1, verifying the new package CRC matched the approved baseline.

Cleared all 14 stuck jobs from the PRT-ENG-03 queue to remove spool files created while the driver was failing to load, and notified affected users (mreinhardt, losman, tfrey) to resubmit their print jobs.
Restarted the Print Spooler service on PrintServer1 so the refreshed driver package and queue bindings were reinitialized cleanly; confirmed spooler status returned to Running with no error events.

Remapped PRT-ENG-03 to the reinstalled approved HP Universal driver v6 package and submitted test prints from WORKSTATION-MR-ENG (10.40.15.88) and WORKSTATION-LO-ENG to confirm successful queue processing. Tobias Frey confirmed his resubmitted jobs printed normally.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts to downstream service
description: Monitoring detected intermittent 504 and timeout responses from the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal) when proxying requests to the downstream Order Fulfillment API service in EKS us-east-1. Caller application sync jobs submitted by the backend-integration-team — specifically jobs triggered by user dmorales (EMP-40821) — were delayed and sometimes failed because downstream calls exceeded the gateway's 30-second timeout window and triggered retry storms. A gateway pod restart on igw-prod-east-pod-3 did not resolve the issue, and no recent timeout-related deployment change was identified. The alert was initially raised by Priya Nair via the #api-incidents Slack channel. Missing initial context included token expiry state and whether the downstream service was slow or rate limiting during the failure window.
observed_errors: Integration job marked failed due to API timeout
root_cause: Downstream API latency intermittently exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, and the gateway retry behavior amplified the impact into retry storms. Token expiry was not confirmed as the cause, and available evidence points more strongly to downstream response slowness with possible transient throttling pressure rather than an authentication failure.
resolution_steps: Validated that no recent gateway deployment introduced the failures by reviewing the CI/CD pipeline history for igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal (last deploy: 2025-12-08T14:12Z, unrelated config change). Reviewed failing request patterns showing 504s and upstream timeouts clustered around slow downstream Order Fulfillment API responses rather than immediate authentication rejection.

Confirmed the integration token path (client_id: svc-orderfulfillment-prod) required verification but did not show evidence of a broad auth failure pattern in the gateway logs, so token rotation was not performed to avoid introducing an unnecessary credential change during the incident. Daniel Morales (EMP-40821) was asked to schedule a post-incident token rotation as a precaution.

Applied a gateway mitigation on igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal by increasing the downstream request timeout from 30s to 60s for affected order-sync-batch traffic and updating retry behavior to use bounded exponential backoff (base 2s, max 3 retries, jitter enabled) to stop retry storms from compounding downstream slowness.

Captured failing request traces (trace-8a4f21, trace-8a4f34, trace-8a4f47) from the Monitoring System and correlated them with downstream response timing to isolate the bottleneck to the downstream Order Fulfillment API latency window (p99 at 45–55s) rather than the gateway pod itself.

Escalated the latency evidence and trace samples to the downstream service owner Rachel Chen (rchen@corplabs.com) on the Seattle platform team for remediation while keeping the gateway mitigation in place to stabilize sync job completion for the Austin fulfillment queue.

Monitored post-change behavior via the Monitoring System dashboard and verified timeout volume dropped from ~120/min to <5/min and order-sync-batch processing stabilized after the timeout and retry configuration adjustments. Confirmed with Daniel Morales that sync jobs completed successfully by 20:15 UTC.
agent_questions: Hi Daniel — please confirm whether the current downstream API token (client_id: svc-orderfulfillment-prod) is still within its validity window and whether the downstream Order Fulfillment service reported any latency or throttling during the period when 504 timeouts began around 19:00 UTC on 2025-12-10. You can check token issuance via the Integration Gateway admin console at https://igw-admin.corplabs.internal. Also, can you verify from the Monitoring System dashboard whether host WORKSTATION-DMORALES was the primary caller origin?

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: A corporate Surface Pro 7 laptop assigned to Marcus Delgado (employee ID EMP-40291) showed "Encryption not enabled" in Intune. The device, hostname WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD, was marked noncompliant for BitLocker, and no recovery key was visible in Azure AD. The issue affected BitLocker enforcement on a Windows 10 21H2 Azure AD joined endpoint used by the Sales team in the Dallas office and blocked the device from meeting corporate encryption compliance requirements. The user reported the issue after receiving a compliance notification at mdelgado@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: Intune shows 'Encryption not enabled' for device
Recovery keys not found in Azure AD for device
BitLocker failed to start due to TPM protector not initialized
root_cause: The device TPM protector had not been initialized, which prevented BitLocker from starting and completing encryption. In addition, an earlier recovery key escrow attempt failed during enrollment, leaving no recovery key stored in Azure AD for support and compliance validation.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM status on the affected device WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD (mdelgado, EMP-40291) using `Get-Tpm` and initialized the TPM protector via `Initialize-Tpm` so BitLocker could create a valid hardware-backed protector.
Enabled BitLocker encryption locally on the endpoint WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD after TPM readiness was confirmed, using `Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector -EncryptionMethod XtsAes256`.

Forced an Intune device sync from Company Portal on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD and re-applied the assigned BitLocker encryption policy "Corp-BitLocker-Enforce" so the device could receive current compliance settings.

Rotated and generated a current recovery key using `manage-bde -protectors -add C: -RecoveryPassword` and escrowed it to Azure AD via `BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C:`, then verified that the key was visible for WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD under mdelgado's device objects.

Confirmed the device encryption state on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD (C: volume 100% encrypted, XTS-AES 256) and monitored Intune and Device Compliance Service until the endpoint reported compliant for BitLocker. Notified Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Internal users and automated health checks were trying to reach the service-catalog endpoint (https://service-catalog.corplabs.internal) over HTTPS, but beginning around 2025-12-18T08:12Z the service presented an expired certificate and browser trust warnings. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) from the Arlington office, who noticed the certificate warning while accessing the catalog from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC. Clients saw TLS validation failures, including browser certificate warnings and failed handshake checks from multiple internal IPs including 10.22.4.87, which blocked normal access to the internal web service until the certificate and chain were corrected on the load balancer and service endpoint.
observed_errors: curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
root_cause: The end-entity TLS certificate for the Internal Web Service expired, and the renewed certificate chain from the internal Certificate Authority was not deployed to the Load Balancer, which continued presenting the old chain. Certificate expiry monitoring was also misconfigured, so the expected pre-expiration alert did not fire and the renewal gap was not caught before service impact.
resolution_steps: Issued a renewed end-entity TLS certificate (new serial 7D:A1:EE:09:CC:58) from the internal Certificate Authority for the affected internal web service endpoint service-catalog.corplabs.internal, with a validity period through 2026-12-18. Renewal performed by rkapoor.

Deployed the renewed server certificate and full certificate chain to load balancer LB-EAST-01 and the Internal Web Service backend at service-catalog.corplabs.internal so both presentation points were aligned. Deployment verified by d.nguyen@corplabs.com.
Restarted the TLS listener process on load balancer LB-EAST-01 to ensure the new certificate and chain were actively served to clients. Reload completed at 2025-12-18T08:02Z and confirmed by rkapoor.

Corrected the certificate-expiry monitoring rule MON-CERT-047 by updating the SAN scope filter to include *.corplabs.internal, and verified alerting for approaching expiration (30/14/7-day thresholds) and renewal failure conditions. Change reviewed by tmorales.

Validated successful TLS handshakes from client and service perspectives using browser access from WORKSTATION-PC-MC (Maria Chen, 10.22.4.87) and curl from 10.22.8.10, then confirmed internal health checks returned to OK without certificate warnings. James Whitfield in Raleigh also confirmed normal access restored.
agent_questions: We are seeing TLS failures on the service-catalog endpoint (https://service-catalog.corplabs.internal). Can you confirm whether users are receiving browser certificate warnings and whether automation is failing with certificate-expired or handshake errors? I've asked rkapoor from the infrastructure team to pull the current certificate details from the load balancer. Please reach out to me at d.nguyen@corplabs.com if you have additional details.

title: Outlook desktop mailboxes not syncing (resolved by profile rebuild)
description: Multiple users in the Corporate Sales group at the Charlotte office on corporate Windows 10 laptops were trying to use Outlook Desktop to read current mail, but the client showed a 'Disconnected' state and recent mailbox updates were missing after the weekend patch cycle (Feb 7–8). Exchange Online remained available through Outlook on the web (OWA) and Outlook Mobile, which limited the issue to desktop Outlook profiles and blocked normal email review and update activity for the affected group. Initial reports came from Rachel Nguyen (rng4521@corplabs.com, EMP-40291) and at least four other sales team members. Ticket was raised by desktop support lead Marcus Whitfield.
observed_errors: Sync stalled with local data inconsistency
root_cause: Corrupted or stale Outlook desktop profiles caused local OST inconsistencies after the weekend patch cycle, leaving affected clients stuck in a disconnected state even though Exchange Online was healthy.
resolution_steps: Validated that Exchange Online service health and mailbox connectivity were normal via the EXO admin center and Test-OutlookConnectivity for mailboxes rng4521, dkowalski, and pmehta, confirming the issue was isolated to Outlook Desktop clients in the Charlotte office.

Tested affected users with Outlook connection state and profile health checks on WORKSTATION-RNGUYEN (10.42.18.77), WORKSTATION-DKOWALSKI (10.42.18.83), and WORKSTATION-PMEHTA (10.42.18.90), which indicated local profile and OST inconsistency (checksum mismatch, sync stalls) rather than a server-side outage.

Rebuilt the affected Outlook profiles on all impacted Windows laptops — Marcus Whitfield coordinated with each user to remove the corrupted profile via Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles, then recreated the local OST cache for each mailbox (rng4521@corplabs.com, dkowalski@corplabs.com, pmehta@corplabs.com).

Launched Outlook on each workstation and allowed full mailbox re-synchronization against Exchange Online, then verified current email, folder updates, calendar sync, and send/receive behavior were restored. Rachel Nguyen and David Kowalski confirmed normal operation; Priya Mehta confirmed after a brief re-download of her 800 MB mailbox.

Applied a Mobile Device Management conditional access policy to the Corporate Sales Users group in the Charlotte office to auto-reset corrupted Outlook profiles at next login if the same OST inconsistency condition reappears, preventing recurrence after future patch cycles.
