title: Laptop slow after login
description: User Marcus Delgado (emp ID: E-40291) reported his corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) becoming very slow immediately after login, with CPU rising above 90% within minutes and Outlook and Chrome taking roughly 20-40 seconds to open. Marcus is based in the Charlotte office and connects from IP 10.42.17.88. The problem persisted after a reboot and was affecting normal productivity right after sign-in. Initial review also showed low free disk space and endpoint protection scans queued during the login period, with a recent startup policy change (GPO update pushed 2026-01-28) contributing additional startup load.
observed_errors: CPU usage >90% within 2 minutes of login
root_cause: A recently applied startup policy introduced multiple unnecessary resource-heavy startup applications, while endpoint protection had a backlog of queued scans and the device had less than 10% free disk space. Together these conditions caused sustained high CPU usage after login and delayed application launches.
resolution_steps: Disabled nonessential startup applications (CRM sync agent, analytics telemetry collector, and 4 other policy-pushed items) on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD for user mdelgado and refreshed device policy via gpupdate /force so the same unnecessary startup items were not immediately re-applied by the 2026-01-28 GPO.

Reviewed endpoint protection activity on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD, cleared the backlog of 14 queued full scans, and changed full scan scheduling to off-hours (daily at 02:00 EST) to prevent heavy login-time CPU contention for Marcus Delgado's device.

Removed temporary files from C:\Users\mdelgado\AppData\Local\Temp and C:\Windows\Temp, cleared the Windows Update cache, and reclaimed approximately 19 GB of disk space to restore healthier free capacity (~28 GB) and reduce startup-time disk pressure on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD.

Validated post-change performance after login on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD and confirmed CPU utilization dropped below 20% (steady-state ~12%) and common applications (Outlook, Chrome, Word) opened normally within 3-5 seconds. Marcus Delgado confirmed the improvement at 20:05 UTC.

Prepared a follow-up policy update (change request CR-2026-0198) to reduce noncritical startup applications on similarly managed Sales group devices in the Charlotte office to prevent recurrence, and notified endpoint management lead Priya Okonkwo (pokonkwo@corplabs.com) for review.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, can you confirm whether the slowdown starts right after sign-in on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD and whether it continues even after a reboot? I also want to know if Outlook and Chrome are the main apps affected, or if Microsoft Word and other applications are similarly delayed. title: BitLocker not enabling and recovery key not escrowed for Intune-managed device
description: An Intune-managed Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MK) assigned to Marco Kessler (emp ID EMP-40291) in the Zurich office was marked noncompliant for disk encryption in the Device Compliance Service. BitLocker showed as not enabled on the C: drive, and the recovery key was not visible in the portal. The device, with IP 10.42.17.83, had been restarted and manually synced via Company Portal, but neither compliance status nor escrow status changed—blocking the device from meeting the Endpoint Disk Encryption policy requirements for the Field Sales user group.
observed_errors: No BitLocker protectors found on device
Recovery key escrow attempt failed (MDM escrow response failure)
root_cause: BitLocker could not start and escrow a recovery key because no BitLocker protector was configured on the device; the TPM protector had not been initialized despite the encryption policy being assigned.
resolution_steps: Verified that the Endpoint Disk Encryption policy ('FS-Encryption-Win10') was assigned to LAPTOP-SALES-MK (user mkessler, EMP-40291) in Intune and that the device was checking in without policy assignment errors; last successful sync was 2026-01-19T09:12Z from IP 10.42.17.83.
Confirmed locally on LAPTOP-SALES-MK that BitLocker was not enabled by running manage-bde -status C:, which returned 'Fully Decrypted' and no BitLocker protectors present on the OS volume.

Initialized the TPM protector on the endpoint using 'manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm' so BitLocker could create a valid protector set; command completed successfully with TPM 2.0 chip in ready state.

Started BitLocker encryption after protector creation using 'manage-bde -on C:' and verified that protection was active on the system volume; encryption reached 100% and protection status showed 'On'.
Forced an Intune device sync on LAPTOP-SALES-MK via Company Portal to trigger updated encryption compliance reporting and recovery key escrow to the Device Compliance Service.

Confirmed that the recovery key (ID BEK-7A3F) successfully appeared in the Device Compliance Service portal under mkessler's device record and that the device encryption state reported as 'Compliant' in Intune. Notified Marco Kessler (mkessler@corplabs.com) and manager Petra Lindgren that the laptop is now fully encrypted and compliant.

title: Intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal host 'app-db.internal' from one client subnet
description: Users on client subnet 10.20.30.0/24 (primarily the finance team in the Columbus office) were trying to resolve the internal database host app-db.internal, but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN while the same name resolved successfully from other subnets. The issue was originally reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@corplabs.com, emp ID FIN-40821) who noticed her application dashboard could not reach the internal database dependency by hostname in corp-datacenter-1. No recent DNS record change was logged, and Maria did not have access to internal DNS zone data or resolver configuration, so resolver path and forwarding behavior required verification by the network team.
root_cause: Subnet-specific DNS resolution was caused by an affected resolver path for clients on 10.20.30.0/24 that had incorrect or stale conditional forwarding/cache data for the internal zone. This caused that resolver to return NXDOMAIN for app-db.internal while other resolver paths continued to return the correct internal record.
resolution_steps: Identify the resolver serving clients on 10.20.30.0/24 — confirmed as dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal (10.20.30.2) — and compare its response for app-db.internal against a known-good internal resolver (dns-res-core-01.corplabs.internal, 10.50.1.10). NXDOMAIN was returned only by dns-res-east-02.

Review the resolver's conditional forwarder or zone forwarding configuration for the .internal domain on dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal and correct the forwarding target/path — the forwarder was pointing to a decommissioned upstream server — so requests are sent to the proper authoritative internal DNS servers (dns-auth-01.corplabs.internal / dns-auth-02.corplabs.internal).
Flush the DNS cache on the affected resolver dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal after the forwarding correction to remove cached NXDOMAIN responses and stale lookup data for app-db.internal.

Re-test name resolution for app-db.internal from the affected subnet (Maria Gonzalez's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG at 10.20.30.47) and from a known-good subnet (Raj Patel on 10.40.10.0/24) to confirm both return the same internal answer (A 10.60.5.22).

Document the resolver-specific DNS correction (forwarding target update on dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal, performed by Kevin Osei) and configure Network Monitoring alerts to detect recurrence of subnet-specific NXDOMAIN responses on the .internal zone, particularly for the Columbus office subnets.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm the DNS resolver IP used by a client on 10.20.30.0/24 (you can check with 'nslookup' or 'ipconfig /all' on your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG). Also, can you run 'dig app-db.internal' and let us know whether it returns NXDOMAIN consistently from that subnet? For comparison, I've verified the same lookup succeeds from the management VLAN via resolver 10.50.1.10. — Agent: Darren Whitfield

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts impacting data sync
description: Users reported failed scheduled integration jobs and delayed data synchronization for the API Integration used by the Order Processing App. During the past hour, the Integration Gateway in Kubernetes (us-east-1) showed a spike in HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses along with intermittent 401 Unauthorized errors, preventing normal authenticated API calls and delaying downstream data updates. The issue was initially flagged by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Austin office, who noticed that order sync jobs for client account OP-4417 were stalling. Additional reports came in from Priya Nair (emp ID: E-20587) confirming the same behavior from the Portland office.
root_cause: Expired API token used by the Integration Gateway caused token refresh failures and intermittent 401 Unauthorized responses, which cascaded into repeated gateway retries and HTTP 504 timeouts for integration jobs.
resolution_steps: Validated the gateway and downstream API logs to confirm token refresh failures and authentication errors consistent with an expired integration token. Rachel Ito (rito) reviewed logs on the us-east-1 Integration Gateway pods and the API Service audit trail for service account svc-orderproc, confirming over 340 failed refresh attempts between 03:22 and 04:49 UTC.

Rotated the expired API token used by the Integration Gateway and updated the active secret so new authenticated requests could be established successfully. The new token was generated for svc-orderproc and stored in the Kubernetes secret integration-gateway-token in the orderproc namespace.

Restarted gateway pods to ensure the new token was loaded and stale authenticated sessions or connection pools were cleared. All three gateway replica pods in us-east-1 were rolling-restarted, completing by 04:48 UTC.

Adjusted Integration Gateway retry and backoff settings to better tolerate short downstream latency without cascading into prolonged timeout conditions. Specifically, the max retry count was reduced from 10 to 5 and exponential backoff ceiling was set to 8 seconds, as recommended by Rachel Ito.

Implemented or updated the automated token rotation policy and monitoring coverage to alert before token expiry and to detect renewed 401 or 504 patterns early. A scheduled CronJob was added to rotate the svc-orderproc token every 60 days, and a Monitoring System alert rule was configured to fire when 401 error rate exceeds 5% over a 5-minute window, with notifications routed to mdelgado@corplabs.com and the Application Support channel.

Monitored request success rate, error counts, and integration job completion for approximately one hour and confirmed traffic returned to baseline. Rachel Ito and Marcus Delgado verified via the Monitoring System dashboard that all Order Processing App sync jobs completed without errors through 05:50 UTC.

Retried the deployment from Software Center and verified the application became visible to the standard user mreeves and installed successfully on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR; Marcus Reeves confirmed functionality via email at mreeves@corplabs.com.

title: Reopened: Device cannot access Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple users in the London office were trying to reconnect managed laptops and BYOD devices to Corporate Wi-Fi after a recent wireless certificate renewal. The issue was initially reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and confirmed by several colleagues on the 4th floor. Devices failed 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication and showed messages such as "EAP-TLS certificate expired," "Supplicant: certificate verification failed," or "No network access after joining." Rachel's laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) at IP 10.42.16.88 was among the first to fail. The issue began after the certificate was renewed on the primary controller (WLC-LON-PRIMARY), where some endpoints temporarily recovered, but additional devices failed the next morning due to incomplete certificate propagation to secondary nodes (WLC-LON-SEC02, WLC-LON-SEC03) and stale local Wi-Fi profiles, blocking normal network access for the affected user group.
root_cause: The renewed EAP-TLS certificate chain was not fully propagated across all wireless controller cluster nodes after the initial renewal, so some authentication paths still presented or validated against the expired certificate state. Affected endpoints also retained stale or corrupt Corporate Wi-Fi profiles, causing continued certificate validation failures even after the primary controller was updated.
resolution_steps: Validated the renewed wireless certificate chain on the primary controller WLC-LON-PRIMARY and confirmed the correct server certificate (CN=wifi.corplabs.com, issued 2026-04-26) and trust chain were present for EAP-TLS authentication. Verification performed by Carlos Mendes (c.mendes).

Pushed the renewed certificate and related trust chain to all secondary wireless controller nodes (WLC-LON-SEC02, WLC-LON-SEC03) and verified cluster-wide certificate consistency after service synchronization completed at 06:28 UTC on 2026-04-27.

Reviewed Cisco ISE (ise-lon-01.corplabs.internal) and controller authentication logs to confirm failed sessions for r.nguyen, d.marsh, and p.kapoor were tied to expired-certificate presentation or validation mismatch on nodes that had not fully updated prior to the sync.

Removed stale or corrupt Corporate Wi-Fi profiles from affected Windows and macOS endpoints — including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (Rachel Nguyen), WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-DM (David Marsh), and WORKSTATION-IPAD-PK (Priya Kapoor) — then re-enrolled devices to the CorpWiFi SSID so the supplicant could rebuild the 802.1X configuration against the current certificate chain.

Used the temporary NAC allowance only during the propagation window (approx. 05:50–06:35 UTC), then verified successful EAP-TLS handshakes for all three affected users and restored normal access enforcement after all controller nodes and test clients authenticated successfully. Final confirmation provided by Carlos Mendes and desktop support lead Amir Hussain (a.hussain, EMP-33190).
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether your device (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) still shows "EAP-TLS certificate expired" after forgetting and rejoining the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID, and whether other nearby users such as David Marsh or Priya Kapoor are seeing the same behavior this morning. You can reach me at x4417 or email netsupport@corplabs.com if you need immediate assistance.

title: PrintServer01 - Finance printer queue blocked by corrupted driver
description: Finance users were trying to print to the shared Finance printer (HP LaserJet Enterprise M609dn) through PrintServer01, but jobs remained stuck in PRINTER_QUEUE_FINANCE and the printer appeared offline on their workstations. The issue was first reported by Maria Delgado (EMP-40821) at approximately 05:00 UTC after the scheduled morning driver rollout (v3.1.47 push). root_cause: A corrupted printer driver deployed during the recent driver rollout on PrintServer01 caused the Print Spooler to report the queue driver as unavailable, which blocked PRINTER_QUEUE_FINANCE and left jobs stuck without reaching the device.

Installed the approved signed printer driver package (v3.1.46-stable) for the Finance printer queue (HP LaserJet Enterprise M609dn) from the approved driver repository on PrintServer01.
Remapped PRINTER_QUEUE_FINANCE to the newly installed approved driver package (v3.1.46-stable) and verified the queue mapping was active and the driver signature validated correctly.
Cleared all 14 stuck print jobs from PRINTER_QUEUE_FINANCE (submitted by mdelgado, kpark, and other Finance users) and restarted the Print Spooler service on PrintServer01.

Validated successful test printing from Finance workstations after the driver reinstall and queue recovery — confirmed output from WORKSTATION-FIN-MD (Maria Delgado, 10.22.14.87) and WORKSTATION-FIN-KP (Kevin Park, 10.22.14.92). Finance printing fully operational; notified users via email at mdelgado@corplabs.com and kpark@corplabs.com.

title: Users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple users in the Sales and Marketing departments at the Charlotte office were trying to sign in to the SSO Portal through Okta to reach downstream SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Workday, and Confluence. After successful primary authentication, they were repeatedly returned to the MFA challenge screen instead of reaching the application landing page. The issue was first reported by Rachel Simmons (rsimmons, emp ID EMP-40821) and began after a scheduled directory synchronization earlier in the day, blocking affected users from accessing business applications needed for normal work.
observed_errors: Repeated MFA challenge without successful authentication
SAML assertion rejected (Okta logs show mismatch in factor id)
Users stuck on MFA screen for >5 minutes
root_cause: Stale MFA enrollment records for a subset of users after a recent directory synchronization caused Okta factor identifiers to no longer match current enrollment state, resulting in repeated MFA challenges and SAML assertion rejection loops.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Okta authentication logs and isolated impacted accounts — rsimmons (EMP-40821), dnguyen (EMP-40955), and kpatel (EMP-41003) — showing repeated MFA challenges and SAML assertion rejections tied to mismatched factor identifiers.
Reset MFA enrollments for the affected users (rsimmons, dnguyen, kpatel, and 4 additional Sales/Marketing accounts in Charlotte) so stale factor records were removed from the identity provider.
Forced fresh MFA re-enrollment through the Okta end-user portal and validated that new active factor records were created successfully for all impacted users, starting with rsimmons.
Corrected the directory synchronization attribute mapping so Okta enrollment identifiers were preserved during sync processing; change reviewed by Marcus Webb (mwebb@corplabs.com).

Retested SSO sign-in for affected users — Rachel Simmons confirmed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS and David Nguyen confirmed from WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-DN — that they could complete MFA once and access downstream SaaS applications without returning to the challenge screen.

Monitored post-change authentication activity for two hours across all Charlotte Sales and Marketing accounts to verify the loop did not recur; agent Lauren Morris confirmed closure at 2026-04-09T01:15Z.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether the MFA prompt reappears after you approve the factor and whether this is happening across multiple apps in the SSO Portal or only one application. Also, can you let us know if other team members such as David Nguyen or Karen Patel are experiencing the same behavior? You can reach me at lmorris@corplabs.com if you need to follow up offline.

observed_errors: Print Spooler: driver load failed - checksum mismatch

Rebind PrinterQueue-Finance and any other affected queues on PrintServer01 to the reinstalled approved driver to eliminate stale queue-to-driver mappings left by the failed SCCM push on 2026-03-01. Verified by Natalie Cho (ncho).
Restart the Windows Print Spooler service on PrintServer01 and clear residual stuck jobs (14 pending) from the queue so the server loads the repaired driver package cleanly.

Submit a controlled test print through PrinterQueue-Finance from workstation WORKSTATION-FIN-RD (rdominguez) and verify jobs leave the queue normally without recurring driver load or checksum mismatch errors in the spooler logs. Confirmed successful test print at 01:48 UTC on 2026-03-02.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Internal users and dependent health checks were trying to reach service.example.internal over HTTPS, but beginning at 2025-12-21 09:12 UTC the endpoint started failing TLS negotiation. Multiple users in the Denver office reported that browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings when accessing the portal. Load balancer LB-PROD-INT-02 health checks reported TLS errors against the backend pool, making the Internal Web Service unavailable over secure access. The issue was initially reported by Rachel Nguyen (emp ID E-40821) via the infrastructure channel. Investigation by the network team showed the load balancer was still presenting an expired certificate (CN=service.example.internal, issued by CorpLabs Internal CA) and old intermediate chain after the renewal window passed. Affected clients included workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (IP 10.42.17.88) used by Rachel during initial triage.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failure: certificate expired (Not After 2025-12-21)
root_cause: The load balancer continued presenting a TLS certificate that expired on 2025-12-21 because the expected CA renewal process did not complete and the renewed certificate chain was not deployed to the load balancer configuration.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the presented certificate for service.example.internal had passed its Not After date (2025-12-21T00:00:00Z, serial 4A:7C:3E:91:BB:02) and Derek Castillo (dcastillo) requested a renewed certificate from the CorpLabs Internal Certificate Authority via the internal CA portal, specifying a 1-year validity and matching SAN entries.

Uploaded the renewed server certificate (new serial 7B:11:FA:C0:29:5D) and full certificate chain to load balancer LB-PROD-INT-02 at /etc/lb/certs/service-example-chain.pem and updated the HTTPS listener configuration to reference the new chain file.

Reloaded the load balancer LB-PROD-INT-02 configuration via the management CLI so the HTTPS endpoint on service.example.internal:443 began presenting the renewed certificate chain to clients immediately without dropping existing non-TLS connections.

Validated successful TLS handshakes from internal client WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (10.42.17.88, Rachel Nguyen) and the internal-health-check probe path, confirming the service endpoint name matched the deployed certificate SAN and no further NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings were observed. Marco Pellegrini also confirmed his workflow completed successfully.

Restored certificate monitoring by re-enabling the cert-expiry-30d alerting rule and added verification for renewal job failure conditions so future certificate expiry and missed renewals alert to infra-alerts@corplabs.com at 30, 14, and 7 days before service impact. Derek Castillo confirmed test alerts were received at dcastillo@corplabs.com and the infrastructure channel.

title: Internal hostname resolution failing
description: The inventory-service running on internal app hosts (including APPHOST-LNX-04 and APPHOST-LNX-05 in the Austin datacenter) could not connect to db01.corp.local because internal DNS resolution was failing. Affected hosts returned NXDOMAIN for the hostname and some hosts saw intermittent DNS timeouts, blocking database connectivity for the service in corp-datacenter-1. The issue was initially reported by DevOps engineer Priya Nambiar (pnambiar, emp ID DVP-2294) who noticed inventory-service health checks failing at approximately 15:50 UTC. Investigation focused on the internal DNS zone and resolver cache path for the corporate .local namespace.
observed_errors: DNS lookup timeout from some app hosts
root_cause: Internal DNS was serving stale data because db01.corp.local had an out-of-sync A record in the internal zone and stale negative cache entries on the DNS resolver tier, causing NXDOMAIN responses and intermittent lookup failures from app hosts.
resolution_steps: Validated the authoritative internal DNS zone entry for db01.corp.local and corrected the A record from the stale address 10.40.5.20 to the current database server IP address 10.40.5.35, as confirmed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) from the network infrastructure team.

Flushed stale resolver cache entries, including negative cache data, on dns-cache01 and dns-cache02 using 'rndc flush' so cached NXDOMAIN responses for db01.corp.local were removed from both resolver nodes.
Restarted the resolver service on dns-cache01 via systemctl to ensure the updated zone data and refreshed cache state were being served consistently to all downstream app hosts in corp-datacenter-1.

Re-ran hostname resolution tests for db01.corp.local from the affected app host path (APPHOST-LNX-04 at 10.40.12.87 and APPHOST-LNX-05 at 10.40.12.88) and confirmed the expected address 10.40.5.35 was returned without timeout on both hosts.

Verified dependent service recovery by confirming inventory-service could resolve the database hostname db01.corp.local and establish connections successfully, and that Network Monitoring checks for internal DNS lookups returned healthy. Notified Priya Nambiar (pnambiar@corplabs.com, ext. 4718) that the issue was resolved.

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed
description: A managed Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, asset tag ENG-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID E-20487) in the Portland office was reported as noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. The device, with IP 10.42.17.93, could not meet endpoint compliance requirements because BitLocker was not enabled locally and no recovery key was visible in Azure AD/Intune for the user mreeves. Local checks via manage-bde showed the TPM protector was not initialized, which prevented BitLocker from starting, and later MDM sync attempts intermittently failed to escrow the generated recovery key, causing compliance status to lag and temporarily toggle between noncompliant and pending.
observed_errors: Intune key escrow failed: intermittent timeout on key escrow API
Device compliance: encryption not enabled (portal flag)
root_cause: BitLocker could not start because the device TPM protector was not initialized, and recovery key escrow to Intune/Azure AD was intermittently failing during MDM sync, delaying compliant status after local remediation.
resolution_steps: Confirmed TPM was present on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR but no usable BitLocker TPM protector had been initialized — Get-Tpm showed TPMReady: False. Ran Initialize-Tpm to prepare the TPM module, then added a TPM protector locally via manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm so the device could support BitLocker protectors.

title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service causing TLS outage
description: Internal users and automated integrations were trying to reach the internal web service at internal.example.corp, but browsers showed certificate warnings and dependent health checks failed TLS validation. The outage was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Portland office, noting that multiple teams including DevOps and QA were unable to access the service. The outage affected the load-balanced service endpoint because the load balancer (LB-PROD-01.corplabs.internal) continued serving an expired certificate chain after the service certificate expired on 2025-12-21, blocking normal internal application access until the certificate and chain were refreshed. Automated monitoring from host WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC at 10.42.17.88 also flagged the TLS failure.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failed: certificate has expired
Health check failed: TLS validation error
root_cause: The TLS outage was caused by expiration of the certificate for internal.example.corp, combined with the load balancer continuing to present the outdated certificate chain and missing certificate renewal monitoring that failed to alert before expiry.
resolution_steps: Requested and issued a renewed TLS certificate for internal.example.corp from the internal Certificate Authority, with the renewal request submitted by Raj Patel (rpatel, E-30187) and approved by the Portland infrastructure team lead Sandra Liu (sliu@corplabs.com).

Uploaded the renewed server certificate and complete intermediate chain to the load balancer certificate store on LB-PROD-01.corplabs.internal and updated the TLS termination binding for the affected virtual service, verified by rpatel from the Portland datacenter console.

Restarted or reloaded the load balancer TLS termination process so the new certificate chain was actively served to clients, confirmed via service reload on LB-PROD-01.corplabs.internal at 11:42 UTC by Raj Patel.

Validated from multiple internal networks that the endpoint presented the correct hostname, current expiry date, and complete trusted certificate chain without TLS validation errors — verification performed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (10.42.17.88) in Portland and WORKSTATION-DESK-KO (10.42.18.55) in Denver by Maria Chen and Kevin Oduya respectively.

Restored certificate expiry monitoring and renewal alerting, then documented the renewal ownership and cadence in the infrastructure support process to prevent recurrence. Monitoring rule for internal.example.corp was re-enabled in the cert-monitor dashboard and assigned to rpatel with a 60-day pre-expiry alert threshold; Sandra Liu (sliu) confirmed the updated process documentation.

Can you also verify if the issue is reported from specific client machines? title: Users unable to join Corporate Wi‑Fi - authentication failures
description: Multiple Sales users in the Dallas office were trying to connect managed Windows, macOS, and iOS devices to the corporate SSID 'CorpWiFi' but were unable to complete network access starting around 07:45 CDT this morning. The issue was first reported by regional sales manager Karen Whitfield (EMP-40821) who noticed her MacBook Pro and iPhone both failed 802.1X authentication during join. Other affected users — including jmorales, bthornton, and lli — experienced similar symptoms: devices either failed EAP-TLS authentication outright or connected briefly and were immediately disconnected with no usable network access. The issue affected corporate Wi-Fi access needed for normal business connectivity across the 4th-floor Sales wing. Wireless Controller (WLC-DAL-01.corp.net) and RADIUS logs on ISE-PROD-02.corp.net showed EAP-TLS failures tied to an expired certificate in the wireless authentication chain.
observed_errors: Client denied network access after join
root_cause: The TLS certificate used in the corporate wireless 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication chain had expired on the RADIUS/Wireless Controller path, causing certificate validation failure and rejection of client authentication requests. A subset of legacy devices also retained stale or outdated Wi-Fi profiles after certificate replacement, requiring profile re-enrollment.
resolution_steps: Generated and signed a replacement TLS intermediate certificate (CN=CorpWiFi-ISE-Intermediate, valid through 2028-04-27) for the wireless authentication service using the internal PKI, and validated the full issuing chain before deployment. Work performed by network engineer Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-51209).

Installed the renewed intermediate certificate on the RADIUS server (ISE-PROD-02.corp.net) and updated the Wireless Controller (WLC-DAL-01.corp.net) trust chain, confirming the correct certificate and private key binding for EAP-TLS authentication. Verified chain validity using openssl s_client against the ISE node.

Restarted the ISE authentication service on ISE-PROD-02.corp.net and cleared stale RADIUS and wireless client sessions on WLC-DAL-01.corp.net so new 802.1X attempts would use the updated certificate path. Session flush completed at 09:32 CDT.

Retested affected client connections for kwhitfield (WORKSTATION-MBP-KW), jmorales (10.22.48.117), and other impacted Sales users — confirmed successful EAP-TLS handshakes and normal network access on CorpWiFi for the majority of impacted devices. Karen Whitfield confirmed full connectivity restored on both her MacBook and iPhone.

Directed users with remaining failures on older device profiles — specifically bthornton (iPad) and lli (iPhone 12) — to forget the CorpWiFi SSID and re-enroll the corporate Wi-Fi profile/certificate via the MDM self-service portal, restoring connectivity for the residual legacy-device cases. Followed up with each user by email (bthornton@corplabs.com, lli@corplabs.com) to confirm resolution.
agent_questions: Hi Karen — thanks for reporting this. Can you confirm whether affected users like jmorales and bthornton are failing on all managed devices or only older profiles? Specifically, does the CorpWiFi join attempt on your MacBook (WORKSTATION-MBP-KW) show repeated disconnects after the 802.1X authentication prompt, or does it fail before association completes? Also, please check whether the same behavior occurs on your iPhone. I've opened a bridge with the network team and we're pulling RADIUS logs from ISE-PROD-02.corp.net now.

title: BitLocker protection off
description: I'm Rachel Nguyen (employee ID EMP-40921) on corporate laptop CORP-LTP-0234 (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN). The device was marked noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. BitLocker had not been enabled, protection status showed Off, and no recovery key was available in Azure AD/Intune escrow. observed_errors: TPM state: Ready but not initialized
root_cause: TPM was ready but not initialized, so a valid TPM-based BitLocker protector was not created and encryption never started or escrowed a recovery key.
resolution_steps: Validated the endpoint encryption state on CORP-LTP-0234 (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN, user rnguyen, IP 10.42.18.97) and confirmed BitLocker protection was Off via manage-bde -status C:, TPM was reported as Ready but not initialized via Get-Tpm, and no recovery key was present in Azure AD/Intune escrow for the device.

Initialized the device TPM on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN using Initialize-Tpm and enabled a TPM-based BitLocker protector via Add-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector so the endpoint could support managed disk encryption per the Corp-Endpoint-Encryption-Win10 policy.

Started BitLocker encryption on the C: system drive using Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -EncryptionMethod XtsAes256 -UsedSpaceOnly and verified the protection state changed to On via manage-bde -status C: on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN.

Escrowed the newly generated 48-digit recovery key to Azure AD/Intune using BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector and confirmed the key was visible under Azure AD > Devices > CORP-LTP-0234 > BitLocker keys for support recovery operations. Key escrow timestamp: 2026-01-28T21:12Z.

Forced an Intune device sync on CORP-LTP-0234 via the Intune admin console and rechecked Device Compliance Service until the encryption compliance state for user rnguyen (EMP-40921) returned to compliant. Final compliance status confirmed at 2026-01-28T21:18Z. Notified Rachel Nguyen at rng-sales@corplabs.com that the device is now fully compliant.

root_cause: The server certificate used by the Wireless Controller for Corporate Wi-Fi 802.1X authentication had expired, causing EAP handshakes to fail against the Network Access Control system and preventing successful authorization and DHCP assignment.
resolution_steps: Renew and install a valid server certificate (CN=wlc-corp.corplabs.internal) on the Wireless Controller WLC-CHARLOTTE-01 for the Corporate Wi-Fi (CorpNet-5G) 802.1X EAP-TLS service, using the CorpLabs Internal CA. Certificate renewal performed by Raj Menon (rmenon).

Restart the controller 802.1X authentication service on WLC-CHARLOTTE-01 so the renewed certificate is actively presented during new EAP-TLS handshakes; confirm the new certificate serial and expiry date (2027-05-04) in the controller certificate store.

Update and verify certificate trust chain and 802.1X authorization policy bindings on the Network Access Control system (Cisco ISE) so the renewed WLC server certificate is accepted correctly. Lisa Hwang (lhwang) confirmed ISE trust store updated and policy bindings validated.

Validate successful 802.1X authentication from test devices on the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-5G) across the affected environment in Charlotte Building A (floors 2–5) and confirm clients receive normal network access with valid DHCP leases. Test performed from Maria Castillo's device (WORKSTATION-MC-7240, IP 10.22.14.87) and Dev Patel's MacBook (WORKSTATION-MBP-DP, IP 10.22.14.93).

Have affected users reconnect to the CorpNet-5G SSID; where failures persist, remove stale or corrupt wireless profiles and re-enroll the device wireless configuration via the corporate MDM portal. Karen Liu (kliu) coordinated reconnection with remaining affected Sales and Engineering users.

title: Internal hostnames intermittently fail DNS resolution
description: Internal developers on the DevOps team (reported by Priya Nambiar, emp ID DVP-40821) were trying to reach service.internal.corp for application access and deployment activity from the Arlington office, but since early morning the hostname intermittently returned NXDOMAIN from some sites and an old IP address (10.42.16.55) from others. The issue affected internal-service-api connectivity and the deployment-pipeline because clients on subnet 10.42.0.0/16 could not reliably resolve the internal endpoint by name across the us-east-1 internal network. Priya's workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN (IP 10.42.3.117) consistently received NXDOMAIN, while colleagues in the Raleigh office intermittently got the stale address.
observed_errors: stale A record served by resolver
root_cause: An outdated A record for service.internal.corp remained in the internal DNS zone while the internal resolver cache still served the previous IP, causing clients to receive mixed answers including NXDOMAIN and stale resolution results.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone entry for service.internal.corp and corrected the A record from the stale address 10.42.16.55 to the current production IP address 10.42.18.90, performed by ktran via the Internal DNS Zone management console.

Checked the resolver path serving the internal zone and identified that dns-resolver-1 still had the previous address 10.42.16.55 cached for service.internal.corp with ~1,400 seconds of TTL remaining.

Flushed the stale cache entry on dns-resolver-1 so subsequent queries would return the updated zone data (10.42.18.90) instead of the old IP 10.42.16.55. Confirmed cache clear via rndc flushname service.internal.corp.

Validated name resolution for service.internal.corp from multiple client subnets — Arlington (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN at 10.42.3.117, user pnambiar) and Raleigh (10.44.1.22, user mreeves) — and confirmed consistent responses with the correct address 10.42.18.90 and no further NXDOMAIN results.

Scheduled and documented the internal DNS policy update to replace the deprecated zone policy reference with the current version (v2.4) to reduce recurrence risk. Change request CR-20260111-0087 filed by ktran and assigned to network_team lead Sandra Cho (scho) for review.

title: MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple users in the EMEA Sales team based out of the Frankfurt office were trying to access Office 365, Salesforce, and Confluence through the SSO Portal using Okta and Azure AD. After completing MFA via Okta Verify, they were returned to repeated MFA prompts or received 401/403 access failures. The issue was first reported by Claudia Reinhardt (creinhardt, EMP-40821) around 21:45 UTC on 2026-04-09, and subsequently confirmed by at least four other Sales users including Marco Bellini (mbellini) and Priya Nair (pnair). The issue began after a recent identity group restructure that moved the EMEA Sales team into a new organizational unit, blocked access to SaaS applications, and affected several users rather than a single device or enrollment.
observed_errors: Access denied by conditional access policy
root_cause: Azure AD Conditional Access policy scope did not include the updated Sales user group after the group change, causing repeated MFA challenges and access denials even when user MFA enrollment was valid.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Azure AD Conditional Access policy 'CA-SaaS-MFA-Enforce' assignments and identified that the updated Sales group 'SG-EMEA-Sales-2026' was excluded or not included in the intended policy scope. The old group 'SG-EMEA-Sales' had been emptied during the restructure but was still the only group referenced in the policy. Review performed by Dominik Kowalski (dkowalski) from the Identity Support team.

Updated the Conditional Access policy 'CA-SaaS-MFA-Enforce' to include the correct user group 'SG-EMEA-Sales-2026' and re-published the policy configuration. Change was applied at 22:25 UTC and confirmed active via Azure AD audit log.

Validated that affected users (creinhardt, mbellini, pnair, therrera, and others) had the expected group membership in 'SG-EMEA-Sales-2026' after the recent restructure and confirmed membership synchronization from Okta to Azure AD was complete with no delta sync errors.

Retested SSO sign-in to Office 365, Salesforce, and Confluence for previously impacted users. Claudia Reinhardt (creinhardt) confirmed successful login from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-CR at 22:32 UTC, and Marco Bellini (mbellini) and Priya Nair (pnair) verified MFA completed once without looping across all three applications.

Documented that MFA re-enrollment could temporarily help an individual user (as observed with mbellini during diagnostics) but was not the systemic fix for the broader access issue. Added a note to the identity team runbook to verify Conditional Access policy group references whenever organizational group restructures are performed. Ticket closed by Dominik Kowalski (dkowalski, EMP-51204).
agent_questions: Hi Claudia — please confirm whether the MFA loop happens across multiple SaaS apps (Office 365, Salesforce, Confluence) and whether this started after the recent Sales group membership change in Azure AD. Also, can you let me know if other users on your team such as Marco Bellini or Priya Nair are experiencing the same behavior? title: Internal host failing to resolve
description: Engineering users in the Arlington office were trying to reach internal-app.company.local on the internal network, but between 09:12 and 09:40 EST the hostname intermittently failed to resolve and client systems received NXDOMAIN responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) via the #dns-ops Slack channel and affected access to the internal application by name through the BIND 9 cache cluster (cache-east-01.infra.company.local / cache-east-02.infra.company.local) in the us-east-1 primary datacenter. Investigation tied the failures to an outdated internal DNS A record pointing to the decommissioned IP 10.22.4.17 instead of the current 10.22.8.55, and delayed remediation because the runbook referenced a deprecated DNS change-control policy (POL-DNS-2019, superseded by POL-DNS-2025).
platform: internal network DNS infrastructure (BIND 9 cache cluster)
observed_errors: Resolver returned NXDOMAIN from caching resolver (cache-hit)
root_cause: An outdated A record for internal-app.company.local remained in the authoritative internal DNS zone, and a deprecated change-control policy reference in the runbook slowed validation and correction of the DNS change.
resolution_steps: Correct the authoritative A record for internal-app.company.local in the internal DNS zone on ns-auth-01.infra.company.local from the stale address 10.22.4.17 to the current service IP address 10.22.8.55 (change performed by Priya Nair, pnair).

Increment the zone serial from 2025120901 to 2026010701 and reload the updated zone on the authoritative DNS server ns-auth-01.infra.company.local via `rndc reload company.local` so secondaries (ns-auth-02.infra.company.local) can receive the change via AXFR.

Confirm the corrected record has propagated to secondary DNS servers serving the internal zone by querying ns-auth-02.infra.company.local and verifying the serial matches 2026010701 and the A record returns 10.22.8.55.

Flush cached DNS entries on the primary and secondary resolvers (cache-east-01.infra.company.local and cache-east-02.infra.company.local) using `rndc flush` and restart the named caching service on the primary resolver cache-east-01 to clear stale NXDOMAIN responses.

Validate successful resolution for internal-app.company.local from Network Monitoring probes and from affected client subnets (10.22.50.0/24, 10.22.51.0/24, 10.22.52.0/24), confirming the hostname now returns the expected address 10.22.8.55. Confirmed with mdelgado and jtorres that their workstations resolve correctly.

Update the DNS runbook to replace the deprecated policy reference POL-DNS-2019 with the current POL-DNS-2025 so future DNS record corrections follow the current change process without delay. Runbook update assigned to Priya Nair (pnair) with review by team lead David Chen (dchen).
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — can you confirm the exact hostname and the failure window so we can correlate NXDOMAIN responses with resolver logs on cache-east-01.infra.company.local and cache-east-02.infra.company.local and cross-reference the internal zone data on ns-auth-01.infra.company.local? Also, could you share the client IP or hostname where you first saw the failure? — Priya Nair, Network Engineering

title: Device marked noncompliant

Company Portal manual sync did not update compliance, and the BitLocker encryption status was missing from device inventory, preventing normal access to Microsoft 365 resources needed for remote work. Please reach me at marcus.delgado@corplabs.com or ext 4-7183 if you need remote access to the machine.
observed_errors: Conditional Access blocked access to SharePoint
Missing encryption status (BitLocker) in device inventory
root_cause: The device fell out of compliance because Intune had a stale check-in state and was not receiving the required BitLocker encryption compliance signal. Conditional Access then enforced the noncompliant result and blocked SharePoint and Teams access until the device re-reported encryption and compliance state.
resolution_steps: Validated that WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (enrolled under mdelgado, EMP-40291) had not checked in to Intune for approximately 72 hours (last check-in 2025-12-24T22:48:00Z) and confirmed the missing BitLocker encryption attribute was the compliance signal causing the Noncompliant state.
Triggered a remote device sync from the Intune admin console targeting WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and had Marcus Delgado retry local sync from Company Portal to force a fresh compliance evaluation.
Reapplied the assigned encryption/compliance policy (ENG-RemoteWorkers-Compliance-v3) so the endpoint WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD could submit the required BitLocker status back to Intune device inventory.

Used re-enrollment as the remediation path for devices that still failed to report encryption after sync. Priya Nair guided mdelgado through the re-enrollment steps, then verified WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD resumed normal management check-in from IP 10.42.88.117.

Confirmed the device compliance state for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD returned to Compliant and removed the temporary Conditional Access exemption for mdelgado after SharePoint and Teams access was restored. Marcus Delgado confirmed full access at 2025-12-28T01:45:00Z.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether Company Portal sync completes successfully on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and whether the device is showing any local BitLocker or encryption prompts after the SharePoint block. Also, can you verify that your account mdelgado is not locked out in Active Directory? I've asked our endpoint lead, Priya Nair (pnair), to review the Intune device record on our side in the meantime.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal service
description: Engineering users and internal application teams were trying to reach internal-service1 at service1.company.local from on-premises Linux hosts in the private us-east-1 data center (Ashburn facility). For roughly the last 3 hours, name resolution intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or timed out for 30-60 seconds even though the target host was reachable by IP at 10.42.18.61. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) and confirmed by several members of the platform engineering group. It affected internal-service1 and internal-frontend, blocked application connectivity by hostname, and coincided with resolver latency spikes and cache inconsistencies after a recent DNS zone update performed earlier that morning.
observed_errors: DNS lookup timeout from internal resolver
cached A record mismatch observed in resolver logs
root_cause: The internal DNS resolver served a stale cached A record for service1.company.local after a recent zone update, causing intermittent mismatches between resolver cache contents and the current internal zone data and resulting in NXDOMAIN responses and lookup timeouts until the cache was flushed.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the authoritative internal DNS zone for service1.company.local, corrected the A record to match the current endpoint address (10.42.18.61), and confirmed the zone data reflected the intended value. Raj Kapoor (rkapoor) performed the verification against the zone file on the authoritative server.
Flushed the internal DNS resolver cache on dns-resolver-east-01 to remove the stale cached entry (10.42.18.40) that was being returned instead of the updated zone record.

Retested name resolution from the affected resolver path and from application hosts including WORKSTATION-LNX-MD and WORKSTATION-LNX-PN to confirm service1.company.local consistently returned the current address without NXDOMAIN or timeout responses.

Validated recovery through monitoring and application connectivity checks to confirm resolver latency normalized and the service was reachable by name. Marcus Delgado and Priya Nair both confirmed their applications reconnected successfully.
Adjusted the DNS TTL from 86400s to 300s to reduce the likelihood and duration of stale-cache impact after future record changes.

Documented follow-up review of conditional forwarder behavior to ensure the resolver refreshes the internal zone correctly after updates. Follow-up ticket assigned to Raj Kapoor (rkapoor, EMP-30157) for completion by 2026-01-21.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing scheduled job failures
description: The nightly customer synchronization job (job ID: SYNC-CUST-7041) managed by rchandra was failing through the Integration Gateway in us-east-1. Requests from integration client host WORKSTATION-APPSVC-RC (10.42.18.97) to the API Service endpoint began returning 504 Gateway Timeout responses after earlier 401 token validation failures on service account svc_intsync_prod. The scheduled job failed twice within the hour between 05:00 and 06:00 UTC, blocking downstream data sync to the CRM application and delaying customer record updates for the Austin operations team until the integration client authentication issue and gateway retry behavior were corrected.
root_cause: Expired API token for the integration client caused repeated authentication failures, which increased retry activity and gateway latency until scheduled sync requests began returning 504 timeouts.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc_intsync_prod (client_id: intgw-cust-sync-0029) used by the integration client on WORKSTATION-APPSVC-RC and updated the credential in the Integration Gateway connection configuration vault, performed by Priya Nair (pnair, E-40821).

Forced a token refresh for svc_intsync_prod and revalidated authenticated requests from 10.42.18.97 to confirm the API Service was accepting calls on path /api/v2/customer-sync without further 401 errors.

Temporarily increased the gateway timeout on the affected integration path /api/v2/customer-sync from 30s to 90s on gw-east-node-04 to reduce immediate job failures while authentication was being restored for svc_intsync_prod.

Updated gateway retry and backoff settings on the integration client from 3 retries/5s fixed interval to 5 retries with exponential backoff (base 10s, max 120s) to prevent rapid retry storms from amplifying upstream latency during future auth-related failures.

Implemented an automated token rotation process for svc_intsync_prod with a 60-day renewal cycle and alerting at 7 days before expiry, and verified that subsequent scheduled sync requests (SYNC-CUST-7041 at 06:00 UTC) completed successfully through the gateway as confirmed by rchandra.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: Corporate Windows laptop ENG-LAP-237, assigned to Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40291) in the Portland engineering office, was recently reimaged and re-enrolled into Intune. After re-enrollment, manage-bde showed BitLocker Protection Off on the OS drive (C:) and the device was marked noncompliant for disk encryption in the Device Compliance Service. No BitLocker recovery key was visible in Intune or the Device Compliance Service for this device, preventing compliance validation and leaving the endpoint without managed recovery escrow. User reported the issue via email at m.delgado@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: No recovery key found in Intune for device
root_cause: After the device reimage, the TPM protector was not initialized on the OS volume. This prevented BitLocker from starting successfully and blocked recovery key escrow to Intune even though the encryption policy assignment was present.
resolution_steps: Validated the device state on ENG-LAP-237 (hostname WORKSTATION-ENGDEL-04, IP 10.42.18.77, assigned to Marcus Delgado / mdelgado) by confirming manage-bde -status C: reported Protection Off with no key protectors and that no recovery key was present in Intune for the enrolled device.

Initialized the TPM protector state on ENG-LAP-237 using Initialize-Tpm and manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm so the OS volume had a valid TPM-based BitLocker protector available after the reimage. Desktop support tech Javier Ortiz (jortiz, emp ID E-31784) performed the local remediation.

Enabled BitLocker encryption on C: using manage-bde -on C: and confirmed encryption began with the TPM protector attached to the operating system volume. Encryption progress verified via manage-bde -status showing 'Encryption in Progress'.

Forced an Intune device sync on ENG-LAP-237 (Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Sync) to refresh policy and trigger BitLocker recovery key escrow from the endpoint to the Intune management service.

Verified the recovery key became visible in Intune and the Device Compliance Service for ENG-LAP-237 under user mdelgado. Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen) from the endpoint security team confirmed the device encryption status changed to compliant and the key was accessible for support recovery scenarios.

Recommended updating the Portland office imaging workflow and task sequence to include Initialize-Tpm and TPM protector initialization checks before or during Intune enrollment to prevent repeat BitLocker escrow failures on reimaged devices. Escalated recommendation to imaging team lead Carlos Vega (cvega) at ext. 4127.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — thanks for the details. Please confirm whether TPM was cleared or reinitialized during the imaging process and whether BitLocker ever completed encryption after enrollment. I'm checking the protector state on ENG-LAP-237 versus the Intune encryption policy assignment for user mdelgado. I've also looped in Rachel Nguyen from the endpoint security team for visibility. Will update shortly.

title: Print jobs stuck on PS01
description: Multiple Finance users in the Charlotte office were trying to print to the HR network printer (\\PS01\HR-Printer-Queue) through Print Server PS01, but submitted jobs remained stuck in the shared HR-Printer-Queue and the printer appeared offline. Users including Rachel Dominguez (EMP-40218) and Kevin Ostrowski (EMP-40335) could not complete normal printing tasks because queued jobs never processed. Server-side review on PS01 (10.42.16.80) showed repeated driver load failures (Event ID 372 — 'Driver not found') and spooler errors, indicating the installed HP-Driver-v5.2 printer driver package on PS01 was corrupted rather than a user-specific printing issue.
observed_errors: Spooler service error entries during job submission
root_cause: Corrupt approved printer driver package on Print Server PS01 caused driver load failures for HR-Printer-Queue and prevented the spooler from processing queued print jobs.
resolution_steps: Verified the HR-Printer-Queue on Print Server PS01 (10.42.16.80) was holding 14 stuck jobs and associated the failures with repeated driver load errors (Event ID 372) in the print server logs. Issue reported by Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez, EMP-40218) and Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski, EMP-40335) from the Charlotte Finance team.

Removed the corrupt printer driver package (checksum d4e812bb) and reinstalled the approved HP-Driver-v5.2 package on PS01 for the affected HR printer queue. Remediation performed by Marcus Tan (mtan) from Workplace Services.
Cleared all 14 pending jobs from HR-Printer-Queue and removed stale queue mappings left by the failed driver state.
Restarted the Print Spooler service on PS01 and confirmed the service started cleanly without recurring driver load errors in the event log.

Submitted and validated successful test prints from two user workstations — WORKSTATION-PC-RD (rdominguez, 10.42.19.104) and WORKSTATION-PC-KO (kostrowski, 10.42.19.117) — to confirm normal queue processing and printer availability.

title: MFA prompt loop for SSO users
description: Multiple users in the Sales group at the Charlotte office were trying to access the SSO Portal and downstream SaaS applications including Salesforce, Confluence, and Slack. After signing in through Okta and completing MFA via Okta Verify, they were immediately returned to another MFA challenge and sometimes saw "Authentication rejected" (error AUTH_REJECTED), preventing normal access. The issue was first reported by Rachel Simmons (rsimmons@corplabs.com) around 08:15 ET and began after an overnight conditional access policy update pushed at 02:00 ET on 2026-04-04. At least six Sales team members were affected, with access failures observed across multiple applications from various workstations on the 10.40.12.0/24 subnet.
root_cause: Okta sign-on for affected Sales users was still mapped to deprecated policy MFA-Policy-v1 after the overnight policy change, while some users also had stale MFA enrollment state. This caused MFA enrollment or verification tokens to be rejected and resulted in a repeated MFA prompt loop with intermittent authentication rejection.
resolution_steps: Validated the issue with test Sales user rsimmons (IP 10.40.12.47, workstation WORKSTATION-PC-RS) and confirmed the SSO flow at https://sso.corplabs.com was referencing deprecated Okta policy MFA-Policy-v1 (pol_0a8f3xQ2) instead of the current MFA-Policy-v2 (pol_7b2gYw9R) for the Sales group.

Updated the Okta sign-on and policy mappings for the Sales group scope to replace all references to MFA-Policy-v1 (pol_0a8f3xQ2) with MFA-Policy-v2 (pol_7b2gYw9R). Change executed by kmarsh on the Identity Engineering team and verified in the Okta admin console.

Reset stale MFA enrollments for affected users including rsimmons and mdelgado so they could establish a fresh valid Okta Verify factor registration during the corrected sign-in flow. A total of six Sales users at the Charlotte office required enrollment resets.

Retested login with a test cohort from the Sales group (rsimmons, mdelgado, and four additional users) and confirmed successful single MFA completion and access to assigned SaaS applications (Salesforce, Confluence, Slack) without looping or AUTH_REJECTED errors.

Advised impacted users via email from Rachel Simmons (rsimmons@corplabs.com) and the Sales team channel to re-enroll MFA if prompted, and monitored post-change sign-in behavior in Okta system logs for 24 hours to confirm the MFA loop no longer occurred for any Sales group member.
agent_questions: Can you confirm whether affected users recently re-enrolled MFA, whether their authenticator apps show the correct clock settings, and provide one sample Sales username for testing? Specifically, could you check the Okta factor enrollment status for the user rsimmons and confirm whether she is seeing the loop on her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-RS (IP 10.40.12.47)? Also, please verify the Okta Verify app time sync on her device.

title: Cannot reconnect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple Sales users in the Frankfurt office were trying to reconnect managed laptops and mobile devices to the Corporate Wi-Fi (SSID-Corp) after the scheduled overnight certificate rotation on 2026-04-29. Affected devices — including those belonging to rgarcia (EMP-40218) and mkovacs (EMP-40335) — could join the SSID but then showed 802.1X authentication errors, repeated disconnects, or "No network access," blocking normal wireless access after the maintenance window. The issue was reported across at least six endpoints and was limited to the corporate wireless authentication path involving the Wireless Controller cluster (WLC-EMEA-01) and Cisco ISE. Initial reports were filed by Rachel Garcia (rgarcia@corplabs.com) and escalated by the Frankfurt network operations team.
observed_errors: No network access after joining SSID-Corp
root_cause: Expired or improperly propagated EAP-TLS server certificate and trust chain on the Wireless Controller and Cisco ISE after the scheduled certificate rotation, causing 802.1X authentication failures and intermittent post-association network denial for Corporate Wi-Fi clients.
resolution_steps: Renewed the wireless EAP-TLS server certificate (CN=wifi-auth.corplabs.internal) and reinstalled it on the Wireless Controller cluster WLC-EMEA-01 with the correct certificate chain, verified by Dmitri Petrov (dpetrov).

Updated the Cisco ISE trust anchor to trust the renewed wireless certificate path and verified certificate validity across the authentication workflow. Anita Sharma (asharma) confirmed the updated trust store on the ISE policy node.

Validated 802.1X authentication from affected Corporate Wi-Fi clients — including LAPTOP-RGARCIA-7F (rgarcia, IP 10.42.18.97) and IPHONE-MKOVACS-3A (mkovacs) — and confirmed successful policy application and network access without relying on the temporary NAC exception "EMEA-Sales-TempBypass."

Removed the temporary NAC exception "EMEA-Sales-TempBypass" after certificate propagation completed and authentication stabilized for the affected Sales user group in Frankfurt. Removal confirmed by dpetrov at 2026-04-30T01:45Z.

Instructed affected users (Rachel Garcia, Marton Kovacs, and four other Sales team members) to forget and re-add the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID-Corp and re-enroll device certificates where needed so endpoints would trust and use the updated certificate chain. Follow-up confirmation received from rgarcia@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — before we replace certificates, please confirm whether the device (hostname LAPTOP-RGARCIA-7F) connects to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID-Corp and then drops to no network access, or if authentication fails immediately with the 802.1X EAP-TLS error message. Also, can you confirm whether Marton Kovacs and the other affected Sales users in Frankfurt are seeing the same behavior on their devices? Please share the client IP if you have it.

title: Device compliance policy failure — missing encryption signal and stale check-in
description: Multiple remote Windows 10 21H2 users in the Portland office were blocked from corporate resources because Conditional Access evaluated their managed devices as noncompliant in Intune. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40291) after she was unable to access SharePoint and Teams from her laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC. Affected endpoints showed no encryption compliance signal and had not successfully checked in for more than 14 days, preventing normal access to services that require a compliant device. At least five users in the RemoteWorkers group were impacted, including Derek Holloway (dholloway@corplabs.com) and Priya Nair (pnair).
observed_errors: Access blocked by Conditional Access - device noncompliant
Intune reporting: compliance status stale (no check-in >14 days)
root_cause: Stale Intune device check-in older than 14 days prevented current compliance telemetry from reaching the Device Compliance Service, leaving the BitLocker encryption signal missing and causing Conditional Access to classify affected devices as noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Triggered immediate remote sync for impacted devices in Intune — including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (mchen), WORKSTATION-PC-DH (dholloway), and WORKSTATION-SURFACE-TB (tbeckett) — to refresh endpoint management check-in and force updated compliance telemetry submission. Agent Raj Patel (rpatel@corplabs.com) initiated the bulk sync action from the Intune admin console.

Initiated compliance reassessment for the affected device population (four devices across the Portland RemoteWorkers group) so Conditional Access could reevaluate device state after the new sync cycle completed. Reassessment was triggered via the Device Compliance Service at 2025-12-31T09:15:00Z.

Guided users — Maria Chen (503-555-0193), Derek Holloway, Priya Nair, and Tom Beckett — to confirm BitLocker was enabled on their Windows devices and to open Company Portal so the encryption state could be re-registered and reported back to Intune. All four users confirmed BitLocker active and Company Portal sync initiated.

Validated that device check-in timestamps advanced to 2025-12-31 and that the encryption compliance signal populated correctly (EncryptionStatus: Compliant) for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC, WORKSTATION-PC-DH, and WORKSTATION-SURFACE-TB before confirming access restoration for all affected users.

Adjusted reassessment timing to a 7-day compliance evaluation interval and placed short-term monitoring on devices that had previously stale check-ins so non-reporting endpoints can be escalated promptly if compliance telemetry stops updating again. Monitoring alerts configured by Raj Patel and assigned to the Portland endpoint management queue.
agent_questions: We are checking whether affected devices are failing due to stale Intune check-in or missing encryption reporting. Please confirm whether BitLocker is enabled and whether Company Portal shows the device as recently synced. I've pulled the Intune records for Maria Chen's device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.47.83.112) and Derek Holloway's device WORKSTATION-PC-DH (IP 10.47.84.56) as initial samples. Can you also verify with the affected users whether they have been connected to VPN or had network access during the past two weeks?

title: BitLocker recovery key not escrowed
description: I have a managed Windows 10 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MR, asset tag EP-4417) assigned to user Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com, employee ID EMP-90234) in the Portland office showing noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. BitLocker was confirmed enabled locally on the endpoint (C: drive, XTS-AES 256-bit), but the recovery key was not visible in Azure AD / Intune escrow, preventing the device from meeting encryption compliance requirements and blocking normal managed-device status. The device IP at time of report was 10.42.18.77.
observed_errors: Recovery key not found in Azure AD
root_cause: BitLocker recovery key escrow to Azure AD failed because the device had an MDM sync error with Intune, leaving encryption active locally but no recovery key available to the management service.
resolution_steps: Verified on the affected laptop LAPTOP-SALES-MR (user mreeves, IP 10.42.18.77) that BitLocker was enabled on C: with XTS-AES 256-bit encryption and that a valid TPM 2.0 protector existed before attempting remediation.

Triggered a manual device sync from the Intune admin center for LAPTOP-SALES-MR (Intune Device ID 6b3e91a4-c8f2-4d07-b5a1-3920ef18dc44) to re-establish policy and compliance communication with the endpoint, clearing the prior 0x80180014 sync error.
Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on LAPTOP-SALES-MR using 'Rotate BitLocker keys' action in Intune to force generation of a new escrow event to Azure AD.

Confirmed the new BitLocker recovery key (Key ID ending ...9F3A) successfully appeared in Azure AD / Intune under mreeves' device objects after the sync completed at approximately 2026-01-26T05:22:00Z.

Rechecked device compliance status in Intune for LAPTOP-SALES-MR and verified the endpoint returned to compliant for encryption policy 'Corp-Encryption-Win10-v3'. Notified Marcus Reeves and Tanya Okafor that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether BitLocker shows as enabled locally on LAPTOP-SALES-MR and whether you have recently connected the device to the corporate network so it can complete an Intune sync. Also, can you verify the device is signed in under your account mreeves@corplabs.com? If you're working from the Portland office, please try a wired connection to rule out VPN-related sync issues.

title: Outlook not syncing

Cleared the affected mobile sync partnership for rnguyen@corplabs.internal using Remove-MobileDevice in Exchange Online PowerShell, remediated device compliance in MDM for IPHONE-RNGUYEN, and re-enrolled the iPhone to restore a healthy mobile connection state.

Confirmed full folder synchronization completed on the desktop client WORKSTATION-RNGUYEN and monitored mailbox sync for rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com over the next 24 hours to verify stable operation on both desktop and mobile. Rachel Nguyen confirmed normal email flow restored on both devices.

Confirmed that the FinanceTools deployment became visible in Software Center on WORKSTATION-FIN-MK after entitlement and policy propagation completed at approximately 2026-03-29T08:10Z.

Retried the installation from Software Center on WORKSTATION-FIN-MK and verified that the application installed successfully without the entitlement block. Notified Miriam Kaplan and Diane Ostrowski of resolution via email.
